# Song of Songs

שיר השירים

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs)

שיח פיוטי בין נאהבים שנתפרש במסורת חז"ל כאלגוריה ליחסי עם ישראל עם אלוקיו.

Poetic conversations of two lovers, traditionally read as a metaphor for God and Israel.

Sections: Chapter-Verse

Location: Tanakh/Writings

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Miqra according to the Masorah (Segments: 117, License: CC-BY-SA)

Versions (En):
  - The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001 (Segments: 117, License: CC-BY)
  - The Koren Jerusalem Bible (Segments: 117, License: CC-BY-NC)
  - The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein (Segments: 117, License: CC-BY)


## Chapter 1

###### Song of Songs 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:1)


שִׁ֥יר הַשִּׁירִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִשְׁלֹמֹֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The song of songs which is Shlomo’s.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The song of songs, which is Shelomo’s.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The Song of Songs [(All of Scripture is holy; but the Song of Songs, holy of holies)], which is Solomon's. [(Throughout Shir Hashirim, "Solomon" (Shlomoh) is understood as "the King of Peace [shalem]," all of it being compounded of the fear of Heaven and the acceptance of the yoke of Heaven.)]


###### Song of Songs 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:2)


יִשָּׁקֵ֙נִי֙ מִנְּשִׁיק֣וֹת פִּ֔יהוּ כִּֽי־טוֹבִ֥ים דֹּדֶ֖יךָ מִיָּֽיִן׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for your love is dearer than wine.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Let Him kiss me [(the Congregation of Israel)] of the kisses of His mouth, for Your love is better than [feasts of] wine.


###### Song of Songs 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:3)


לְרֵ֙יחַ֙ שְׁמָנֶ֣יךָ טוֹבִ֔ים שֶׁ֖מֶן תּוּרַ֣ק שְׁמֶ֑ךָ עַל־כֵּ֖ן עֲלָמ֥וֹת אֲהֵבֽוּךָ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Like the fragrance of good oils, your name is like flowing oil; therefore young maidens love you.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thy ointments are fragrant; for thy flowing oil thou art renowned: therefore do the virgins love thee.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For fragrance Your oils are good. Oil poured forth [(its fragrance spreading abroad)] is Your name; therefore, the "virgins" [(the proselytes, e.g., Yithro, Rachav, etc.)] have loved You.


###### Song of Songs 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:4)


מׇשְׁכֵ֖נִי אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ נָּר֑וּצָה הֱבִיאַ֨נִי הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ חֲדָרָ֗יו נָגִ֤ילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה֙ בָּ֔ךְ נַזְכִּ֤ירָה דֹדֶ֙יךָ֙ מִיַּ֔יִן מֵישָׁרִ֖ים אֲהֵבֽוּךָ׃{פ}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Draw me, we will run after you; the king has brought me into his chambers, we will be glad and rejoice in you, we recall your love more than wine, they loved you sincerely.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Draw me, we will run after thee: the king has brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will praise thy love more than wine: sincerely they love thee.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[I have heard You say] "Draw Me [to you. And, accordingly,] after You shall we run [(to be Your bride)]. The King has brought me into His chambers, [and even today] we are glad and rejoice in You. [Even today, in "living widowhood," we mention Your [first] love more than [any feast of] wine. A "straight" [i.e., "unalloyed" love] have they loved You.


###### Song of Songs 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:5)


שְׁחוֹרָ֤ה אֲנִי֙ וְֽנָאוָ֔ה בְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם כְּאׇהֳלֵ֣י קֵדָ֔ר כִּירִיע֖וֹת שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I am black, but comely, daughters of Jerusalem; like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Shlomo.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I am black, but comely, O daughters of Yerushalayim, like the tents of Qedar, like the curtains of Shelomo.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I may be "black" [(outwardly)], but I am beautiful [(inwardly)], O daughters of Jerusalem — ([black)] like the tents of Kedar; [(beautiful)], like the curtains of Solomon.


###### Song of Songs 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:6)


אַל־תִּרְא֙וּנִי֙ שֶׁאֲנִ֣י שְׁחַרְחֹ֔רֶת שֶׁשְּׁזָפַ֖תְנִי הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ בְּנֵ֧י אִמִּ֣י נִֽחֲרוּ־בִ֗י שָׂמֻ֙נִי֙ נֹטֵרָ֣ה אֶת־הַכְּרָמִ֔ים כַּרְמִ֥י שֶׁלִּ֖י לֹ֥א נָטָֽרְתִּי׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Do not look upon me [with contempt] that I am so black, for the sun has tanned me; my mother’s sons were incensed against me, they made me keeper of the vineyards, [but] my own vineyard I did not watch.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Do not gaze upon me, because I am black, because the sun has scorched me: my mother’s children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but my own vineyard I have not kept.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not look at me [scornfully] because I am black; for the sun has scorched me [and I can return to my former beauty]. The sons of my mother [(among whom I was reared and who ascended with me from Egypt as the "mixed multitude”)] have taunted me [(with their idolatries)], making me a keeper of their vineyards [i.e., gods]; my own vineyards I did not keep.


###### Song of Songs 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:7)


הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י שֶׁ֤אָֽהֲבָה֙ נַפְשִׁ֔י אֵיכָ֣ה תִרְעֶ֔ה אֵיכָ֖ה תַּרְבִּ֣יץ בַּֽצׇּהֳרָ֑יִם שַׁלָּמָ֤ה אֶֽהְיֶה֙ כְּעֹ֣טְיָ֔ה עַ֖ל עֶדְרֵ֥י חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where do you graze your flock where do you rest your flock at noon; for why should I flit about around the flocks of your companions?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Tell me, O thou whom my soul loves, where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon: for why should I be like one who cloaks himself by the flocks of thy companions?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[(The Congregation of Israel says to G-d):] Tell me, [You] whom my soul loves, how will You graze [Your flock among these wolves, the nations of the exile]? How will You make [them] lie down in the afternoon [of the exile? (the afternoon being a particularly difficult time for sheep)]. For why shall I be enwrapped [to the lip like a mourner at the plight of my sheep] among the flocks of Your neighbors [i.e., among the hordes of the nations, who rely on other gods]?


###### Song of Songs 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:8)


אִם־לֹ֤א תֵֽדְעִי֙ לָ֔ךְ הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים צְֽאִי־לָ֞ךְ בְּעִקְבֵ֣י הַצֹּ֗אן וּרְעִי֙ אֶת־גְּדִיֹּתַ֔יִךְ עַ֖ל מִשְׁכְּנ֥וֹת הָרֹעִֽים׃{פ}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
If you do not know [you who are the] fairest of women; go forth in the footsteps of the sheep and pasture your kids near the dwellings of the shepherds.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids besides the shepherds’ tents.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[G-d responds:] If you do not know [where to graze your sheep (in the absence of My immanence in exile)], you fairest among the women, go forth in the footsteps of the flock [i.e., retrace the steps of your forefathers, return to the Law] and [in reward] you will graze your kids by the shepherds' dwellings [i.e., among the dignitaries of the nations.]


###### Song of Songs 1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:9)


לְסֻֽסָתִי֙ בְּרִכְבֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה דִּמִּיתִ֖יךְ רַעְיָתִֽי׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
To steeds in the chariots of Pharaoh I have likened you, my beloved.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I compare thee, O my love, to a mare of the chariots of Par῾o.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
With My "squadrons" against the chariots of Pharaoh [(at the Red Sea)] did I silence you [i.e., your cries], My love.


###### Song of Songs 1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:10)


נָאו֤וּ לְחָיַ֙יִךְ֙ בַּתֹּרִ֔ים צַוָּארֵ֖ךְ בַּחֲרוּזִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Your cheeks are comely with rows of gems your neck with [pearl] necklaces.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thy cheeks would be comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with strings of beads.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Your cheeks are lovely with rows [of jewels (from the "spoils" of the Red Sea)]; your neck, with strings of gems.


###### Song of Songs 1:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:11)


תּוֹרֵ֤י זָהָב֙ נַֽעֲשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ עִ֖ם נְקֻדּ֥וֹת הַכָּֽסֶף׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Circlets of gold we will make for you with spangles of silver.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
We will make thee necklets of gold studded with silver.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[My tribunal and I devised that at the splitting of the Sea, by impelling Pharaoh to pursue Israel with all the glories of his treasure houses,] we would provide for you rows of gold along with the studs of silver [that you had already taken from Egypt (the spoils of the Sea being greater than the spoils of Egypt)].


###### Song of Songs 1:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:12)


עַד־שֶׁ֤הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בִּמְסִבּ֔וֹ נִרְדִּ֖י נָתַ֥ן רֵיחֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
While the king was at his table, my spikenard gave out its fragrance.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
While the king was reclining at his board, my nard sent forth its fragrance.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[The congregation of Israel responds: All that You say is so. You conferred good upon me and I reciprocated with evil. For] while the King was still at His banquet [(under the Torah "canopy" at Sinai)], my nard "gave forth" [(euphemism for "vitiated")] its fragrance [(in the sin of the golden calf)].


###### Song of Songs 1:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:13)


צְר֨וֹר הַמֹּ֤ר׀דּוֹדִי֙ לִ֔י בֵּ֥ין שָׁדַ֖י יָלִֽין׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, between my breasts he shall lie.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
My wellbeloved is to me a bundle of myrrh that lies between my breasts.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[(But, instead of destroying me,)] my Beloved was like a bundle of nard to me [i.e., as if there were a bundle of nard in His "bosom," and He said to me, as it were: Take this bundle. It will give forth even a finer fragrance than the one you "lost." (the analogy:) G-d effects reconciliation between Himself and Israel by finding atonement for the sin of the golden calf in their donations for the sanctuary. "Let the gold of the sanctuary come and atone for the gold of the calf." He assured me that] between my breasts [(the two jutting poles of the ark)] He would lie [i.e., repose His Shechinah.]


###### Song of Songs 1:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:14)


אֶשְׁכֹּ֨ל הַכֹּ֤פֶר׀דּוֹדִי֙ לִ֔י בְּכַרְמֵ֖י עֵ֥ין גֶּֽדִי׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
A cluster of henna is my beloved to me in the vineyards of En-gedi.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
My beloved is to me a cluster of henna in the vineyards of ῾En-gedi.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A cluster of henna [(kofer - an allusion to all of the kapparoth (atonements) granted the children of Israel by the L-rd for their many trials of Him in the desert)] is my Beloved to me in the vineyards of Ein Geddi [(which give forth fruit four or five times a year)].


###### Song of Songs 1:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:15)


הִנָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י הִנָּ֥ךְ יָפָ֖ה עֵינַ֥יִךְ יוֹנִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Behold you are beautiful, my beloved, behold you are beautiful; your eyes are like doves.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves’ eyes.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[I was confounded by my shameful acts, but He strengthened me, and forgave me, saying:] Behold, you are fair, My love [viz. Numbers 14:20]; behold, you are fair; your eyes are doves.


###### Song of Songs 1:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:16)


הִנְּךָ֨ יָפֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ אַ֣ף נָעִ֔ים אַף־עַרְשֵׂ֖נוּ רַעֲנָנָֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
You are handsome, my beloved, most handsome; indeed our bed is fresh.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our couch is green.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[Israel responds:] Behold, You are fair my Beloved, exceedingly fair, [(for having forgiven my offenses and having reposed Your Shechinah within me, viz. Leviticus 9:24)]; our "couch," [the sanctuary] too, is fruitful.


###### Song of Songs 1:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/1:17)


קֹר֤וֹת בָּתֵּ֙ינוּ֙ אֲרָזִ֔ים (רחיטנו) [רַהִיטֵ֖נוּ] בְּרוֹתִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The beams of our houses are cedars, our panels are cypresses.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters are of cypress.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The beams of our house [(the sanctuary)] are cedars; our rafters are cypress.



## Chapter 2

###### Song of Songs 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/2:1)


אֲנִי֙ חֲבַצֶּ֣לֶת הַשָּׁר֔וֹן שׁוֹשַׁנַּ֖ת הָעֲמָקִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I am a rose of Sharon a rose of the valleys.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I am the tulip of the Sharon; the daffodil of the vallies.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[The congregation of Israel:] I am the rose of Sharon, the lily of the valleys [(even more beautiful than the rose of Sharon)].


###### Song of Songs 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/2:2)


כְּשֽׁוֹשַׁנָּה֙ בֵּ֣ין הַחוֹחִ֔ים כֵּ֥ן רַעְיָתִ֖י בֵּ֥ין הַבָּנֽוֹת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
As a rose among the thorns, so is my beloved among the daughters.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Like the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
As a lily among the thorns [(which remains "upright" and beautiful though the thorns constantly prick it)], so is My loved one among the daughters [of the nations, resisting all their blandishments to idolatry].


###### Song of Songs 2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/2:3)


כְּתַפּ֙וּחַ֙ בַּעֲצֵ֣י הַיַּ֔עַר כֵּ֥ן דּוֹדִ֖י בֵּ֣ין הַבָּנִ֑ים בְּצִלּוֹ֙ חִמַּ֣דְתִּי וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי וּפִרְי֖וֹ מָת֥וֹק לְחִכִּֽי׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
As an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the sons; in its shade I delighted and sat, and its fruit was sweet to my palate.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Like the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
As a flourishing apple tree among the [desiccated] trees of the forest, so is my Beloved among the "sons" [i.e., the idolatries of the nations.] For His shade did I long and I sat (therein), and His fruit was sweet to my taste.


###### Song of Songs 2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/2:4)


הֱבִיאַ֙נִי֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַיָּ֔יִן וְדִגְל֥וֹ עָלַ֖י אַהֲבָֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He brought me to the banqueting-house, and his banner is raised over me in love.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He has brought me to the house of wine [(the tent of meeting, where the details and exegeses of Torah were given)], and His banner [(which is still suspended)] over me is love.


###### Song of Songs 2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Song%20of%20Songs/r/2:5)


סַמְּכ֙וּנִי֙ בָּאֲשִׁישׁ֔וֹת רַפְּד֖וּנִי בַּתַּפּוּחִ֑ים כִּי־חוֹלַ֥ת אַהֲבָ֖ה אָֽנִי׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Sustain me with dainty cakes refresh my bed with [the scent of] apples; for I am lovesick.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Let me lean against the stout trunks, let me couch among the apple trees: for I am sick with love.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

Psalms 2:12)].

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I have come to my garden, my sister, O bride, I have gathered my myrrh with my spice, I have eaten my sugar cane with my honey, I have drunk my wine with my milk; eat [my] friends, drink and become intoxicated, [my] beloved ones.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I am come into my garden, my sister, my bride: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O dear ones, and drink; drink deep, O loving companions.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I came to My garden [(in the days of the investiture of the sanctuary, My sister, [My] bride. I gathered My myrrh with My spice [(the incense offered by the princes of the tribes)]. I ate [i.e., consumed] My honeycomb with My wine [(in My "overflowing" love for them)]. I have drunk My wine [(the libations)] with [i.e., which are sweeter and purer than] milk. Eat, [your portions, My] friends, [(Aaron and his sons, in the tent of meeting)]; drink deep, [My] loved ones, [(Israel, who ate the flesh of the peace-offering at the investiture of the Sanctuary)].


###### Song of Songs 5:2

אֲנִ֥י יְשֵׁנָ֖ה וְלִבִּ֣י עֵ֑ר ק֣וֹל**׀** דּוֹדִ֣י דוֹפֵ֗ק פִּתְחִי־לִ֞י אֲחֹתִ֤י רַעְיָתִי֙ יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י שֶׁרֹּאשִׁי֙ נִמְלָא־טָ֔ל קְוֻצּוֹתַ֖י רְסִ֥יסֵי לָֽיְלָה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I slept but my heart was awake; a sound! My beloved knocks, open for me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfection, for my head is drenched [as though] with dew, my sidelocks drip with the rains of the night.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I sleep, but my heart wakes: hark, my beloved is knocking, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I [(the Congregation of Israel, in the period of the first Temple)] was asleep [i.e., negligent in the service of the L-rd], but my "Heart" was awake [(to guard me and to confer good upon me)]. The voice of my Beloved knocks. [(He reposes His Shechinah on the prophets and exhorts me through them constantly;)] Open to Me, [(Do not cause Me to depart from you)] My sister, My love, My dove, My innocent one. For my head is filled with [the] dew [of blessings and reward, if you return to Me] — but My locks with the drops of night [i.e., punishments, if you spurn Me].

## Chapter 6

###### Song of Songs 6:1

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Where has your beloved gone O fairest among women? Where has your beloved turned that we may seek him with you?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Where is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? where has thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[The nations taunt Israel:] Where did your Beloved go, you loveliest among the women" [Why has He left you widowed and forsaken?] [When He returned and reposed His spirit on Koresh (who permitted the rebuilding of the Temple), when they began to build, they came and said to them:] Whither has your Beloved turned? [If He is returning to you,] let us seek Him with you [(their intention being to subvert the building of the Temple, viz. Ezra 4:2)].

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[And Israel replies:] My Beloved has gone down to His garden [(He has commanded us to rebuild His sanctuary, and He will be there with us)], [He has gone down] to the beds of spices [(where the incense is burned.) And He has further gone down] to graze [His flock] in the "gardens" [of exile whither they are dispersed, to repose His Shechinah in the synagogues and the study halls] and to gather "lilies" [i.e., to savor their Torah converse, viz. Malachi 3:16. And, as to your wishing to seek Him with us],

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Turn your eyes away from me, for they made me haughty; your hair is like a flock of goats descending from Mount Gilad.

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Turn your eyes away from Me, for they emboldened Me [in the first Temple] to show you too much love, wherefore you were faithless to Me (so that in this Temple I cannot restore to you the ark, the kaporeth [the ark-lid], and the cherubs, which intensified this "emboldenment")]. Your hair [i.e., the "slightest" among you] (sparkles) like a flock of goats sliding down [Mount] Gilead.

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Your teeth are like a flock of ewe-lambs, rising from the washing, all perfect, no blemish among them.

Like a slice of pomegranate are your cheeks from within your kerchief.

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[But] one [i.e., unique] is My dove, My perfect one; one to her mother, clear [i.e., without blemish] to her begetter. Daughters [i.e., the nations] saw her [(Israel in her grandeur)]; queens and concubines [saw her], and they praised her.

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Who is this that gazes down like the [breaking] dawn, beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun, awesome as the hosts [of angels]?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Who is she that looks out like the dawn, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Who is this that is seen [(rising gradually in splendor)] like the morning star [(an allusion to Israel's ascent from subjugation to dominance during the second Temple period)], beautiful as the moon, clear as the sun, awesome among the legions?

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
To a nut-garden [(the second Temple)] did I go down, to see the flowering of the stream [i.e., what good deeds "flowed" within you] — Had the vine [i.e., Torah scholars, scribes, and teachers] blossomed? Had the pomegranates [i.e., doers of mitzvoth] bloomed?

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[Israel responds:] I did not know my soul [i.e., I could not keep from sinning]. It [(my soul)] made me the chariot of a patronizing people (Rome) [i.e., it made me tributary to them, to receive their doles.]

[The nations, to Israel:] Turn away, turn away [from G-d], O Shulamith [(you who are perfect [shalem] in faith with Him)]. Turn away, turn away [to us] and we will seek out [(high positions] for you. [Israel responds:] What can you seek out for Shulamith like [i.e., equal in grandeur to] the [flag] encirclement [of the desert]?

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The baskets emit fragrance, and at our door are all luscious fruits, both new and old; my beloved, I have kept them for you.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The baskets of figs [viz. Jeremiah 24:1-3 (one basket of good figs [the righteous]; the other, of bad figs [the sinners])] have given forth a fragrance [ — all are seeking You]. And at our doors are all manner of delicacies [i.e., reward for many mitzvoth], new [i.e., originated by the Scribes] and old [ordained by Scripture] alike. # Ruth

רות

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth)

אלמנה מואבייה נוהגת בחמותה במידת החסד ומצטרפת לעם ישראל בצאתה לדרך חדשה.

A Moabite widow remains loyal to her mother-in-law and to Israel, embarking on a new beginning.

Sections: Chapter-Verse

Location: Tanakh/Writings

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Versions (En):
  - The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001 (Segments: 85, License: CC-BY)
  - The Koren Jerusalem Bible (Segments: 85, License: CC-BY-NC)
  - The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein (Segments: 85, License: CC-BY)


## Chapter 1

###### Ruth 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/1:1)


וַיְהִ֗י בִּימֵי֙ שְׁפֹ֣ט הַשֹּׁפְטִ֔ים וַיְהִ֥י רָעָ֖ב בָּאָ֑רֶץ וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ אִ֜ישׁ מִבֵּ֧ית לֶ֣חֶם יְהוּדָ֗ה לָגוּר֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב ה֥וּא וְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ וּשְׁנֵ֥י בָנָֽיו׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And it happened in the days when the Judges judged, that there was a famine in the land, and a man of Bethlehem in Judah went to sojourn in the fields of Moab; he with his wife and two sons.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled, that there was a famine in the land. And a certain man of Bet-leĥem in Yehuda went to sojourn in the country of Mo᾽av, he, and his wife, and his two sons.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And it was, in the days of the rule of the judges [i.e., before the reign of King Saul, when the people were led by judges, the judge at that particular time being Ivtzan [(Boaz, viz. Judges 12:8)], that there was a hunger in the land. And there went a man from Bethlehem in Judah to dwell in the fields of Moav, he, his wife, and his two sons.


###### Ruth 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/1:2)

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Ruth 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/1:3)

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**

She carried it and went into the city. Her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned, and she took it out [to show her] and she gave her what she had left over after eating her fill.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And she took it up, and went into the city: and her mother in law saw what she had gleaned: and she brought it out, and gave to her what she had left over after she had eaten her fill.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And she took (it) up and went into the city. And her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. And she brought (it) out and gave her what she had left over after having sated herself.

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

לִ֣ינִי**׀** הַלַּ֗יְלָה וְהָיָ֤ה בַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ אִם־יִגְאָלֵ֥ךְ טוֹב֙ יִגְאָ֔ל וְאִם־לֹ֨א יַחְפֹּ֧ץ לְגׇאֳלֵ֛ךְ וּגְאַלְתִּ֥יךְ אָנֹ֖כִי חַי־יְהֹוָ֑ה שִׁכְבִ֖י עַד־הַבֹּֽקֶר׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Stay the night; and in the morning—if he will redeem you—well and good, let him redeem you, but if he does not wish to redeem you, then I will redeem you, as Adonoy lives—lie here until the morning.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Tarry this night, and it shall be in the morning, that if he will perform to thee the part of a kinsman, well; let him do the kinsman’s part: but if he will not do the part of a kinsman to thee, then will I do the part of a kinsman to thee, as the Lord lives: lie down until the morning.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Lie [(without a husband)] this night, and, it shall be in the morning, if he redeems you, good; and if he does not wish to redeem you, then I shall redeem you — I swear by the L-rd! Lie [here] until the morning.


###### Ruth 3:14

וַתִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מַרְגְּלוֹתָו֙ עַד־הַבֹּ֔קֶר וַתָּ֕קׇם (בטרום) [בְּטֶ֛רֶם] יַכִּ֥יר אִ֖ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַל־יִוָּדַ֔ע כִּי־בָ֥אָה הָאִשָּׁ֖ה הַגֹּֽרֶן׃

###### Ruth 4:4

וַאֲנִ֨י אָמַ֜רְתִּי אֶגְלֶ֧ה אׇזְנְךָ֣ לֵאמֹ֗ר קְ֠נֵ֠ה נֶ֥גֶד הַיֹּשְׁבִים֮ וְנֶ֣גֶד זִקְנֵ֣י עַמִּי֒ אִם־תִּגְאַל֙ גְּאָ֔ל וְאִם־לֹ֨א יִגְאַ֜ל הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י (ואדע) [וְאֵֽדְעָה֙] כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין זוּלָֽתְךָ֙ לִגְא֔וֹל וְאָנֹכִ֖י אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָנֹכִ֥י אֶגְאָֽל׃

And I decided to tell you about it, in these words—Buy it in the presence of those sitting here, and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you desire to redeem it, redeem it, and if it will not be redeemed, tell me, that I may know [now], for beside you there is no one to redeem it, and I am [next in line] after you.” And he said, “I will redeem it.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and I thought to advise thee of it, saying, Buy it in the presence of the inhabitants, and in the presence of the elders of my people. If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it: but if thou wilt not redeem it, then tell me, that I may know: for there is none to redeem it besides thee; and I am after thee. And he said, I will redeem it.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I said that I would tell you (of it), saying: Acquire (it) in the presence of the inhabitants and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you will redeem, redeem; and if he [i.e., you] will not redeem, tell me and I shall know. For there is no [close kin] other than you to redeem, and I, after you. And he said: I shall redeem.

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר בֹּ֔עַז בְּיוֹם־קְנוֹתְךָ֥ הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה מִיַּ֣ד נׇעֳמִ֑י וּ֠מֵאֵ֠ת ר֣וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֤ה אֵֽשֶׁת־הַמֵּת֙ (קניתי) [קָנִ֔יתָ] לְהָקִ֥ים שֵׁם־הַמֵּ֖ת עַל־נַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I harm my own inheritance: take my right of redemption for thyself; for I cannot redeem it.

And the redeemer said: I cannot redeem it unto me lest I destroy [i.e., blemish] my seed [(Ploni Almoni mistakenly assuming that "An Ammonite and a Moavite shall not come into the congregation of the L-rd" [Deuteronomy 23:4] applies to a Moavitess as well)]. You redeem my inheritance, for I cannot redeem it.

וְזֹאת֩ לְפָנִ֨ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל עַל־הַגְּאֻלָּ֤ה וְעַל־הַתְּמוּרָה֙ לְקַיֵּ֣ם כׇּל־דָּבָ֔ר שָׁלַ֥ף אִ֛ישׁ נַעֲל֖וֹ וְנָתַ֣ן לְרֵעֵ֑הוּ וְזֹ֥את הַתְּעוּדָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And this was the custom of yore in Israel for redemption [(sale)] and for exchange [(substitution [chalifin])] to establish every thing: a man [(as a sign of acquisition)] would remove his shoe and give it to his neighbor. And this [became] the [manner of] attestation in Israel.

###### Ruth 4:11

And all the people said who were at the gate, and the elders [also] said: “We are witnesses! May Adonoy make this woman, who is coming into your home, like Rachel and like Leah, who together built the House of Israel. May you perform deeds of valor in Ephrath, and be famous in Bethlehem.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders, said, We are witnesses. The Lord make the woman that is come into thy house like Raĥel and like Le᾽a, which two did build the house of Yisra᾽el; and be prosperous in Efrata, and be famous in Bet-leĥem:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And all the people in the gate and the elders said: [We are] witnesses. May the L-rd make the woman who is coming to your house as Rachel and as Leah, the two of whom built the house of Israel; and be prosperous in Efrata, and be renowned in Bethlehem.


###### Ruth 4:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:12)


וִיהִ֤י בֵֽיתְךָ֙ כְּבֵ֣ית פֶּ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָ֥ה תָמָ֖ר לִיהוּדָ֑ה מִן־הַזֶּ֗רַע אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֤ן יְהֹוָה֙ לְךָ֔ מִן־הַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
May your house be like the house of Peretz, whom Tamar bore to Judah, through the offspring which Adonoy will give you from this young woman.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and let thy house be like the house of Pereż, whom Tamar bore to Yehuda, of the seed which the Lord shall give thee of this young woman.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And may your house be as that of Peretz [(from whom you descended)], whom Tamar begot of Judah, of the seed that the L-rd shall give you from this maiden.


###### Ruth 4:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:13)


וַיִּקַּ֨ח בֹּ֤עַז אֶת־רוּת֙ וַתְּהִי־ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א אֵלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהֹוָ֥ה לָ֛הּ הֵרָי֖וֹן וַתֵּ֥לֶד בֵּֽן׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
So Boaz took Rus and she became his wife; and he came to her. And Adonoy made her conceive and she gave birth to a son.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
So Bo῾az took Rut, and she was his wife: and he went in to her, and the Lord gave her conception, and she bore a son.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Boaz took Ruth, and she was a wife to him, and he lived with her, and the L-rd granted her conception, and she bore a son.


###### Ruth 4:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:14)


וַתֹּאמַ֤רְנָה הַנָּשִׁים֙ אֶֽל־נׇעֳמִ֔י בָּר֣וּךְ יְהֹוָ֔ה אֲ֠שֶׁ֠ר לֹ֣א הִשְׁבִּ֥ית לָ֛ךְ גֹּאֵ֖ל הַיּ֑וֹם וְיִקָּרֵ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And the women said to Naomi, “Blessed is Adonoy, Who has not withheld from you a redeeming kinsman [even] this day; and may his name be famous in Israel.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the women said to No῾omi, Blessed is the Lord, who has not left thee this day without a redeemer, that his name may be famous in Yisra᾽el.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the women said to Na'ami: Blessed is the L-rd, who did not leave you without a redeemer this day; and may his name be renowned in Israel.


###### Ruth 4:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:15)


וְהָ֤יָה לָךְ֙ לְמֵשִׁ֣יב נֶ֔פֶשׁ וּלְכַלְכֵּ֖ל אֶת־שֵׂיבָתֵ֑ךְ כִּ֣י כַלָּתֵ֤ךְ אֲֽשֶׁר־אֲהֵבַ֙תֶךְ֙ יְלָדַ֔תּוּ אֲשֶׁר־הִיא֙ ט֣וֹבָה לָ֔ךְ מִשִּׁבְעָ֖ה בָּנִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And he will be unto you a restorer of life, and a support in your old age, for your daughter-in-law who loves you has borne him, [and] she is better to you than seven sons.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he shall be to thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thy old age: for thy daughter in law, who loves thee, who is better to thee than seven sons, she has born him.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And may he be to you a restorer of life and a nourisher of old age; for your daughter-in-law, who loves you, has borne him — she, being better to you than seven sons.


###### Ruth 4:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:16)


וַתִּקַּ֨ח נׇעֳמִ֤י אֶת־הַיֶּ֙לֶד֙ וַתְּשִׁתֵ֣הוּ בְחֵיקָ֔הּ וַתְּהִי־ל֖וֹ לְאֹמֶֽנֶת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And Naomi took the child, and held it in her bosom, and she became his nurse.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And No῾omi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse to it.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Na'ami took the child and laid it on her bosom, and she was his nurse.


###### Ruth 4:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:17)


וַתִּקְרֶ֩אנָה֩ ל֨וֹ הַשְּׁכֵנ֥וֹת שֵׁם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יֻלַּד־בֵּ֖ן לְנׇעֳמִ֑י וַתִּקְרֶ֤אנָֽה שְׁמוֹ֙ עוֹבֵ֔ד ה֥וּא אֲבִֽי־יִשַׁ֖י אֲבִ֥י דָוִֽד׃{פ}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The [woman] neighbors gave him a name, saying, “A son has been born to Naomi,” and they called his name, Oved; he was the father of Yishai [who was] the father of Dovid.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to No῾omi; and they called his name ῾Oved: he is the father of Yishay, the father of David.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the neighbor women gave him a name, saying: A son was born to Na'ami. And they named him "Oved"; he was the father of Yishai, who was the father of David.


###### Ruth 4:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:18)


וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ תּוֹלְד֣וֹת פָּ֔רֶץ פֶּ֖רֶץ הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־חֶצְרֽוֹן׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
These are the generations of Peretz: Perets begot Hetzron;


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Now these are the generations of Pereż: Pereż begot Ḥeżron,


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[(Having traced David to Ruth, he now traces him to Judah.)] And these are the generations of Peretz [(the son of Judah)]: Peretz begot Chetzron,


###### Ruth 4:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:19)


וְחֶצְרוֹן֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־רָ֔ם וְרָ֖ם הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־עַמִּינָדָֽב׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
and Hetzron begot Ram, and Ram begot Aminadav;


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and Ḥeżron begot Ram, and Ram begot ῾Amminadav,


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Chetzron begot Ram, and Ram begot Aminadav,


###### Ruth 4:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:20)


וְעַמִּֽינָדָב֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־נַחְשׁ֔וֹן וְנַחְשׁ֖וֹן הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־שַׂלְמָֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
and Aminadav begot Nachshon, and Nachshon begot Salmah;


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and ῾Amminadav begot Naĥshon, and Naĥshon begot Salma,


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Aminadav begot Nachshon, and Nachshon begot Salmah,


###### Ruth 4:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:21)


וְשַׂלְמוֹן֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־בֹּ֔עַז וּבֹ֖עַז הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־עוֹבֵֽד׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
and Salmon begot Boaz, and Boaz begot Oved;


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and Salmon begot Bo῾az, and Bo῾az begot ῾Oved,


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Salmah begot Boaz, and Boaz begot Oved,


###### Ruth 4:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ruth/r/4:22)


וְעֹבֵד֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־יִשָׁ֔י וְיִשַׁ֖י הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־דָּוִֽד׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
and Oved begot Yishai; and Yishai begot Dovid.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and ῾Oved begot Yishay, and Yishay begot David.

And Oved begot Yishai, and Yishai begot David.

# Lamentations

איכה

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations)

קינה על חורבן ירושלים והתמודדות עם נימוקים תאולוגיים לחורבן.

Laments of Jerusalem’s destruction, grappling with theological explanations.

Sections: Chapter-Verse

Location: Tanakh/Writings

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Miqra according to the Masorah (Segments: 154, License: CC-BY-SA)

Versions (En):
  - The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001 (Segments: 154, License: CC-BY)
  - The Koren Jerusalem Bible (Segments: 154, License: CC-BY-NC)
  - The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein (Segments: 154, License: CC-BY)


## Chapter 1

###### Lamentations 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:1)


אֵיכָ֣ה**׀** יָשְׁבָ֣ה בָדָ֗ד הָעִיר֙ רַבָּ֣תִי עָ֔ם הָיְתָ֖ה כְּאַלְמָנָ֑ה רַבָּ֣תִי בַגּוֹיִ֗ם שָׂרָ֙תִי֙ בַּמְּדִינ֔וֹת הָיְתָ֖ה לָמַֽס׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
How can it be that she sits in isolation the city teeming with people has become like a widow? Immense among nations, noble among provinces—she has become a payer of tribute.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
How does the city sit solitary, that was full of people! how is she become like a widow! she that was great among the nations, and princess among the provinces, how is she become a vassal!


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
How solitary does she sit, the city [formerly] rich in people. She has become like a widow. The great among the nations, the princess of the provinces, has become tributary.


###### Lamentations 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:2)


בָּכ֨וֹ תִבְכֶּ֜ה בַּלַּ֗יְלָה וְדִמְעָתָהּ֙ עַ֣ל לֶֽחֱיָ֔הּ אֵֽין־לָ֥הּ מְנַחֵ֖ם מִכׇּל־אֹהֲבֶ֑יהָ כׇּל־רֵעֶ֙יהָ֙ בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔הּ הָ֥יוּ לָ֖הּ לְאֹיְבִֽים׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
She weeps bitterly in the night, her tear on her cheek. No one consoles her, among all her lovers. All of her friends have betrayed her, they have become her enemies.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
She weeps sore in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks: among all her lovers she has none to comfort her: all her friends have dealt treacherously with her, they have become her enemies.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
She weeps, she weeps [(two "weepings" for two Temples)] at night [(the Temple having been destroyed at night)], and her tears are on her cheeks [(with constant weeping)]. She has no consolers of all her lovers. All her lovers have betrayed her; they have become foes to her.


###### Lamentations 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:3)


גָּֽלְתָ֨ה יְהוּדָ֤ה מֵעֹ֙נִי֙ וּמֵרֹ֣ב עֲבֹדָ֔ה הִ֚יא יָשְׁבָ֣ה בַגּוֹיִ֔ם לֹ֥א מָצְאָ֖ה מָנ֑וֹחַ כׇּל־רֹדְפֶ֥יהָ הִשִּׂיג֖וּהָ בֵּ֥ין הַמְּצָרִֽים׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Yehudah was exiled because of torment and excessive toil. [Even] when she dwelt among the nations, she found no rest. All her pursuers overtook her between the barriers.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Yehuda is gone into exile because of affliction, and because of great servitude: she dwells among the nations, she finds no rest: all her persecutors overtook her within the straits.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Judah has gone into exile from affliction and from much servitude [(of the Kasdim.)] She sat among the nations, (but) found no rest. All of her pursuers overtook her between the straits.


###### Lamentations 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:4)


דַּרְכֵ֨י צִיּ֜וֹן אֲבֵל֗וֹת מִבְּלִי֙ בָּאֵ֣י מוֹעֵ֔ד כׇּל־שְׁעָרֶ֙יהָ֙ שֽׁוֹמֵמִ֔ין כֹּהֲנֶ֖יהָ נֶאֱנָחִ֑ים בְּתוּלֹתֶ֥יהָ נּוּג֖וֹת וְהִ֥יא מַר־לָֽהּ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The roads of *Tzion* grieve, for lack of festival visitors. All her gateways are in ruins, her *Kohanim* groan, her maidens grieve; and she is embittered.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The ways of Żiyyon do mourn, because none come to the solemn assembly: all her gates are desolate: her priests sigh, her virgins are afflicted, and she is in bitterness.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The ways of Zion mourn, without the festival-pilgrims. All of her gates are desolate; her priests sigh; her virgins are afflicted; and she is bitter unto herself.


###### Lamentations 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:5)


הָי֨וּ צָרֶ֤יהָ לְרֹאשׁ֙ אֹיְבֶ֣יהָ שָׁל֔וּ כִּֽי־יְהֹוָ֥ה הוֹגָ֖הּ עַ֣ל רֹב־פְּשָׁעֶ֑יהָ עוֹלָלֶ֛יהָ הָלְכ֥וּ שְׁבִ֖י לִפְנֵי־צָֽר׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Her oppressors have become elevated, her enemies are at ease. For Adonoy has brought her grief for her excessive iniquity. Her young were taken captive before the oppressors.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Her adversaries have become the chief, her enemies prosper; for the Lord has afflicted her for the multitude of her transgressions: her infants are gone into captivity before the enemy.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Her adversaries have become the heads; her foes have prospered. For the L-rd has afflicted her for the multitude of her transgressions. Her young children are gone captive before the enemy.


###### Lamentations 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:6)


וַיֵּצֵ֥א (מן בת) [מִבַּת־]צִיּ֖וֹן כׇּל־הֲדָרָ֑הּ הָי֣וּ שָׂרֶ֗יהָ כְּאַיָּלִים֙ לֹא־מָצְא֣וּ מִרְעֶ֔ה וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ בְלֹא־כֹ֖חַ לִפְנֵ֥י רוֹדֵֽף׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Gone from the city of *Tzion,* is all her splendor her nobles have become like harts who could find no pasture, plodding powerlessly before the pursuer.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And from the daughter of Żiyyon all her splendour is departed: her princes are become like harts that find no pasture, and they are gone without strength before the pursuer.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And there went forth from the daughter of Zion all of her splendor. Her princes have become like harts not finding pasture, and they have gone without strength before the pursuer.


###### Lamentations 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:7)


זָֽכְרָ֣ה יְרוּשָׁלַ֗͏ִם יְמֵ֤י עׇנְיָהּ֙ וּמְרוּדֶ֔יהָ כֹּ֚ל מַחֲמֻדֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ מִ֣ימֵי קֶ֑דֶם בִּנְפֹ֧ל עַמָּ֣הּ בְּיַד־צָ֗ר וְאֵ֤ין עוֹזֵר֙ לָ֔הּ רָא֣וּהָ צָרִ֔ים שָׂחֲק֖וּ עַ֥ל מִשְׁבַּתֶּֽהָ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Yerusholayim, remembered the days of her [ruin] [which brought her] poverty and lamenting; [and] all her treasures she had in early times. When her people fell into the hands of the oppressors and no one came to her aid, her enemies watched her, laughing derisively when she was curbed (from celebrating her holidays).


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Yerushalayim remembers in the days of her affliction and of her miseries all her pleasant things that she had in the days of old, when her people fell into the hand of the enemy, and none did help her: the adversaries saw her, and gloated at her destruction.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Jerusalem [(i.e., the daughter of Zion in her exile)] remembered the days of [her destruction which led to] her affliction and her grieving. [She remembered] all of her precious things which she enjoyed in days of yore. When her people fell into the hand of the oppressor, with none to help her, oppressors beheld her and rejoiced at her cessations [(the cessations of her joyous festivals, New Moons, and Sabbaths)].


###### Lamentations 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:8)


חֵ֤טְא חָֽטְאָה֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלַ֔͏ִם עַל־כֵּ֖ן לְנִידָ֣ה הָיָ֑תָה כׇּֽל־מְכַבְּדֶ֤יהָ הִזִּיל֙וּהָ֙ כִּי־רָא֣וּ עֶרְוָתָ֔הּ גַּם־הִ֥יא נֶאֶנְחָ֖ה וַתָּ֥שׇׁב אָחֽוֹר׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Jerusalem has grievously sinned, and, therefore, has become a wanderer. All those who glorified her scorn her, for they have seen her degradation. She, too, is sorrowful, and has turned backward, (humiliated and ashamed).


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Yerushalayim has grievously sinned; therefore she is become loathsome: all that honoured her despise her, because they have seen her nakedness: she herself also sighs, and turns backward.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A sin has Jerusalem sinned; she has, therefore, been made an exile. All who honored her cheapened her, for they saw her shame; she herself sighed and recoiled.


###### Lamentations 1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:9)


טֻמְאָתָ֣הּ בְּשׁוּלֶ֗יהָ לֹ֤א זָֽכְרָה֙ אַחֲרִיתָ֔הּ וַתֵּ֣רֶד פְּלָאִ֔ים אֵ֥ין מְנַחֵ֖ם לָ֑הּ רְאֵ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־עׇנְיִ֔י כִּ֥י הִגְדִּ֖יל אוֹיֵֽב׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Her defilement is at her hem, she was not mindful of her end—so she plummeted astonishingly, with no one to console her. Adonoy look at my suffering, for the enemy has gone to excess.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Her filthiness was in her skirts; she took no thought of her last end; therefore she came down astonishingly: she has no comforter. O Lord, behold my affliction: for the enemy has magnified himself.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Her blood was on her skirts [i.e., she sinned openly]. She did not bethink herself of her latter end, wherefore she has fallen awesomely, with none to console her. See, O L-rd, my affliction, for the foe has grown bold.


###### Lamentations 1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:10)


יָדוֹ֙ פָּ֣רַשׂ צָ֔ר עַ֖ל כׇּל־מַחֲמַדֶּ֑יהָ כִּֽי־רָאֲתָ֤ה גוֹיִם֙ בָּ֣אוּ מִקְדָּשָׁ֔הּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֔יתָה לֹא־יָבֹ֥אוּ בַקָּהָ֖ל לָֽךְ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The oppressor extended his hand over all her treasures, as she witnessed peoples entering her Sanctuary concerning whom You commanded, “Let them not enter your community.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The adversary has spread out his hand upon all her pleasant things: for she has seen that heathen nations invade her sanctuary, those whom Thou didst forbid to enter into Thy congregation.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The foe [(Ammon and Moav)] has stretched out his hand against all her precious things [(Torah scrolls)]. For she has seen nations entering her sanctuary, concerning whom You commanded [viz. Deuteronomy 23:4]: They may not enter the congregation [(of Israel)] unto you.


###### Lamentations 1:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:11)


כׇּל־עַמָּ֤הּ נֶאֱנָחִים֙ מְבַקְשִׁ֣ים לֶ֔חֶם נָתְנ֧וּ (מחמודיהם) [מַחֲמַדֵּיהֶ֛ם] בְּאֹ֖כֶל לְהָשִׁ֣יב נָ֑פֶשׁ רְאֵ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה כִּ֥י הָיִ֖יתִי זוֹלֵלָֽה׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
All her people are groaning, searching for bread. They have given away their treasures for food to keep their souls intact. Look, Adonoy, and take notice how I have become degraded.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All her people sigh, they seek bread; they have given their pleasant things for food to relieve the soul: see, O Lord, and consider; how abject I am become.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All her people sigh, seeking bread. They have given their precious things for food to restore their souls. See, O L-rd, and look upon it, how I have been cheapened.


###### Lamentations 1:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:12)


ל֣וֹא אֲלֵיכֶם֮ כׇּל־עֹ֣בְרֵי דֶ֒רֶךְ֒ הַבִּ֣יטוּ וּרְא֔וּ אִם־יֵ֤שׁ מַכְאוֹב֙ כְּמַכְאֹבִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר עוֹלַ֖ל לִ֑י אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹגָ֣ה יְהֹוָ֔ה בְּי֖וֹם חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
May this not happen to you, all who stray from the path. Notice, see if there is such agony like my agony, that has been visited upon me when Adonoy brought me to grief on the day He vented His wrath.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Is it nothing to you, all you that pass by? behold, and see if there is any pain like my pain, which is done to me, with which the Lord has afflicted me in the day of his fierce anger.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
May [such woe] nevermore [be inflicted upon] all who transgress the way [i.e., the ordinance of the L-rd]! Look and see if there is a pain like my pain that has been wrought unto me, which the L-rd inflicted (upon me) in the day of His wrath.


###### Lamentations 1:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:13)


מִמָּר֛וֹם שָֽׁלַח־אֵ֥שׁ בְּעַצְמֹתַ֖י וַיִּרְדֶּ֑נָּה פָּרַ֨שׂ רֶ֤שֶׁת לְרַגְלַי֙ הֱשִׁיבַ֣נִי אָח֔וֹר נְתָנַ֙נִי֙ שֹֽׁמֵמָ֔ה כׇּל־הַיּ֖וֹם דָּוָֽה׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
From a lofty place He hurled fire into my bones, crushing it. He spread a net for my feet, thrust me back, placed me in ruins, [so that I] suffer throughout the day.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
From above he has sent fire into my bones, and it prevails against them: he has spread a net for my feet, he has turned me back: he has made me desolate and faint all the day.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
From the heights He sent fire against my bones, and He has overmastered [(and broken them)]. He has spread a net for my feet. He has set me back. He has made me desolate, faint all the day.


###### Lamentations 1:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:14)


נִשְׂקַד֩ עֹ֨ל פְּשָׁעַ֜י בְּיָד֗וֹ יִשְׂתָּ֥רְג֛וּ עָל֥וּ עַל־צַוָּארִ֖י הִכְשִׁ֣יל כֹּחִ֑י נְתָנַ֣נִי אֲדֹנָ֔י בִּידֵ֖י לֹא־אוּכַ֥ל קֽוּם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The yoke of my iniquities is recorded in His hand. They have become interwoven, and have encumbered my neck. He has caused my strength to fail. God has placed me in the hands of those whom I cannot withstand.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The yoke of my transgressions is fastened on by his hand: they are knit together, and come up upon my neck: he has made my strength to fall, the Lord has delivered me into the hands of those against whom I am not able to rise up.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The yoke of my offenses has become spotted in His hand [i.e., each of them has become an indelible spot before Him]. They have intermixed and come up upon my neck. My strength has failed. The L-rd has delivered me into the hands of [one against whom] I cannot rise.


###### Lamentations 1:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:15)


סִלָּ֨ה כׇל־אַבִּירַ֤י׀אֲדֹנָי֙ בְּקִרְבִּ֔י קָרָ֥א עָלַ֛י מוֹעֵ֖ד לִשְׁבֹּ֣ר בַּחוּרָ֑י גַּ֚ת דָּרַ֣ךְ אֲדֹנָ֔י לִבְתוּלַ֖ת בַּת־יְהוּדָֽה׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
God has trampled all my stalwarts in my midst, He has proclaimed a gathering against me to crush my young men. [As with] a wine press, God has trodden the maidens of the province of Yehudah.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The Lord has spurned all my mighty men in the midst of me: he has called an assembly against me to crush my young men: the Lord has trodden the virgin, the daughter of Yehuda, as in a winepress.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The L-rd has trodden down all my mighty ones in my midst. He has called out a host against me to break my young men. As a winepress did the L-rd tread the virgin daughter of Judah.


###### Lamentations 1:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:16)


עַל־אֵ֣לֶּה**׀** אֲנִ֣י בוֹכִיָּ֗ה עֵינִ֤י׀עֵינִי֙ יֹ֣רְדָה מַּ֔יִם כִּֽי־רָחַ֥ק מִמֶּ֛נִּי מְנַחֵ֖ם מֵשִׁ֣יב נַפְשִׁ֑י הָי֤וּ בָנַי֙ שֽׁוֹמֵמִ֔ים כִּ֥י גָבַ֖ר אוֹיֵֽב׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For these I weep, my eyes [lit. my eye, my eye] gush water, for remote from me is a consoler who can calm my soul. My sons are devastated, for the enemy has conquered.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For these things I weep; my eye, my eye runs down with water, because the comforter that should relieve my soul is far from me: my children are desolate, because the enemy has prevailed.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Over these I weep. My eye, my eye, [endlessly] sheds water; for consolation is far from me, the restorer of my soul. My children are become desolate, for the foe has grown strong.


###### Lamentations 1:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:17)


פֵּֽרְשָׂ֨ה צִיּ֜וֹן בְּיָדֶ֗יהָ אֵ֤ין מְנַחֵם֙ לָ֔הּ צִוָּ֧ה יְהֹוָ֛ה לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב סְבִיבָ֣יו צָרָ֑יו הָיְתָ֧ה יְרוּשָׁלַ֛͏ִם לְנִדָּ֖ה בֵּינֵיהֶֽם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
*Tzion* spreads her arms, there is no one to console her. Adonoy has commanded, concerning Yaakov, that his oppressors surround him. Jerusalem has become despicable among them.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Żiyyon spreads out her hands, and there is none to comfort her: the Lord has commanded against Ya῾aqov, adversaries round about him: Yerushalayim is like a menstruous woman among them.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Zion has spread out her hands [(in agony)]; there is none to console her. The L-rd has commanded against Jacob his foes roundabout him. [(Even when they were exiled to Bavel and Ashur, Sancherev exiled their foes, Ammon and Moav, and settled them around them to harass them.)] Jerusalem has become an outcast among them.


###### Lamentations 1:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:18)


צַדִּ֥יק ה֛וּא יְהֹוָ֖ה כִּ֣י פִ֣יהוּ מָרִ֑יתִי שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֣א כׇל־[הָֽעַמִּ֗ים] (עמים) וּרְאוּ֙ מַכְאֹבִ֔י בְּתוּלֹתַ֥י וּבַחוּרַ֖י הָלְכ֥וּ בַשֶּֽׁבִי׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Adonoy is just, for it is I who rejected His word. Listen here, all you nations, look at my torment; my maidens and my young men have gone into captivity.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The Lord is righteous; for I have rebelled against his word: hear, I pray you, all the peoples, and behold my pain: my virgins and my young men are gone into captivity.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Righteous is the L-rd, for I have rebelled against His word. Hear, I pray you, all the peoples, and see my pain. My virgins and my young men are gone into captivity.


###### Lamentations 1:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:19)


קָרָ֤אתִי לַֽמְאַהֲבַי֙ הֵ֣מָּה רִמּ֔וּנִי כֹּהֲנַ֥י וּזְקֵנַ֖י בָּעִ֣יר גָּוָ֑עוּ כִּֽי־בִקְשׁ֥וּ אֹ֙כֶל֙ לָ֔מוֹ וְיָשִׁ֖יבוּ אֶת־נַפְשָֽׁם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I cried out to those who appeared to love me, but they deceived me. My *kohanim* and elders expired in the city while they searched for food for themselves, to sustain their souls.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I called for my lovers, but they deceived me: my priests and my elders perished in the city, while they sought food for themselves to relieve their souls.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I called [(those who appeared to be)] my lovers; they deceived me. My priests and my elders perished in the city while seeking bread for themselves wherewith to restore their souls.


###### Lamentations 1:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:20)


רְאֵ֨ה יְהֹוָ֤ה כִּֽי־צַר־לִי֙ מֵעַ֣י חֳמַרְמָ֔רוּ נֶהְפַּ֤ךְ לִבִּי֙ בְּקִרְבִּ֔י כִּ֥י מָר֖וֹ מָרִ֑יתִי מִח֥וּץ שִׁכְּלָה־חֶ֖רֶב בַּבַּ֥יִת כַּמָּֽוֶת׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Adonoy, see how oppressed I am? My gut has shriveled, my heart is twisting inside me, because of my rebelliousness. Outside, the sword brings bereavement, within, it is like death.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Behold, O Lord; for I am in distress: my bowels are troubled; my heart is turned within me; for I have grievously rebelled: abroad the sword bereaves, at home it is like death.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
See, O L-rd, that I am afflicted; my innards are shriveled. My heart is overturned in my midst, for I have deeply rebelled. Outside, the sword bereaved; inside [it was] like death.


###### Lamentations 1:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:21)


שָׁמְע֞וּ כִּ֧י נֶאֱנָחָ֣ה אָ֗נִי אֵ֤ין מְנַחֵם֙ לִ֔י כׇּל־אֹ֨יְבַ֜י שָׁמְע֤וּ רָֽעָתִי֙ שָׂ֔שׂוּ כִּ֥י אַתָּ֖ה עָשִׂ֑יתָ הֵבֵ֥אתָ יוֹם־קָרָ֖אתָ וְיִֽהְי֥וּ כָמֹֽנִי׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
They have heard how I groan, and no one consoles me; all my enemies have heard of my calamity, and rejoiced, for it is Your doing. Bring the day that You proclaimed, and let them resemble me.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
They have heard that I sigh: there is none to comfort me: all my enemies have heard of my trouble; they are glad that Thou hast done it: Thou wilt bring the day that Thou hast called, and they shall be like me.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
They have heard how I sigh, but none console me. All of my foes have heard of my evil. They have rejoiced, for You have wrought (it) [i.e., You have caused them to hate me by forbidding me to intermingle with them]. Would that you brought [upon them] the day [(of destruction)] that You called out [upon me], that they be as I.


###### Lamentations 1:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/1:22)


תָּבֹ֨א כׇל־רָעָתָ֤ם לְפָנֶ֙יךָ֙ וְעוֹלֵ֣ל לָ֔מוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עוֹלַ֛לְתָּ לִ֖י עַ֣ל כׇּל־פְּשָׁעָ֑י כִּֽי־רַבּ֥וֹת אַנְחֹתַ֖י וְלִבִּ֥י דַוָּֽי׃{פ}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Let all their evil come before You, and do, to them, what You have done to me for all my iniquity, for I groan much, and my heart aches.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Let all their wickedness come before Thee; and do to them, as Thou hast done to me for all my transgressions: for my sighs are many, and my heart is faint.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Let all their evil come [(in remembrance)] before You, and do to them as You have done to me for all of my offenses; for my sighs are many and my heart is faint.



## Chapter 2

###### Lamentations 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/2:1)


אֵיכָה֩ יָעִ֨יב בְּאַפּ֤וֹ׀אֲדֹנָי֙ אֶת־בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן הִשְׁלִ֤יךְ מִשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ אֶ֔רֶץ תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹא־זָכַ֥ר הֲדֹם־רַגְלָ֖יו בְּי֥וֹם אַפּֽוֹ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
How can it be that God, in his wrath, has cast a gloom upon the city of *Tzion,* that He flung from heaven to earth the glory of Israel, and did not remember His footstool on the day of His wrath?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
How has the Lord covered the daughter of Żiyyon with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven to earth the beauty of Yisra᾽el, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger!


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
How the L-rd has beclouded in His wrath the daughter of Zion! He has cast down from heaven to earth the glory of Israel and not remembered His footstool [(the Temple)] in the day of His wrath.


###### Lamentations 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/2:2)


בִּלַּ֨ע אֲדֹנָ֜י (לא) [וְלֹ֣א] חָמַ֗ל אֵ֚ת כׇּל־נְא֣וֹת יַעֲקֹ֔ב הָרַ֧ס בְּעֶבְרָת֛וֹ מִבְצְרֵ֥י בַת־יְהוּדָ֖ה הִגִּ֣יעַ לָאָ֑רֶץ חִלֵּ֥ל מַמְלָכָ֖ה וְשָׂרֶֽיהָ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
God swallowed up mercilessly every residence of Ya’akov. He smashed, in His fury, the fortifications of the province of Yehudah, razing them to the ground. He desecrated the kingdom and its princes.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The Lord has swallowed up without pity all the habitations of Ya῾aqov: he has thrown down in his wrath the strongholds of the daughter of Yehuda; he has brought them down to the ground: he has profaned the kingdom and its princes.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The L-rd has swallowed up without pity all the habitations of Jacob. He has destroyed in His wrath the strongholds of the daughter of Judah. He has brought them down to the ground. He has profaned the kingdom [(Israel, "a kingdom of priests")] and its princes.


###### Lamentations 2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/2:3)


גָּדַ֣ע בׇּֽחֳרִי־אַ֗ף כֹּ֚ל קֶ֣רֶן יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֵשִׁ֥יב אָח֛וֹר יְמִינ֖וֹ מִפְּנֵ֣י אוֹיֵ֑ב וַיִּבְעַ֤ר בְּיַעֲקֹב֙ כְּאֵ֣שׁ לֶֽהָבָ֔ה אָכְלָ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He tore down, in his wrath, all the power [lit. horn] of Israel. He withheld His right arm in the face of the enemy. He ignited Ya’akov like a blazing flame which consumes on every side.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has cut off in his fierce anger all the horn of Yisra᾽el: he has drawn back his right hand from before the enemy, and he has burned against Ya῾aqov like a flaming fire, which devours round about.

###### Lamentations 2:18

###### Lamentations 2:19
