Arise, cry out in the night: in the beginning of the watches pour out thy heart like water before the face of the Lord: lift up thy hands towards him for the life of thy young children, that faint for hunger at the head of every street.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Arise, cry out in the night, at the start of [(the last two)] of the [(three night-)] watches. Spill out your heart as water before the presence of the L-rd. Lift your hands to Him for the Lives of your young ones, who languish with hunger at the head of every street.


###### Lamentations 2:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/2:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/2:20)


רְאֵ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה לְמִ֖י עוֹלַ֣לְתָּ כֹּ֑ה אִם־תֹּאכַ֨לְנָה נָשִׁ֤ים פִּרְיָם֙ עֹלְלֵ֣י טִפֻּחִ֔ים אִם־יֵהָרֵ֛ג בְּמִקְדַּ֥שׁ אֲדֹנָ֖י כֹּהֵ֥ן וְנָבִֽיא׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Adonoy, look, notice upon whom you have visited this, when women devour their own offspring, infants who were lovingly attended. When in the Sanctuary of God, was murdered—a *kohein* and prophet.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Behold, O Lord, and consider to whom Thou hast done this. Shall the women eat their fruit, their cherished babes? shall priest and prophet be slain in the sanctuary of the Lord?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
See, O L-rd, and behold: To whom have You wrought thus? Shall women eat their fruit? their fondled young ones? Shall there be killed in the sanctuary of the L-rd, priest and prophet?


###### Lamentations 2:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/2:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/2:21)


שָׁכְב֨וּ לָאָ֤רֶץ חוּצוֹת֙ נַ֣עַר וְזָקֵ֔ן בְּתוּלֹתַ֥י וּבַחוּרַ֖י נָפְל֣וּ בֶחָ֑רֶב הָרַ֙גְתָּ֙ בְּי֣וֹם אַפֶּ֔ךָ טָבַ֖חְתָּ לֹ֥א חָמָֽלְתָּ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
On the ground, in the streets they lie, young and old. My maidens and youths have fallen by the sword. You killed, on the day of Your wrath, you slaughtered mercilessly.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Young and old lie on the ground in the streets: my virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword; Thou hast slain them in the day of Thy anger; Thou hast killed, and not pitied.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
They lay on the ground in the streets, young and old. My virgins and my young men fell by the sword. You killed on the day of Your wrath; You slaughtered; You did not pity.


###### Lamentations 2:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/2:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/2:22)


תִּקְרָא֩ כְי֨וֹם מוֹעֵ֤ד מְגוּרַי֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב וְלֹ֥א הָיָ֛ה בְּי֥וֹם אַף־יְהֹוָ֖ה פָּלִ֣יט וְשָׂרִ֑יד אֲשֶׁר־טִפַּ֥חְתִּי וְרִבִּ֖יתִי אֹיְבִ֥י כִלָּֽם׃{פ}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
You summoned, as if to a festive day, my surrounding neighbors. There was no one, on the day of Adonoy’s wrath, who found refuge or survived. Those whom I attended lovingly and reared, my enemy has annihilated.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou hast called as in the day of a solemn assembly, my terrors round about, so that in the day of the Lord’s anger none escaped or remained: those that I have cherished and brought up my enemy has consumed.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
You have called, as on a festival day, my [evil] neighbors roundabout [to participate in the slaughter], and there remained not on the day of the L-rd's wrath a survivor or a remnant. Those [(children)] whom I fondled and reared, my foe destroyed.



## Chapter 3

###### Lamentations 3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:1)


אֲנִ֤י הַגֶּ֙בֶר֙ רָאָ֣ה עֳנִ֔י בְּשֵׁ֖בֶט עֶבְרָתֽוֹ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I am the man who has seen torment, by the rod of His fury.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I am the man who has seen affliction by the rod of his wrath.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I [(Jeremiah, am the prophet who)] has seen affliction [(i.e., the destruction of the Temple), more so than any other prophet who foretold it (it not having taken place in their days, but in mine)], by the rod of His wrath.


###### Lamentations 3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:2)


אוֹתִ֥י נָהַ֛ג וַיֹּלַ֖ךְ חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וְלֹא־אֽוֹר׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He drove me, led me on, into total darkness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has led me, and brought me into darkness, but not into light.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He has led me, and He has brought [me into] darkness and not light.


###### Lamentations 3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:3)


אַ֣ךְ בִּ֥י יָשֻׁ֛ב יַהֲפֹ֥ךְ יָד֖וֹ כׇּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
At me alone, He repeatedly swings His hand, throughout the day.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Surely he is turned against me; he turns his hand against me all the day.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Only against me does He renew [His blows], turning His hand [against me] all the day.


###### Lamentations 3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:4)


בִּלָּ֤ה בְשָׂרִי֙ וְעוֹרִ֔י שִׁבַּ֖ר עַצְמוֹתָֽי׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He rotted my flesh and skin, smashed my bones.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has made my flesh and my skin to waste away; he has broken my bones.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He has worn away my flesh and my skin. He has broken my bones.


###### Lamentations 3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:5)


בָּנָ֥ה עָלַ֛י וַיַּקַּ֖ף רֹ֥אשׁ וּתְלָאָֽה׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He constructed, against me, encircling me with gall and bitter plants.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has built a mound against me, and has beset me round about at head and hell.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He has built [(mounds)] upon me and has encompassed me with gall and woe.


###### Lamentations 3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:6)


בְּמַחֲשַׁכִּ֥ים הוֹשִׁיבַ֖נִי כְּמֵתֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He seated me in gloom like the dead of the world.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has set me in dark places, as those who are long ago dead.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
In darkness did He seat me, as the dead of yore.


###### Lamentations 3:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:7)


גָּדַ֧ר בַּעֲדִ֛י וְלֹ֥א אֵצֵ֖א הִכְבִּ֥יד נְחׇשְׁתִּֽי׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He fenced me in and I cannot go out, He chained me heavily.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has hedged me about, so that I cannot get out: he has made my chain heavy.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He has fenced me about; I cannot escape. He has weighted down my [foot] with shackles.


###### Lamentations 3:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:8)


גַּ֣ם כִּ֤י אֶזְעַק֙ וַאֲשַׁוֵּ֔עַ שָׂתַ֖ם תְּפִלָּתִֽי׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Even when I cry out and implore, He represses my prayer.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Even when I cry and call for help, he stops up my prayer.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Though I call and cry out, He closes up [(the "windows of heaven" to)] my prayer.


###### Lamentations 3:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:9)


גָּדַ֤ר דְּרָכַי֙ בְּגָזִ֔ית נְתִיבֹתַ֖י עִוָּֽה׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He blockaded my roads with stone, He made my paths crooked.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has enclosed my ways with hewn stone, he has made my paths crooked.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He has blocked my ways with hewn stones; He has made my paths crooked [(by blocking the roads)].


###### Lamentations 3:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:10)


דֹּ֣ב אֹרֵ֥ב הוּא֙ לִ֔י (אריה) [אֲרִ֖י] בְּמִסְתָּרִֽים׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He is a bear lying in wait for me, a stealthy lion.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He is to me like a bear lying in wait, and like a lion in secret places.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He has become a bear in ambush to me; a lion in the covert.


###### Lamentations 3:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:11)


דְּרָכַ֥י סוֹרֵ֛ר וַֽיְפַשְּׁחֵ֖נִי שָׂמַ֥נִי שֹׁמֵֽם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He spread thorns across my roads, He made me hurdle them. He devastated me.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has turned aside my ways, and pulled me in pieces: he has made me desolate.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He has turned aside my ways and straitened my strides; He has made me desolate.


###### Lamentations 3:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:12)


דָּרַ֤ךְ קַשְׁתּוֹ֙ וַיַּצִּיבֵ֔נִי כַּמַּטָּרָ֖א לַחֵֽץ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He arched His bow, and positioned me as a target for the arrow.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He has bent His bow and set me up as a target for the arrow.


###### Lamentations 3:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:13)


הֵבִיא֙ בְּכִלְיֹתָ֔י בְּנֵ֖י אַשְׁפָּתֽוֹ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He aimed the arrows of His quiver into my kidneys.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has caused the arrows of his quiver to enter into my reins.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He has brought into my reins the "sons of His quiver" [i.e., His arrows].


###### Lamentations 3:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:14)


הָיִ֤יתִי שְּׂחֹק֙ לְכׇל־עַמִּ֔י נְגִינָתָ֖ם כׇּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I was ridiculed by all my people, the subject of their satirical songs throughout the day.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I am become a derision to all my people; and their song all the day.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I was a mockery to all my people, their song the entire day.


###### Lamentations 3:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:15)


הִשְׂבִּיעַ֥נִי בַמְּרוֹרִ֖ים הִרְוַ֥נִי לַעֲנָֽה׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He satiated me with bitterness, glutted me with bitter plants.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has filled me with bitterness, he has sated me with wormwood.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He has sated me with bitterness; He has glutted me with wormwood.


###### Lamentations 3:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:16)


וַיַּגְרֵ֤ס בֶּֽחָצָץ֙ שִׁנָּ֔י הִכְפִּישַׁ֖נִי בָּאֵֽפֶר׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He ground my teeth on pebblestones, He made me grovel in the dust.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has also broken my teeth with gravel stones, he has pressed me down into the ashes.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He broke my teeth with gravel [(The exiles were constrained to knead their dough in the ground and earth particles adhered to it)]; He pressed me [i.e., my face] down to the dust.


###### Lamentations 3:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:17)


וַתִּזְנַ֧ח מִשָּׁל֛וֹם נַפְשִׁ֖י נָשִׁ֥יתִי טוֹבָֽה׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
My soul despaired of peace, I have forgotten goodness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
My soul is far removed from peace: I have forgotten prosperity.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
My soul was removed from peace; I forgot good.


###### Lamentations 3:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:18)


וָאֹמַר֙ אָבַ֣ד נִצְחִ֔י וְתוֹחַלְתִּ֖י מֵיְהֹוָֽה׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I thought that my world was ruined, my hope from Adonoy.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And I said, My strength and my hope are perished from the Lord.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I said: My world and my hope are lost from the L-rd.


###### Lamentations 3:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:19)


זְכׇר־עׇנְיִ֥י וּמְרוּדִ֖י לַעֲנָ֥ה וָרֹֽאשׁ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Remember my torment and my lament, the bitter plants and the gall.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Remember my affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the gall.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Remember my affliction and my plaint, wormwood and gall.


###### Lamentations 3:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:20)


זָכ֣וֹר תִּזְכּ֔וֹר (ותשיח) [וְתָשׁ֥וֹחַ] עָלַ֖י נַפְשִֽׁי׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
When remembering, my soul is utterly dejected.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
My soul has them still in remembrance, and is bowed down within me.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
My soul well remembers and is bowed down within me.


###### Lamentations 3:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:21)


זֹ֛את אָשִׁ֥יב אֶל־לִבִּ֖י עַל־כֵּ֥ן אוֹחִֽיל׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Still, I take this to heart, and, therefore, continue to hope:


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
This I recall to my mind, therefore I have hope:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
(But) this shall I return to my heart, and, therefore, I shall hope [again]:


###### Lamentations 3:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:22)


חַֽסְדֵ֤י יְהֹוָה֙ כִּ֣י לֹא־תָ֔מְנוּ כִּ֥י לֹא־כָל֖וּ רַחֲמָֽיו׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
By the grace of Adonoy we have not perished, for His compassion is not ended.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
that the Lord’s steadfast love has not ceased, and that his compassions do not fail.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The lovingkindnesses of the L-rd do not cease, for His mercies are endless.


###### Lamentations 3:23

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:23](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:23)


חֲדָשִׁים֙ לַבְּקָרִ֔ים רַבָּ֖ה אֱמוּנָתֶֽךָ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Each morning refreshed, Your faithfulness is immense.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
They renew themselves every morning; great is Your trust [(to fulfill Your assurances, and our trust in You to do so)].


###### Lamentations 3:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:24)


חֶלְקִ֤י יְהֹוָה֙ אָמְרָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֔י עַל־כֵּ֖ן אוֹחִ֥יל לֽוֹ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
‘Adonoy is my portion,’ my soul declares, I therefore hope to Him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The Lord is my portion, says my soul; therefore I will hope in him.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The L-rd is my portion, my soul has said; and, therefore, I shall trust in Him.


###### Lamentations 3:25

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:25](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:25)


ט֤וֹב יְהֹוָה֙ לְקֹוָ֔ו לְנֶ֖פֶשׁ תִּדְרְשֶֽׁנּוּ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Adonoy is good to those who hope to Him, to the soul which searches for Him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The Lord is good to those who wait for him, to the soul that seeks him.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The L-rd is good to those who hope in him, to the soul that seeks Him.


###### Lamentations 3:26

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:26](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:26)


ט֤וֹב וְיָחִיל֙ וְדוּמָ֔ם לִתְשׁוּעַ֖ת יְהֹוָֽה׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
It is good to hope, in stillness, for Adonoy’s deliverance.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
It is good that a man should quietly hope for the salvation of the Lord.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
It is good that one hope and await the salvation of the L-rd.


###### Lamentations 3:27

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:27](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:27)


ט֣וֹב לַגֶּ֔בֶר כִּֽי־יִשָּׂ֥א עֹ֖ל בִּנְעוּרָֽיו׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
It is good for man to bear a yoke during his youth.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.


###### Lamentations 3:28

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:61](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:61)


שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ חֶרְפָּתָם֙ יְהֹוָ֔ה כׇּל־מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֖ם עָלָֽי׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
You have heard their affronts, Adonoy all their [insulting] thoughts concerning me.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou hast heard their insult, O Lord, and all their devices against me;


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
You have heard their insults, O L-rd, all their thoughts against me,


###### Lamentations 3:62

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:62](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:62)


שִׂפְתֵ֤י קָמַי֙ וְהֶגְיוֹנָ֔ם עָלַ֖י כׇּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
My opponents’ conversation, their unspoken thoughts, are about me, throughout the day.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
the lips of those who rose up against me, and their muttering against me all the day.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
the lips of those who rose against me, and their muttering against me all the day.


###### Lamentations 3:63

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:63](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:63)


שִׁבְתָּ֤ם וְקִֽימָתָם֙ הַבִּ֔יטָה אֲנִ֖י מַנְגִּינָתָֽם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Observe them as they sit or rise—I am the subject of their satirical songs.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Behold their sitting down, and their rising up; I am their song.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Behold their sitting down and their rising up — I am their song.


###### Lamentations 3:64

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:64](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:64)


תָּשִׁ֨יב לָהֶ֥ם גְּמ֛וּל יְהֹוָ֖ה כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Inflict punishment on them, Adonoy as befits their deeds.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Render to them a recompense, O Lord, according to the work of their hands.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Render them their recompense, O L-rd, according to the work of their hands.


###### Lamentations 3:65

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:65](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:65)


תִּתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ מְגִנַּת־לֵ֔ב תַּאֲלָֽתְךָ֖ לָהֶֽם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Break their hearts, turn them into fools.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Give them sorrow of heart; Thy curse be on them!


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Give them breaking of heart; [cast] Your curse upon them!


###### Lamentations 3:66

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:66](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/3:66)


תִּרְדֹּ֤ף בְּאַף֙ וְתַשְׁמִידֵ֔ם מִתַּ֖חַת שְׁמֵ֥י יְהֹוָֽה׃{פ}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Pursue wrathfully, annihilate them from under Adonoy’s heavens.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the Lord.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Pursue (them) in wrath and wipe them out from under the heavens of the L-rd!



## Chapter 4

###### Lamentations 4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:1)


אֵיכָה֙ יוּעַ֣ם זָהָ֔ב יִשְׁנֶ֖א הַכֶּ֣תֶם הַטּ֑וֹב תִּשְׁתַּפֵּ֙כְנָה֙ אַבְנֵי־קֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּרֹ֖אשׁ כׇּל־חוּצֽוֹת׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
How can it be that the golden glow has paled, that the splendid jewel is altered? Sacred gems are spilled at the head of every street.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
How is the gold become dim! how is the most fine gold changed! the hallowed stones are poured out at the top of every street.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
How is the gold [(the face of King Yoshiyahu, which glowed like gold)] dulled! [How is] the fine gold transformed! [viz. Chronicles 35:25], the hallowed stones [(young men who shone like precious stones)] spilled out at the head of every street!


###### Lamentations 4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:2)


בְּנֵ֤י צִיּוֹן֙ הַיְקָרִ֔ים הַמְסֻלָּאִ֖ים בַּפָּ֑ז אֵיכָ֤ה נֶחְשְׁבוּ֙ לְנִבְלֵי־חֶ֔רֶשׂ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י יוֹצֵֽר׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The cherished children of *Tzion,* who were evaluated in golden currency—how can they be considered like flasks of clay, the potter’s handiwork?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The precious sons of Żiyyon, comparable to fine gold, how are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The precious sons of Zion, valued as fine gold — how are they become as earthen jugs, the work of the potter!


###### Lamentations 4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:3)


גַּם־[תַּנִּים֙] (תנין) חָ֣לְצוּ שַׁ֔ד הֵינִ֖יקוּ גּוּרֵיהֶ֑ן בַּת־עַמִּ֣י לְאַכְזָ֔ר (כי ענים) [כַּיְעֵינִ֖ים] בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Even the serpent bares its breast to nurse its young, yet the daughters of my people have become brutal, like the desert ostrich.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Even the jackals draw out the breast, they give suck to their young ones: the daughter of my people is become cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Even the jackals draw out the breast; they give suck to their young ones. The daughter of my people has become cruel [(They deafen themselves to the cries of their starving children to assuage their own hunger)], like ostriches in the wilderness.


###### Lamentations 4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:4)


דָּבַ֨ק לְשׁ֥וֹן יוֹנֵ֛ק אֶל־חִכּ֖וֹ בַּצָּמָ֑א עֽוֹלָלִים֙ שָׁ֣אֲלוּ לֶ֔חֶם פֹּרֵ֖שׂ אֵ֥ין לָהֶֽם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The tongue of the nursing infant pasted to its palate with thirst, babies pleaded for bread, but no one offered it to them.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The tongue of the sucking child cleaves to the roof of his mouth for thirst: the young children ask bread, and no man gives it to them.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The tongue of the nursing child cleaves to its palate in thirst. Young children begged for bread. There is no one to break it for them.


###### Lamentations 4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:5)


הָאֹֽכְלִים֙ לְמַ֣עֲדַנִּ֔ים נָשַׁ֖מּוּ בַּחוּצ֑וֹת הָאֱמֻנִים֙ עֲלֵ֣י תוֹלָ֔ע חִבְּק֖וּ אַשְׁפַּתּֽוֹת׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Those who feasted on delicacies were ravaged in the streets, those raised on richly colored brocade embraced the dungheaps.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
They that did feed on dainties are desolate in the streets: they that were brought up in scarlet embrace dunghills.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Those who were fed on delicacies expired in the streets. Those who were reared in scarlet embraced the dung hills.


###### Lamentations 4:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:6)


וַיִּגְדַּל֙ עֲוֺ֣ן בַּת־עַמִּ֔י מֵֽחַטַּ֖את סְדֹ֑ם הַֽהֲפוּכָ֣ה כְמוֹ־רָ֔גַע וְלֹא־חָ֥לוּ בָ֖הּ יָדָֽיִם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
My people’s transgressions surpassed the sins of S’dom, which was instantaneously overturned, untouched by [human] hands.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For the doom of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sedom, that was overthrown as in a moment, no hands being laid upon her.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the transgression of the daughter of my people [(judging from the severity and duration of its punishment)] was greater than the sins of Sodom, which was overturned but in a moment, the hands [of enemies] not prevailing in her [(but those of angels)].


###### Lamentations 4:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:7)


זַכּ֤וּ נְזִירֶ֙יהָ֙ מִשֶּׁ֔לֶג צַח֖וּ מֵחָלָ֑ב אָ֤דְמוּ עֶ֙צֶם֙ מִפְּנִינִ֔ים סַפִּ֖יר גִּזְרָתָֽם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Her nazirites were more pristine than snow, more lustrous than milk. Those who appeared redder than pearls, who were hewn like sapphire—

Her Nazirites were purer than snow, they were whiter than milk, they were more ruddy in body than rubies, their polishing was as of sapphire:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Her [(Jerusalem's)] Nazirites were purer than snow, whiter than milk, ruddier than rubies, formed as the sapphire.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:8)


חָשַׁ֤ךְ מִשְּׁחוֹר֙ תׇּֽאֳרָ֔ם לֹ֥א נִכְּר֖וּ בַּחוּצ֑וֹת צָפַ֤ד עוֹרָם֙ עַל־עַצְמָ֔ם יָבֵ֖שׁ הָיָ֥ה כָעֵֽץ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Have become blacker than charcoal in appearance, are unrecognizable in the streets. Their skin is shrivelled on their bones, having become dry as wood.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
now their visage is blacker than coal; they are not known in the streets: their skin is shrivelled upon their bones; it is withered, it is become like a stick.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[But now,] darker than coal is their visage; they are not recognized in the streets. Their skin is shriveled upon them; it has become dry as a stick.


###### Lamentations 4:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:9)


טוֹבִ֤ים הָיוּ֙ חַלְלֵי־חֶ֔רֶב מֵֽחַלְלֵ֖י רָעָ֑ב שֶׁ֣הֵ֤ם יָזֻ֙בוּ֙ מְדֻקָּרִ֔ים מִתְּנוּבֹ֖ת שָׂדָֽי׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
They were at an advantage—those who died by the sword—over those who died of starvation, for they dripped, with burst bellies, from [eating] the produce of the fields.

Those slain with the sword are better than those slain with hunger: for when pierced through, the former do ooze with the produce of the fields.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
More fortunate were those slain by the sword than those slain by hunger. For they [(the latter)] oozed [excrement] when [their bellies] split [(from hunger and)] from the fruits of the field [i.e., from the roots and grasses that they were forced to subsist on].


###### Lamentations 4:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:10)


יְדֵ֗י נָשִׁים֙ רַחֲמָ֣נִיּ֔וֹת בִּשְּׁל֖וּ יַלְדֵיהֶ֑ן הָי֤וּ לְבָרוֹת֙ לָ֔מוֹ בְּשֶׁ֖בֶר בַּת־עַמִּֽי׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The hands of merciful women cooked their children. They became their food, when my people disintegrated.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Hands of compassionate women have boiled their own children: they were their food in the destruction of the daughter of my people.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The hands of merciful women boiled their children. They were a meal to them in the breaking of the daughter of my people.


###### Lamentations 4:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:11)


כִּלָּ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־חֲמָת֔וֹ שָׁפַ֖ךְ חֲר֣וֹן אַפּ֑וֹ וַיַּצֶּת־אֵ֣שׁ בְּצִיּ֔וֹן וַתֹּ֖אכַל יְסֹדֹתֶֽיהָ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
God spent His wrath, poured out His rage. He ignited a blaze in *Tzion,* and it consumed its foundations.

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The L-rd has consummated His wrath [(which burned in Him for many years)]. He has poured out His burning wrath. And He has kindled a fire in Zion, which has consumed her foundations.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:12)


לֹ֤א הֶאֱמִ֙ינוּ֙ מַלְכֵי־אֶ֔רֶץ (וכל) [כֹּ֖ל] יֹשְׁבֵ֣י תֵבֵ֑ל כִּ֤י יָבֹא֙ צַ֣ר וְאוֹיֵ֔ב בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The kings of the earth did not believe nor did all the residents of the world [believe] that an oppressor or an enemy could enter the portals of Jerusalem.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The kings of the earth, and all the inhabitants of the world, would not have believed that the adversary and the enemy would enter the gates of Yerushalayim.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The kings of the earth could not believe, and all the inhabitants of the world, that the oppressor and the foe could enter the gates of Jerusalem.


###### Lamentations 4:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:13)


מֵֽחַטֹּ֣אות נְבִיאֶ֔יהָ עֲוֺנֹ֖ת כֹּהֲנֶ֑יהָ הַשֹּׁפְכִ֥ים בְּקִרְבָּ֖הּ דַּ֥ם צַדִּיקִֽים׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For the sins of her false prophets, the transgressions of her *kohanim,* who spilled, within her, the blood of the righteous.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Because of the sins of her prophets, the transgressions of her priests, the spilling in her midst of the blood of the righteous.


###### Lamentations 4:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:14)


נָע֤וּ עִוְרִים֙ בַּֽחוּצ֔וֹת נְגֹֽאֲל֖וּ בַּדָּ֑ם בְּלֹ֣א יֽוּכְל֔וּ יִגְּע֖וּ בִּלְבֻשֵׁיהֶֽם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The blind slithered in the streets, filthied with blood, so that no one could bear touching their garments.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
They wandered blind through the streets, polluted with blood, so that none could touch their garments.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The blind wandered in the streets, smeared with the blood [(of the slain, on which they slipped)]. [Their kin,] being unable to touch their garments —


###### Lamentations 4:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:15)


ס֣וּרוּ טָמֵ֞א קָ֣רְאוּ לָ֗מוֹ ס֤וּרוּ ס֙וּרוּ֙ אַל־תִּגָּ֔עוּ כִּ֥י נָצ֖וּ גַּם־נָ֑עוּ אָֽמְרוּ֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֖פוּ לָגֽוּר׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
“Get away, you are contaminated!” they shouted at them. Get away, get away, don’t touch!”, for they were obscene and slithering. They said, among the nations, “They will no longer reside here.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Away! unclean! they cried at them; away! away! do not touch. So they fled, and wandered away: among the nations it was said, They shall no longer sojourn here.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Away! unclean ones, they cried out to them. Away! Away! do not touch. For they were befouled; they had also slipped [on the blood]. They said among the nations: They will not continue to live [here].


###### Lamentations 4:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:16)


פְּנֵ֤י יְהֹוָה֙ חִלְּקָ֔ם לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֖יף לְהַבִּיטָ֑ם פְּנֵ֤י כֹהֲנִים֙ לֹ֣א נָשָׂ֔אוּ (זקנים) [וּזְקֵנִ֖ים] לֹ֥א חָנָֽנוּ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
In Adonoy’s glaring anger, He dispersed them; He will no longer pay attention to them, because they did not venerate the *kohanim,* nor oblige the elders.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The anger of the Lord has divided them; he will no more regard them: they respected not the persons of the priests, they were not gracious to the elders.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The face [(of wrath)] of the L-rd has divided them [(among the nations)]. He will look on them no more, [for] they did not respect the priests; they were not gracious to the elders [(when they were at peace)].


###### Lamentations 4:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:17)


(עודינה) [עוֹדֵ֙ינוּ֙] תִּכְלֶ֣ינָה עֵינֵ֔ינוּ אֶל־עֶזְרָתֵ֖נוּ הָ֑בֶל בְּצִפִּיָּתֵ֣נוּ צִפִּ֔ינוּ אֶל־גּ֖וֹי לֹ֥א יוֹשִֽׁעַ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
We persisted in longingly eyeing illusive reinforcements, our yearning was for a nation that would never come to our aid.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
As for us, our eyes do yet fail for our vain help: in our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[When the evil came upon us,] our eyes yet looked out for our vain help [(Egypt)], keeping a watch for a nation that would not save.


###### Lamentations 4:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:18)


צָד֣וּ צְעָדֵ֔ינוּ מִלֶּ֖כֶת בִּרְחֹבֹתֵ֑ינוּ קָרַ֥ב קִצֵּ֛נוּ מָלְא֥וּ יָמֵ֖ינוּ כִּי־בָ֥א קִצֵּֽנוּ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
They lurked behind our footsteps, so that we couldn’t walk our streets, [we felt that] our end was near, our time was up, we were finished.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
They hunt our steps, that we cannot walk in our broad places: our end is near, our days are fulfilled; for our end is come.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
They [(our enemies)] spied out our steps against walking in our broad places. Our end has drawn near. Our days have run full, for our end has come.


###### Lamentations 4:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:19)


קַלִּ֤ים הָיוּ֙ רֹדְפֵ֔ינוּ מִנִּשְׁרֵ֖י שָׁמָ֑יִם עַל־הֶהָרִ֣ים דְּלָקֻ֔נוּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר אָ֥רְבוּ לָֽנוּ׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles in the skies. They hounded us on the hills, laid ambush for us in the wilderness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Our pursuers were swifter than the vultures in the sky: they chased us upon the mountains, they lay in wait for us in the wilderness.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Swifter were our pursuers than the eagles in the heavens. On the mountains they chased us; in the desert they lay in wait for us.


###### Lamentations 4:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:20)


ר֤וּחַ אַפֵּ֙ינוּ֙ מְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהֹוָ֔ה נִלְכַּ֖ד בִּשְׁחִיתוֹתָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְנוּ בְּצִלּ֖וֹ נִֽחְיֶ֥ה בַגּוֹיִֽם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The breath of our nostrils, Adonoy’s anointed, was ensnared in their pitfalls, when we thought that under His shelter, we would survive among the nations.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the Lord, was taken in their pits, of whom we said, Under his shadow we shall live among the nations.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the L-rd [(King Yoshiyahu, viz. II Chronicles 35:25)] was caught in their pits — he of whom we said: Under his [(protective)] shadow shall we live among the nations.


###### Lamentations 4:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:21)


שִׂ֤ישִׂי וְשִׂמְחִי֙ בַּת־אֱד֔וֹם (יושבתי) [יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת] בְּאֶ֣רֶץ ע֑וּץ גַּם־עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ תַּעֲבׇר־כּ֔וֹס תִּשְׁכְּרִ֖י וְתִתְעָרִֽי׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Rejoice in gladness, city of Edom, residing in the land of Utz—unto you, as well, shall the come to pass, intoxicating you till you vomit.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, that dwellest in the land of ῾Uż; the cup shall also pass over to thee: thou shalt be drunken, and strip thyself bare.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[(Jeremiah now prophesies the destruction of the second Temple by the Romans:)] Rejoice and regale, O daughter of Edom, dweller in the land of Utz, [but] over you, too, will pass the cup [(of punishment)]. You will become drunk [on it] and vomit [it up]!


###### Lamentations 4:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/4:22)


תַּם־עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֖יף לְהַגְלוֹתֵ֑ךְ פָּקַ֤ד עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ בַּת־אֱד֔וֹם גִּלָּ֖ה עַל־חַטֹּאתָֽיִךְ׃{פ}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
You have been fully chastised for your sins, city of *Tzion.* He will never exile you again. He remembers your sins, city of Edom, your iniquity is exposed.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The punishment of thy iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Żiyyon; he will no more carry thee away into exile: he will visit thy iniquity, O daughter of Edom; he will uncover thy sins.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Your transgression is ended, O daughter of Zion [i.e., you have been punished for all of your sins]; He will exile you no more — He has remembered your transgression, O daughter of Edom; He has bared all of your sins [(for punishment)].



## Chapter 5

###### Lamentations 5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:1)


זְכֹ֤ר יְהֹוָה֙ מֶֽה־הָ֣יָה לָ֔נוּ (הביט) [הַבִּ֖יטָה] וּרְאֵ֥ה אֶת־חֶרְפָּתֵֽנוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
God, remember what happened to us; look, take note of our degradation.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Remember, O Lord, what is come upon us: consider, and behold our insult.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Remember, O L-rd, what has become of us. Look, and behold our shame.


###### Lamentations 5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:2)


נַחֲלָתֵ֙נוּ֙ נֶֽהֶפְכָ֣ה לְזָרִ֔ים בָּתֵּ֖ינוּ לְנׇכְרִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Our heritage was subverted to strangers, our homes to foreigners.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Our inheritance is turned over to strangers, our houses to aliens.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Our inheritance has been overturned by foreigners; our houses, by strangers.


###### Lamentations 5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:3)


יְתוֹמִ֤ים הָיִ֙ינוּ֙ (אין) [וְאֵ֣ין] אָ֔ב אִמֹּתֵ֖ינוּ כְּאַלְמָנֽוֹת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
We have been orphaned, there is no father, our mothers are as widows.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
We are become orphans and fatherless, our mothers are like widows.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
We are as orphans, without a father; our mothers, as widows.


###### Lamentations 5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:4)


מֵימֵ֙ינוּ֙ בְּכֶ֣סֶף שָׁתִ֔ינוּ עֵצֵ֖ינוּ בִּמְחִ֥יר יָבֹֽאוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
We pay to drink our own water, our wood is acquired for a price.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
We have drunk our water for money; our own wood is sold to us.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[(Fearing to draw water from the river lest we be attacked by our foes,)] we drank our water for money [i.e., we bought it from them]; our wood was sold to us.


###### Lamentations 5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:5)


עַ֤ל צַוָּארֵ֙נוּ֙ נִרְדָּ֔פְנוּ יָגַ֖עְנוּ (לא) [וְלֹ֥א] הֽוּנַֽח־לָֽנוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
We are hounded around our necks, we exhaust ourselves, but nothing remains for us.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
We are pursued to our necks: we labour, and have no rest.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
We were pursued [with the yoke of hard labor] on our necks. We wearied ourselves [(to earn something)], but it [(what we earned)] was not left with us [(but exacted in taxes)].


###### Lamentations 5:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:6)


מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ נָתַ֣נּוּ יָ֔ד אַשּׁ֖וּר לִשְׂבֹּ֥עַֽ לָֽחֶם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
We extended a hand toward Egypt [for assistance,] toward Ashur, to satiate us with bread.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
We have given the hand to Miżrayim, and to Ashshur, to be satisfied with bread.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[To] Egypt we stretched out a hand [(to support ourselves on them)]; [to] Ashur, to be sated with [their] bread.


###### Lamentations 5:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:7)


אֲבֹתֵ֤ינוּ חָֽטְאוּ֙ (אינם) [וְאֵינָ֔ם] (אנחנו) [וַאֲנַ֖חְנוּ] עֲוֺנֹתֵיהֶ֥ם סָבָֽלְנוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Our forefathers sinned, and are no longer—we must bear the burden of their transgressions.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Our fathers have sinned, and are no more; but we bear their iniquities.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Our fathers sinned and are no more, and we have borne their sins.


###### Lamentations 5:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:8)


עֲבָדִים֙ מָ֣שְׁלוּ בָ֔נוּ פֹּרֵ֖ק אֵ֥ין מִיָּדָֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Slaves rule over us, and there is no redeemer from their clutches.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Servants rule over us: there is none to deliver us out of their hand.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Slaves ruled over us; there is no redeemer from their hand.


###### Lamentations 5:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:9)


בְּנַפְשֵׁ֙נוּ֙ נָבִ֣יא לַחְמֵ֔נוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י חֶ֥רֶב הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
We gain our bread at the risk of our lives, from the sword of the wilderness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
We get our bread with the peril of our lives because of the sword of the wilderness.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
At [the risk of] our lives we brought our bread, because of the sword of [marauders in] the wilderness.


###### Lamentations 5:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:10)


עוֹרֵ֙נוּ֙ כְּתַנּ֣וּר נִכְמָ֔רוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י זַלְעֲפ֥וֹת רָעָֽב׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Our skin is inflamed like a furnace, from burning hunger.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Our skin is hot like an oven because of the burning famine.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Our skin as [(in)] an oven was parched, because of the burning famine.


###### Lamentations 5:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:11)


נָשִׁים֙ בְּצִיּ֣וֹן עִנּ֔וּ בְּתֻלֹ֖ת בְּעָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Matrons were ravished in *Tzion,* maidens in the cities of *Yehudah.*


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Women are ravished in Żiyyon, and maidens in the cities of Yehuda.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Women in Zion they ravished; virgins in the cities of Judah.


###### Lamentations 5:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:12)


שָׂרִים֙ בְּיָדָ֣ם נִתְל֔וּ פְּנֵ֥י זְקֵנִ֖ים לֹ֥א נֶהְדָּֽרוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Noblemen were hung by the hands, elders were accorded no reverence.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Princes are hanged up by their hand: the faces of elders are not honoured.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Princes they hanged by their hands; they showed no deference for elders.


###### Lamentations 5:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:13)


בַּחוּרִים֙ טְח֣וֹן נָשָׂ֔אוּ וּנְעָרִ֖ים בָּעֵ֥ץ כָּשָֽׁלוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Youths were encumbered with millstones, boys staggered with beams.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Young men drag the millstone, and youths stumble under the wood.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Young men carried millstones [(on their shoulders to weary them when they were being led in chains)]; youths were weakened by [burdens of] wood.


###### Lamentations 5:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:14)


זְקֵנִים֙ מִשַּׁ֣עַר שָׁבָ֔תוּ בַּחוּרִ֖ים מִנְּגִינָתָֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The elders vanished from the gates of justice, young men from their halls of song.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The elders have ceased from the gate, the young men from their music.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Elders have ceased from the gate; young men from their song.


###### Lamentations 5:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:15)


שָׁבַת֙ מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ לִבֵּ֔נוּ נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ לְאֵ֖בֶל מְחֹלֵֽנוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Joy has disappeared from our hearts, our dance has turned to grief.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The joy of our heart is ceased; our dance is turned into mourning.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The joy of our heart has ceased; our dance turned to mourning.


###### Lamentations 5:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:16)


נָֽפְלָה֙ עֲטֶ֣רֶת רֹאשֵׁ֔נוּ אֽוֹי־נָ֥א לָ֖נוּ כִּ֥י חָטָֽאנוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The crown of our heads has fallen. Woe to us, for we have sinned.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The crown is fallen from our head: woe to us, that we have sinned!


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The crown of our head is fallen — Woe unto us, for we have sinned!


###### Lamentations 5:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:17)


עַל־זֶ֗ה הָיָ֤ה דָוֶה֙ לִבֵּ֔נוּ עַל־אֵ֖לֶּה חָשְׁכ֥וּ עֵינֵֽינוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For this our hearts ached, over these, our eyes were dulled—


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For this our heart is faint; for these things our eyes are dim.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For this [(what follows)] our heart was afflicted; for these our eyes were darkened:


###### Lamentations 5:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:18)


עַ֤ל הַר־צִיּוֹן֙ שֶׁשָּׁמֵ֔ם שׁוּעָלִ֖ים הִלְּכוּ־בֽוֹ׃{פ}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Over Mount *Tzion* which was devastated, foxes meandered across it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Because of the mountain of Żiyyon, which is desolate, foxes prowl over it.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For Mount Zion, which is desolate; foxes prowl on it.


###### Lamentations 5:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:19)


אַתָּ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תֵּשֵׁ֔ב כִּסְאֲךָ֖ לְד֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Adonoy, You shall endure for all eternity, Your throne throughout the generations;


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou, O Lord, art enthroned forever; Thy throne is from generation to generation.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[But] You, O L-rd, forever shall preside; Your throne, from generation to generation.


###### Lamentations 5:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:20)


לָ֤מָּה לָנֶ֙צַח֙ תִּשְׁכָּחֵ֔נוּ תַּֽעַזְבֵ֖נוּ לְאֹ֥רֶךְ יָמִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Why, then, O Eternal, do You forget us, abandon us through lengthy days?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Why dost Thou forget us forever, why dost Thou so long forsake us?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Why [then] should You forget us eternally, forsake us everlastingly? [(Did You not swear to us [to preserve us] by Your everlasting Presence?)]


###### Lamentations 5:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:21)


הֲשִׁיבֵ֨נוּ יְהֹוָ֤ה׀אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ (ונשוב) [וְֽנָשׁ֔וּבָה] חַדֵּ֥שׁ יָמֵ֖ינוּ כְּקֶֽדֶם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Adonoy, return us to You then we shall repent. Rejuvenate our days as in early times.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Turn us to Thee, O Lord, and we shall be turned; renew our days as of old:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Return us, O L-rd, to You, and we shall return; renew our days as of yore.


###### Lamentations 5:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Lamentations/r/5:22)


כִּ֚י אִם־מָאֹ֣ס מְאַסְתָּ֔נוּ קָצַ֥פְתָּ עָלֵ֖ינוּ עַד־מְאֹֽד׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For, although You may have considered us contemptible, You have already vented the utmost fury against us. (Adonoy, God, return us to You, then we shall repent. Rejuvenate our days as in early times.)


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
unless Thou hast utterly rejected us; and art exceedingly angry against us.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For though You have deeply despised us [for our sins], You were overly wrathful with us.

# Ecclesiastes

קהלת

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes)

חקירת משמעות החיים באמצעות בחינת המוות, הבטלה והתכלית.

An exploration of the meaning of life, reckoning with death, futility, and purpose.

Sections: Chapter-Verse

Location: Tanakh/Writings

## Chapter 1

###### Ecclesiastes 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:1)


דִּבְרֵי֙ קֹהֶ֣לֶת בֶּן־דָּוִ֔ד מֶ֖לֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The words of Koheles, the son of Dovid, king in Jerusalem.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The words of Qohelet, the son of David, king in Yerushalayim.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The words of [reproof of] Koheleth [(Solomon, who gathered [kihel] many wisdoms)], the son of David, who reigned in Jerusalem [(the city of wisdom)].


###### Ecclesiastes 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:2)


הֲבֵ֤ל הֲבָלִים֙ אָמַ֣ר קֹהֶ֔לֶת הֲבֵ֥ל הֲבָלִ֖ים הַכֹּ֥ל הָֽבֶל׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Vanity of vanities, said Koheles; vanity of vanities, all is vanity.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Vanity of vanities, says Qohelet, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The vanity (1) of the vanities (2) [of the seven days of creation (Seven "vanities" are intimated in this verse)], said Koheleth — the vanity (1) of the vanities (2) [is that] all is vanity (1, all together 7).


###### Ecclesiastes 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:3)


מַה־יִּתְר֖וֹן לָֽאָדָ֑ם בְּכׇ֨ל־עֲמָל֔וֹ שֶֽׁיַּעֲמֹ֖ל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
What profit does man have for all his labor which he labors beneath the sun.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
What profit has a man of all his labour wherein he labours under the sun?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
What profit is there to a man in all of the toil that he toils in exchange for the sun [(i.e., for the light of Torah)]?


###### Ecclesiastes 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:4)


דּ֤וֹר הֹלֵךְ֙ וְד֣וֹר בָּ֔א וְהָאָ֖רֶץ לְעוֹלָ֥ם עֹמָֽדֶת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
A generation passes away and [another] generation comes, and the earth abides forever.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
One generation passes away, and another generation comes: but the earth abides for ever.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A generation goes and a generation comes [(and a succeeding generation will recover from the sons of the "toiler" whatever he exacted unscrupulously by his toil)], but [the humble one, who lowers himself to] the earth endures forever.


###### Ecclesiastes 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:5)


וְזָרַ֥ח הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וּבָ֣א הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְאֶ֨ל־מְקוֹמ֔וֹ שׁוֹאֵ֛ף זוֹרֵ֥חַֽ ה֖וּא שָֽׁם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The sun rises and the sun sets, and to its place it strives, to rise there [again].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hastens to its place where it rises again.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
["A generation goes and a generation comes"] as the sun rises [in the morning] and the sun sets [in the evening], aspiring [to return] to its place whence it rose.


###### Ecclesiastes 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:6)


הוֹלֵךְ֙ אֶל־דָּר֔וֹם וְסוֹבֵ֖ב אֶל־צָפ֑וֹן סוֹבֵ֤ב׀סֹבֵב֙ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ הָר֔וּחַ וְעַל־סְבִיבֹתָ֖יו שָׁ֥ב הָרֽוּחַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
It [the wind] goes toward the south, and turns about toward the north; round and round goes the wind, and upon its circuits, the wind returns.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The wind goes towards the south, and veers to the north; round and round goes the wind, and on its circuits the wind returns.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
It goes to the south [(of the world in the daytime)] and turns to the north [(at night)]. Round and round [(the eastern and western sides)], the circuit goes, and [on the morrow], the circuit [of the previous day] is retraced. [(And thus with the wicked: Though their sun rises, it is destined to set, and the wicked are destined to return to the place of putridity whence they arose.)]


###### Ecclesiastes 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:7)


כׇּל־הַנְּחָלִים֙ הֹלְכִ֣ים אֶל־הַיָּ֔ם וְהַיָּ֖ם אֵינֶ֣נּוּ מָלֵ֑א אֶל־מְק֗וֹם שֶׁ֤הַנְּחָלִים֙ הֹֽלְכִ֔ים שָׁ֛ם הֵ֥ם שָׁבִ֖ים לָלָֽכֶת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea is not full; to the place where the rivers flow, there they continue to flow.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea is not full; to the place where the rivers flow, thither they return.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All the rivers go to the sea, and the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers go, there [i.e., downwards] they return to go. [And thus with the wicked (viz. 6 above)]


###### Ecclesiastes 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:8)


כׇּל־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים יְגֵעִ֔ים לֹא־יוּכַ֥ל אִ֖ישׁ לְדַבֵּ֑ר לֹא־תִשְׂבַּ֥ע עַ֙יִן֙ לִרְא֔וֹת וְלֹא־תִמָּלֵ֥א אֹ֖זֶן מִשְּׁמֹֽעַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
All things lead to weariness, man cannot speak of them; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All things are full of weariness; man cannot utter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[(a reversion to verse 3)] All words [of "toil"] are wearying; a man cannot speak [all of them]. The eye is not sated with seeing. The ear is not filled with hearing.


###### Ecclesiastes 1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:9)


מַה־שֶּֽׁהָיָה֙ ה֣וּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֔ה וּמַה־שֶּׁנַּֽעֲשָׂ֔ה ה֖וּא שֶׁיֵּעָשֶׂ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין כׇּל־חָדָ֖שׁ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
That which has been is what will be, and that which has been done is that which will be done; and there is nothing new under the sun.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
That which has been, it is that which shall be; and that which has been done is that which shall be done: and there is nothing new under the sun.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[Torah words bring new insights, whereas in the realm of what is exchanged for Torah] — that which was [(in the seven days of creation)], that is what shall be; and that which was done, that is what shall be done, and there is nothing new in exchange for the sun [(of Torah)].


###### Ecclesiastes 1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:10)


יֵ֥שׁ דָּבָ֛ר שֶׁיֹּאמַ֥ר רְאֵה־זֶ֖ה חָדָ֣שׁ ה֑וּא כְּבָר֙ הָיָ֣ה לְעֹֽלָמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה מִלְּפָנֵֽנוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Sometimes there is a thing of which one will exclaim: “See this is new!”; it has already been in existence in the ages which preceded us.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Is there a thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new; but it has already been in the ages before us.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
There is a thing [(in the world)] of which one might say: See, this is new. But, [the truth is that] it had already been of yore, in what had come before us.


###### Ecclesiastes 1:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:11)


אֵ֥ין זִכְר֖וֹן לָרִאשֹׁנִ֑ים וְגַ֨ם לָאַחֲרֹנִ֜ים שֶׁיִּהְי֗וּ לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ זִכָּר֔וֹן עִ֥ם שֶׁיִּהְי֖וּ לָאַחֲרֹנָֽה׃{פ}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
There is no remembrance of earlier generations; also of the later generations that are to come, there will be no remembrance of them among those who will come after.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
There is no remembrance of former things; nor will there be any remembrance of things that are to come among those who shall come after.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For there is no remembrance of the first ones, [i.e., the earlier generations, for which reason the thing seems to be new]; and the later ones, too, who will be [after us], will not be remembered by those who come after them.


###### Ecclesiastes 1:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:12)


אֲנִ֣י קֹהֶ֗לֶת הָיִ֥יתִי מֶ֛לֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I, Koheles, have been king over Israel in Jerusalem.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I Qohelet was king over Yisra᾽el in Yerushalayim.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I, Koheleth, was king [(over all the world, and then, only] over Israel, [and then, only] in Jerusalem.


###### Ecclesiastes 1:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:13)


וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת־לִבִּ֗י לִדְר֤וֹשׁ וְלָתוּר֙ בַּֽחׇכְמָ֔ה עַ֛ל כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם ה֣וּא**׀** עִנְיַ֣ן רָ֗ע נָתַ֧ן אֱלֹהִ֛ים לִבְנֵ֥י הָאָדָ֖ם לַעֲנ֥וֹת בּֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And I applied my heart to search and explore with wisdom, concerning all that happens beneath the heavens; it is an evil thing that God has given to mankind to be afflicted with.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all things that are done under the heaven: it is a sore task that God has given to the sons of man to be exercised with.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I set my heart to seek out and ponder with wisdom [i.e., Torah] everything [evil] that is done under the sun, [and I understood that it is a function of] the [freedom for] evil conduct placed by G-d before the sons of men to conduct themselves by [viz. Deuteronomy 13:15].


###### Ecclesiastes 1:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:14)


רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־כׇּל־הַֽמַּעֲשִׂ֔ים שֶֽׁנַּעֲשׂ֖וּ תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַכֹּ֛ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I have seen all the deeds that were done under the sun; and, behold, all is vanity and vexation of spirit.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all is vanity and a striving after wind.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I saw all the deeds done under the sun, and, behold, they are all vanity and breaking of spirit.


###### Ecclesiastes 1:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:15)


מְעֻוָּ֖ת לֹא־יוּכַ֣ל לִתְקֹ֑ן וְחֶסְר֖וֹן לֹא־יוּכַ֥ל לְהִמָּנֽוֹת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
That which is crooked, cannot be made straight; and that which is wanting, cannot be counted.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
That which is crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The crooked [deed] cannot be corrected [after one's death], and the [one who is] lacking [(from the number of the righteous)] cannot be counted [(with them for the receiving of reward)].


###### Ecclesiastes 1:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:16)


דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי אֲנִ֤י עִם־לִבִּי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אֲנִ֗י הִנֵּ֨ה הִגְדַּ֤לְתִּי וְהוֹסַ֙פְתִּי֙ חׇכְמָ֔ה עַ֛ל כׇּל־אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה לְפָנַ֖י עַל־יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְלִבִּ֛י רָאָ֥ה הַרְבֵּ֖ה חׇכְמָ֥ה וָדָֽעַת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I said to myself: “Behold, I have grown and increased in wisdom over all who were before me in Jerusalem; and my heart has perceived much wisdom and knowledge.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I spoke to my own heart, saying, See, I have acquired great wisdom, surpassing all those who were before me in Yerushalayim: for my heart has seen much of wisdom and knowledge.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[Now, that I have fallen from my greatness,] I commune in my heart: [Who would have thought that I would come to this pass,] I, who had amassed and increased wisdom over all who were before me in Jerusalem, and whose heart had seen [so] much wisdom and knowledge!


###### Ecclesiastes 1:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:17)


וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת חׇכְמָ֔ה וְדַ֥עַת הוֹלֵלֹ֖ת וְשִׂכְל֑וּת יָדַ֕עְתִּי שֶׁגַּם־זֶ֥ה ה֖וּא רַעְי֥וֹן רֽוּחַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly; I understand that this, too, was vexation of the spirit.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also was a striving after wind.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I set my heart on knowing [the nature of] wisdom [i.e., its end] and [the nature of] distraction and folly, and I found that this [i.e., wisdom], too, is breaking of spirit.


###### Ecclesiastes 1:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/1:18)


כִּ֛י בְּרֹ֥ב חׇכְמָ֖ה רׇב־כָּ֑עַס וְיוֹסִ֥יף דַּ֖עַת יוֹסִ֥יף מַכְאֽוֹב׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For with much wisdom, there is much vexation; and he who increases knowledge increases pain.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increases knowledge increases sorrow.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For in much wisdom [i.e., when one relies too much on his own wisdom, he is bound to sin and to cause] much anger [to the L-rd], and the increaser of knowledge increases sorrow.



## Chapter 2

###### Ecclesiastes 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:1)


אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י לְכָה־נָּ֛א אֲנַסְּכָ֥ה בְשִׂמְחָ֖ה וּרְאֵ֣ה בְט֑וֹב וְהִנֵּ֥ה גַם־ה֖וּא הָֽבֶל׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I said to myself, “Come now, I will try [the life of] joy, and enjoy the good life”; and behold, this too was vanity.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I said in my heart, Come now, I will try thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also was vanity.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I said to myself: Come, then, I will [forbear from wisdom and constantly] mix [wine] with joy, and see good; and, behold, this, too, is vanity [(for I saw prophetically that indulging in joy leads to many evils)].


###### Ecclesiastes 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:2)


לִשְׂח֖וֹק אָמַ֣רְתִּי מְהוֹלָ֑ל וּלְשִׂמְחָ֖ה מַה־זֹּ֥ה עֹשָֽׂה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Of laughter, I said, it is senseless; and of joy—what does it accomplish.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I said of laughter, It is mad: and of mirth, What does it achieve?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Of laughter I said: It is commingled [with tears and sighing], and of joy: What [good] does it do?


###### Ecclesiastes 2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:3)


תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י לִמְשׁ֥וֹךְ בַּיַּ֖יִן אֶת־בְּשָׂרִ֑י וְלִבִּ֞י נֹהֵ֤ג בַּֽחׇכְמָה֙ וְלֶאֱחֹ֣ז בְּסִכְל֔וּת עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר־אֶרְאֶ֗ה אֵי־זֶ֨ה ט֜וֹב לִבְנֵ֤י הָאָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַעֲשׂוּ֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם מִסְפַּ֖ר יְמֵ֥י חַיֵּיהֶֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I searched in my heart [for a way] to pamper my flesh with wine; while my heart conducted itself with wisdom, and to grasp foolishness, until I could see which was best for men to do under the heavens during the brief span of their lives.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I sought in my heart to stimulate my body with wine (yet guiding my heart with wisdom;) and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what was good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I [then] sought in my heart [to combine all of them] — to indulge my flesh in [feasts of] wine while my heart conducted (itself) with wisdom, and to hold on to "folly" [(those mitzvoth e.g., sha'atnez and the like] that my reason could not fathom)], until I saw which was good for the sons of man to do under the heavens the number of the days of their lives.


###### Ecclesiastes 2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:4)


הִגְדַּ֖לְתִּי מַעֲשָׂ֑י בָּנִ֤יתִי לִי֙ בָּתִּ֔ים נָטַ֥עְתִּי לִ֖י כְּרָמִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I made great works; I built houses for myself, I planted vineyards for myself.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I made great works for myself; I built houses; I planted vineyards:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I increased my works [(in the days of my greatness)]. I built me houses; I planted me vineyards.


###### Ecclesiastes 2:5

###### Ecclesiastes 2:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:24)


אֵֽין־ט֤וֹב בָּאָדָם֙ שֶׁיֹּאכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֔ה וְהֶרְאָ֧ה אֶת־נַפְשׁ֛וֹ ט֖וֹב בַּעֲמָל֑וֹ גַּם־זֹה֙ רָאִ֣יתִי אָ֔נִי כִּ֛י מִיַּ֥ד הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Is it not beneficial for man that he eats and drinks, and shows himself content with his labor? —this, too, I saw, that it is from the hand of God.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
There is nothing better for a man, than that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour; but this also I saw, that it was from the hand of God.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Is it not good in a man that he eat and drink and show his soul [inclined to] good in his toil? [viz. Jeremiah 2:15] This [inclination], too, have I seen to be from the hand of G-d.


###### Ecclesiastes 2:25

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:25](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:25)


כִּ֣י מִ֥י יֹאכַ֛ל וּמִ֥י יָח֖וּשׁ ח֥וּץ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For who should eat and who should enjoy, if not I?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For who can eat, or who can enjoy pleasure, more than I?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[And the wicked ones (who will leave their toil to others) say: Why should I not rejoice in the fruits of my toil?] For who should eat and who should hasten [to swallow] aside from me?


###### Ecclesiastes 2:26

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:26](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/2:26)


כִּ֤י לְאָדָם֙ שֶׁטּ֣וֹב לְפָנָ֔יו נָתַ֛ן חׇכְמָ֥ה וְדַ֖עַת וְשִׂמְחָ֑ה וְלַחוֹטֶא֩ נָתַ֨ן עִנְיָ֜ן לֶאֱסֹ֣ף וְלִכְנ֗וֹס לָתֵת֙ לְטוֹב֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים גַּם־זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For to the man who is good in His sight, He gives wisdom, knowledge and joy; but to the sinner, He gives the urge to gather and accumulate—that he should [ultimately] hand it [on to him] who is good in the sight of God; this, too, is vanity and vexation of spirit.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Surely he gives to a man that is good in his sight, wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and heaping up, that he may give it to one who is good before God. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For to the man who is good before Him, He has given [(viz. 2:24)] wisdom, and knowledge, and joy [i.e., a heart to occupy himself with Torah and mitzvoth and to rejoice in his lot with food and drink and clean garments]; and to the sinner He has given preoccupation with the amassing and the gathering [of wealth] — to give (it) to him who is good before G-d [viz. Esther 8:2]. This, too, [(one man toiling; the other, taking)] is vanity [(i.e., one of the vanities placed before men)] and breaking of spirit.



## Chapter 3

###### Ecclesiastes 3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:1)


לַכֹּ֖ל זְמָ֑ן וְעֵ֥ת לְכׇל־חֵ֖פֶץ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For everything there is a season and there is a time for everything under the sky:


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
To everything there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For all there is a season, and there is a time for every thing under the heavens.


###### Ecclesiastes 3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:2)


עֵ֥ת לָלֶ֖דֶתוְעֵ֣ת לָמ֑וּתעֵ֣ת לָטַ֔עַתוְעֵ֖ת לַעֲק֥וֹר נָטֽוּעַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
A time to be born and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to uproot the planted.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
There is a time to be born [(nine months)] and a time to die [(the allotted years for each generation)]. A time to plant [(nation and kingdom)] and a time to uproot what has been planted.


###### Ecclesiastes 3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:3)


עֵ֤ת לַהֲרוֹג֙וְעֵ֣ת לִרְפּ֔וֹאעֵ֥ת לִפְר֖וֹץוְעֵ֥ת לִבְנֽוֹת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
A time to kill and a time to heal; a time to wreck and a time to build.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A time to kill [(an entire people, e.g., Isaiah 14:30)], and a time to heal [that "killing," viz. Ibid. 19:22]. A time to breach [(the wall of the city, viz. Nechemiah 1:3)], and a time to build [viz. Amos 9:11].


###### Ecclesiastes 3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:4)


עֵ֤ת לִבְכּוֹת֙וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂח֔וֹקעֵ֥ת סְפ֖וֹדוְעֵ֥ת רְקֽוֹד׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
A time to weep and a time to laugh; a time to mourn and a time to dance.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A time to cry, [(on the ninth of Av)], and a time to laugh, [(in time to come, viz. Psalms 126:2)]. A time to mourn, [(in the days of mourning)], and a time to dance [(with grooms and brides)].


###### Ecclesiastes 3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:5)


עֵ֚ת לְהַשְׁלִ֣יךְ אֲבָנִ֔יםוְעֵ֖ת כְּנ֣וֹס אֲבָנִ֑יםעֵ֣ת לַחֲב֔וֹקוְעֵ֖ת לִרְחֹ֥ק מֵחַבֵּֽק׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A time to cast out "stones" [(the youths of Israel, cast out at the ruin of the Temple, viz. Eichah 4:1)] and a time to gather in "stones" [(from the exile, viz. Zechariah 9:16)]. A time to embrace [(viz. Jeremiah 13:11)], and a time to refrain from embracing [(viz. Isaiah 6:12)].


###### Ecclesiastes 3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:6)


עֵ֤ת לְבַקֵּשׁ֙וְעֵ֣ת לְאַבֵּ֔דעֵ֥ת לִשְׁמ֖וֹרוְעֵ֥ת לְהַשְׁלִֽיךְ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
A time to seek and a time to abandon; a time to preserve, and a time to discard.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A time to seek [(the outcasts of Israel, viz. Ezekiel 34:16)], and a time to cause [them] to go lost, [(in exile, viz. Leviticus 26:38)]. A time to keep [(i.e., to protect you, when you do His will, viz. Numbers 6:24)], and a time to cast away, viz. Deuteronomy 29:27)].


###### Ecclesiastes 3:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:7)


עֵ֤ת לִקְר֙וֹעַ֙וְעֵ֣ת לִתְפּ֔וֹרעֵ֥ת לַחֲשׁ֖וֹתוְעֵ֥ת לְדַבֵּֽר׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
A time to rip apart and a time to sew; a time to be silent and a time to speak.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
a time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A time to rend [(the kingdom of the house of David, viz. I Kings 14:8)], and a time to sew [together again, viz. Ezekiel 37:17]. A time to be silent [(and to receive reward for being so, viz. Leviticus 10:3)], and a time to speak [(viz. Exodus 15:1, Judges 51, Hosea 14:3)].


###### Ecclesiastes 3:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:8)


עֵ֤ת לֶֽאֱהֹב֙וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂנֹ֔אעֵ֥ת מִלְחָמָ֖הוְעֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם׃{ס}


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
A time to love and a time to hate; a time for war and a time for peace.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
a time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A time to love [viz. Deuteronomy 7:13], and a time to hate [viz. Hosea 9:15], a time for war and a time for peace.


###### Ecclesiastes 3:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:9)


מַה־יִּתְרוֹן֙ הָֽעוֹשֶׂ֔ה בַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר ה֥וּא עָמֵֽל׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
What benefit [then] has the worker from his labor?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
