What profit has the worker from his toil?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
What profit is there to the doer [of evil] in [all] that he toils? [(His time, too, will come, and all will go lost.)]


###### Ecclesiastes 3:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:10)


רָאִ֣יתִי אֶת־הָֽעִנְיָ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧ן אֱלֹהִ֛ים לִבְנֵ֥י הָאָדָ֖ם לַעֲנ֥וֹת בּֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I have seen the matter which God has given to man to be afflicted with.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I have seen the task, which God has given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I have seen the [mode of] conduct which G-d has given to the sons of men whereby to conduct themselves.


###### Ecclesiastes 3:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:11)


אֶת־הַכֹּ֥ל עָשָׂ֖ה יָפֶ֣ה בְעִתּ֑וֹ גַּ֤ם אֶת־הָעֹלָם֙ נָתַ֣ן בְּלִבָּ֔ם מִבְּלִ֞י אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹא־יִמְצָ֣א הָאָדָ֗ם אֶת־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים מֵרֹ֥אשׁ וְעַד־סֽוֹף׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He has made everything beautiful in its time; even [a sense of] the external world, He has set in their heart, yet man cannot discover the work that God has done from [the] beginning to the end.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He has made every thing beautiful in his time: also he has set the mystery of the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work which God has made from the beginning to the end.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He made everything beautiful in its time. [(A time of good is "beautiful" [i.e., appropriate] for the rewarding of a good deed, and a time of evil, for the punishment of an evil deed.)] Also, the [wisdom of the] world [lit., of what is hidden], [which] He placed in their heart, [He did not place there in its entirety, in the heart of each one], so that a man not find out the act that G-d had wrought [i.e., projected] from beginning to end. [(So that, not knowing the day of his death, man plans and builds and the world is perpetuated.)]


###### Ecclesiastes 3:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:12)


יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין ט֖וֹב בָּ֑ם כִּ֣י אִם־לִשְׂמ֔וֹחַ וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת ט֖וֹב בְּחַיָּֽיו׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I know there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and perform good deeds in his life.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I know that there is nothing better for them, than to rejoice, and to do good in his life:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I know [now, since the time of death is hidden,] that there is nothing better for them than for (each one) to rejoice [in his lot] and to do what is good [in the eyes of the L-rd] in his lifetime.


###### Ecclesiastes 3:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:13)


וְגַ֤ם כׇּל־הָאָדָם֙ שֶׁיֹּאכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֔ה וְרָאָ֥ה ט֖וֹב בְּכׇל־עֲמָל֑וֹ מַתַּ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And also, when every man eats and drinks, and enjoys the good of all his labors, that is the gift of God.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
also that it is the gift of God that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And also, every man who eats and drinks and sees good [(Torah and mitzvoth)] in all of his toil, this is a gift of G-d.


###### Ecclesiastes 3:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:14)


יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּ֠י כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה הָאֱלֹהִים֙ ה֚וּא יִהְיֶ֣ה לְעוֹלָ֔ם עָלָיו֙ אֵ֣ין לְהוֹסִ֔יף וּמִמֶּ֖נּוּ אֵ֣ין לִגְרֹ֑עַ וְהָאֱלֹהִ֣ים עָשָׂ֔ה שֶׁיִּֽרְא֖וּ מִלְּפָנָֽיו׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I know that whatever God does will endure forever, nothing can be added to it, nor anything be diminished from it; God has so made it that man should fear before Him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I know that, whatever God does, it shall be forever: nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it: and God does it, so that men should fear before him.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I know that everything made by G-d [(in the creation)] is fit to endure [as is] forever, not to be added to or diminished; and [on those rare occasions when] G-d wrought [changes in the natural order, it was] so that men fear Him. [(This, then — doing mitzvoth and fearing G-d — should be the end of man.)]


###### Ecclesiastes 3:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:15)


מַה־שֶּֽׁהָיָה֙ כְּבָ֣ר ה֔וּא וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לִהְי֖וֹת כְּבָ֣ר הָיָ֑ה וְהָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־נִרְדָּֽף׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
That which already was, exists now, and that which is to be, has already been; and God seeks the pursued.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
That which is, already has been; and that which is to be has already been; and only God can find the fleeting moment.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
What happened [(before us)] has already taken place [and is known to us], and what is to come will be [consistent with] what has already been, [(the L-rd not changing in His tributes)] — G-d seeks out [the cause of] the pursued one [(to punish the pursuer. What profit, then, can accrue to him who toils for wrongful gain?)]


###### Ecclesiastes 3:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:16)


וְע֥וֹד רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ מְק֤וֹם הַמִּשְׁפָּט֙ שָׁ֣מָּה הָרֶ֔שַׁע וּמְק֥וֹם הַצֶּ֖דֶק שָׁ֥מָּה הָרָֽשַׁע׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And, furthermore, I have seen under the sun: in the place of justice there was wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there was wickedness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And moreover I saw under the sun in the place of judgment, that wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, that iniquity was there.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I have further seen [(by the Holy Spirit)] that in the place of justice [(the chamber of hewn stone in Jerusalem, viz. Isaiah 1:21, the seat of Sanhedrin)], there will wickedness be adjudicated [viz. Michah 3:11], and in the place of righteousness [(the middle gate, where halachoth were formulated)], there will [the counsels of] wickedness [be seated].


###### Ecclesiastes 3:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:17)


אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י אֶת־הַצַּדִּיק֙ וְאֶת־הָ֣רָשָׁ֔ע יִשְׁפֹּ֖ט הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּי־עֵ֣ת לְכׇל־חֵ֔פֶץ וְעַ֥ל כׇּל־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה שָֽׁם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I said to myself: “The righteous and the wicked God will judge; for there is a time for every desire, and for every deed—there.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I said in my heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[Therefore,] I say in my heart [(that all of these injustices will be redressed, for)] G-d will judge the righteous one and the wicked one. For there is a time for all things [(even for retribution)], and there [i.e., at that time, G-d will judge a man] for every deed [that he has done.]


###### Ecclesiastes 3:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:18)


אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י עַל־דִּבְרַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֔ם לְבָרָ֖ם הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְלִרְא֕וֹת שְׁהֶם־בְּהֵמָ֥ה הֵ֖מָּה לָהֶֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I said to myself: “Concerning the state of man, God has set them apart that they may see that they themselves are as beast.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I said in my heart, after the speech of the sons of men, that God has chosen them out, but only to see that they themselves are but as beasts;


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I said in my heart [(when I saw all this)] that G-d [has chosen] to apprise all those who assert lordship [over those beneath them that their power is naught)], and to show [them] that they [(and all potentates)] are as beasts unto themselves.


###### Ecclesiastes 3:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:19)


כִּי֩ מִקְרֶ֨ה בְֽנֵי־הָאָדָ֜ם וּמִקְרֶ֣ה הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה וּמִקְרֶ֤ה אֶחָד֙ לָהֶ֔ם כְּמ֥וֹת זֶה֙ כֵּ֣ן מ֣וֹת זֶ֔ה וְר֥וּחַ אֶחָ֖ד לַכֹּ֑ל וּמוֹתַ֨ר הָאָדָ֤ם מִן־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ אָ֔יִן כִּ֥י הַכֹּ֖ל הָֽבֶל׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For the fate of men and the fate of the beasts—the same fate befalls both, as one dies, so dies the other, the same breath is in all of them; and the superiority of man over beast is nil for all is vanity.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
that that which befalls the sons of men befalls the beasts; even one thing befalls them both: as the one dies, so the other dies; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man has no preeminence over a beast: for all is vanity.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For what befalls the sons of men and what befalls the beasts — one thing befalls them [both]! As one dies, so the other dies, and there is one spirit to all. And the superiority of man over beast [(in his lifetime)] is naught [i.e., unapparent, at his death], for all is vanity [(everything returning to dust)].


###### Ecclesiastes 3:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:20)


הַכֹּ֥ל הוֹלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־מָק֣וֹם אֶחָ֑ד הַכֹּל֙ הָיָ֣ה מִן־הֶֽעָפָ֔ר וְהַכֹּ֖ל שָׁ֥ב אֶל־הֶעָפָֽר׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
All go to one place; all come from the dust, and all return to the dust.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All go to one place; all are of the dust, and all return to dust.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All goes to one place. All came from the dust and all return to the dust.


###### Ecclesiastes 3:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:21)


מִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ ר֚וּחַ בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֔ם הָעֹלָ֥ה הִ֖יא לְמָ֑עְלָה וְר֙וּחַ֙ הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה הַיֹּרֶ֥דֶת הִ֖יא לְמַ֥טָּה לָאָֽרֶץ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Who knows the spirit of man, whether it rises upwards and the spirit of the beast whether it descends to the earth.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Who knows whether the spirit of man goes upwards, and the spirit of the beast goes downwards to the earth?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Who knows [i.e., Who impresses upon himself that it is the spirit of man that ascends on high [for judgment] and the spirit of the beast that descends below, to the earth [(free of all accounting, and that he should not conduct himself as a beast, which gives no thought to its acts)]?


###### Ecclesiastes 3:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/3:22)


וְרָאִ֗יתִי כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין טוֹב֙ מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׂמַ֤ח הָאָדָם֙ בְּֽמַעֲשָׂ֔יו כִּי־ה֖וּא חֶלְק֑וֹ כִּ֣י מִ֤י יְבִיאֶ֙נּוּ֙ לִרְא֔וֹת בְּמֶ֖ה שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָֽיו׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I perceived, therefore, that there is nothing better than man should rejoice in his work, for that is his lot; for who will bring him to see what will be after him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
So I saw that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his work; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I have seen [(through all these things)] that there is no good [(for a man)] than for a man to rejoice in his acts [(i.e., in the toil of his hands, and not to aspire to luxuries and superfluities)]; for it [(the toil of his hands)] is his portion [(given him by Heaven to rejoice in)]. For [(after his death)], who will bring him to see what will transpire [with his children] after him? [i.e., whether they will or will not prosper as he did with the wealth that he heaped up for them]



## Chapter 4

###### Ecclesiastes 4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:1)


וְשַׁ֣בְתִּֽי אֲנִ֗י וָאֶרְאֶה֙ אֶת־כׇּל־הָ֣עֲשֻׁקִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשִׂ֖ים תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְהִנֵּ֣ה**׀** דִּמְעַ֣ת הָעֲשֻׁקִ֗ים וְאֵ֤ין לָהֶם֙ מְנַחֵ֔ם וּמִיַּ֤ד עֹֽשְׁקֵיהֶם֙ כֹּ֔חַ וְאֵ֥ין לָהֶ֖ם מְנַחֵֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And I returned and considered all the oppressions that are committed under the sun; and behold, tears of the oppressed, with no one to comfort them, and from the hand of their oppressors [flows the] power—with no one to comfort them.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I again saw [(by the Holy Spirit)] all of those who are scourged [(in Gehinnom) for the deeds] which are done in exchange for the sun [of Torah]. And, behold, the tears of the oppressed, [(weeping for their souls, that are scourged by destructive angels, viz. Psalms 87:4)], and who have no consoler. And in the hand of their scourgers there is power [(which they cannot resist)]; and they have no consoler.


###### Ecclesiastes 4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:2)


וְשַׁבֵּ֧חַ אֲנִ֛י אֶת־הַמֵּתִ֖ים שֶׁכְּבָ֣ר מֵ֑תוּ מִן־הַ֣חַיִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥מָּה חַיִּ֖ים עֲדֶֽנָה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And so I praised the dead who already died; more than the living who are still alive.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
So I praised the dead that are already dead more than the living that are yet alive;


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I praise the dead, who have already died [(before the evil inclination could gain control of them and thrust them away from the L-rd)] more than the living who are still alive.


###### Ecclesiastes 4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:3)


וְטוֹב֙ מִשְּׁנֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־עֲדֶ֖ן לֹ֣א הָיָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־רָאָה֙ אֶת־הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה הָרָ֔ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And better than both of these is he who has not yet been born; who has not seen the evil deed that is committed under the sun.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
but better than both of them is he who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And better than both is he who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil deed which is done under the sun.


###### Ecclesiastes 4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:4)


וְרָאִ֨יתִֽי אֲנִ֜י אֶת־כׇּל־עָמָ֗ל וְאֵת֙ כׇּל־כִּשְׁר֣וֹן הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה כִּ֛י הִ֥יא קִנְאַת־אִ֖ישׁ מֵרֵעֵ֑הוּ גַּם־זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And I observed that all labor and all skillful work is the result of man’s envy of his neighbor; this, too, is vanity and vexation of spirit.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Again, I considered all labour, and every skill in work, that it comes from a man’s rivalry with his neighbour. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I saw all the "toil" [i.e., transgressions] and all the perfection of deed [(motivated not by fear of Heaven, but)] by the envy of one man for another — this, too, is vanity and breaking of spirit.


###### Ecclesiastes 4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:5)


הַכְּסִיל֙ חֹבֵ֣ק אֶת־יָדָ֔יו וְאֹכֵ֖ל אֶת־בְּשָׂרֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The fool folds his hands and eats his own flesh.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The fool folds his hands together, and eats his own flesh.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The fool [(the wicked one)] folds his hands [(in sloth and eats from theft)], and he "eats his flesh" [(on the day of judgment, witnessing the glory of the righteous and his own undoing)].


###### Ecclesiastes 4:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:6)


ט֕וֹב מְלֹ֥א כַ֖ף נָ֑חַת מִמְּלֹ֥א חׇפְנַ֛יִם עָמָ֖ל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Better is a handful [earned] in contentment; than two handfuls [earned] in labor and vexation of spirit.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Better is a handful with quietness, than both the hands full of labour and striving after wind.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Better a handful of gratification [(acquiring few possessions by one's labor, which pleases the Creator)] than two handfuls of toil and breaking of spirit [(acquiring many possessions by transgression and perverseness)].


###### Ecclesiastes 4:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:7)


וְשַׁ֧בְתִּי אֲנִ֛י וָאֶרְאֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And I returned and observed [another form of] vanity under the sun.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I again saw vanity under the sun.


###### Ecclesiastes 4:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:8)


יֵ֣שׁ אֶחָד֩ וְאֵ֨ין שֵׁנִ֜י גַּ֣ם בֵּ֧ן וָאָ֣ח אֵֽין־ל֗וֹ וְאֵ֥ין קֵץ֙ לְכׇל־עֲמָל֔וֹ גַּם־[עֵינ֖וֹ] (עיניו) לֹא־תִשְׂבַּ֣ע עֹ֑שֶׁר וּלְמִ֣י**׀** אֲנִ֣י עָמֵ֗ל וּמְחַסֵּ֤ר אֶת־נַפְשִׁי֙ מִטּוֹבָ֔ה גַּם־זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וְעִנְיַ֥ן רָ֖ע הֽוּא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
There is one who is alone, with none other beside him, he has neither son nor brother; yet there is no end to his labor, neither is his eye ever satisfied with riches; [nor does he ask himself] For whom do I labor and deprive myself of goodness? this too is vanity, and an evil matter.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
There is one alone, without a companion; yea, he has neither son nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches: he may say, For whom then do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This is also vanity; indeed, it is a sorry business.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
There is one [(who acts alone)] with no second. Neither a son [(a disciple)] nor a brother [(a companion)] has he; and there is no end to all his toil. His eye [i.e., his intellect], too, will not be sated with wealth [(learning)]. And for whom am I toiling and depriving my soul of good [(if I do not set up disciples)]? This, too, is vanity and ill conduct.


###### Ecclesiastes 4:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:9)


טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן־הָאֶחָ֑ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר יֵשׁ־לָהֶ֛ם שָׂכָ֥ר ט֖וֹב בַּעֲמָלָֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Two are better than one; because they receive a goodly reward for their work.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[(In all areas,)] better the two than the one, who have goodly reward of their toil.


###### Ecclesiastes 4:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:10)


כִּ֣י אִם־יִפֹּ֔לוּ הָאֶחָ֖ד יָקִ֣ים אֶת־חֲבֵר֑וֹ וְאִ֣יל֗וֹ הָֽאֶחָד֙ שֶׁיִּפּ֔וֹל וְאֵ֥ין שֵׁנִ֖י לַהֲקִימֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For if they fall, one will lift up the other; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and there is no one to lift him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falls; for he has not another to help him up.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For if they fall, the one will raise up his fellow; but woe to the one who falls and has no second to raise him.


###### Ecclesiastes 4:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:11)


גַּ֛ם אִם־יִשְׁכְּב֥וּ שְׁנַ֖יִם וְחַ֣ם לָהֶ֑ם וּלְאֶחָ֖ד אֵ֥יךְ יֵחָֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Also, if two lie together they can be warm; but how can one be warm alone?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth: but how can one be warm alone?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Also, if two lie down together, it is warm for them; but how shall one be warmed?


###### Ecclesiastes 4:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:12)


וְאִֽם־יִתְקְפוֹ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם יַעַמְד֣וּ נֶגְדּ֑וֹ וְהַחוּט֙ הַֽמְשֻׁלָּ֔שׁ לֹ֥א בִמְהֵרָ֖ה יִנָּתֵֽק׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And if an individual attacks, the two of them can stand against him; and the threefold cord is not quickly severed.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; but a threefold cord is not quickly broken.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if the one be attacked, the two will stand up against him; and [how much more so is] the three-fold cord not quickly sundered!


###### Ecclesiastes 4:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:13)


ט֛וֹב יֶ֥לֶד מִסְכֵּ֖ן וְחָכָ֑ם מִמֶּ֤לֶךְ זָקֵן֙ וּכְסִ֔יל אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־יָדַ֥ע לְהִזָּהֵ֖ר עֽוֹד׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Better a poor but wise child; than an old and foolish king, who no longer knows how to be vigilant.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who no longer knows how to take care of himself.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Better a child [(the good inclination, which asserts itself in a male at the age of thirteen)], poor [(the limbs not obeying it as they do the evil inclination)], and wise [(directing one to the way of good)], than a king [(the evil inclination, which rules over all the limbs)], old [(asserting itself from birth, viz. Genesis 4:7)] and foolish [(directing one to the way of evil)], which can no longer take heed [(having grown rooted in its ways)].


###### Ecclesiastes 4:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:14)


כִּֽי־מִבֵּ֥ית הָסוּרִ֖ים יָצָ֣א לִמְלֹ֑ךְ כִּ֛י גַּ֥ם בְּמַלְכוּת֖וֹ נוֹלַ֥ד רָֽשׁ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Even though he [the child] emerged from prison to be king; even though in his own kingdom he was born a pauper.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For out of prison one came forth to reign; whilst another in his royal power may become poor.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For [(in the end, men will say that)] from the prison-house has he [(the poor one)] gone forth to reign. [And it is, indeed, right that he do so,] for even in his reigning he assumes [i.e., invests himself with] humility.


###### Ecclesiastes 4:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:15)


רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־כׇּל־הַ֣חַיִּ֔ים הַֽמְהַלְּכִ֖ים תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ עִ֚ם הַיֶּ֣לֶד הַשֵּׁנִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד תַּחְתָּֽיו׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I observed that all the living that walk under the sun were supportive of the young successor who stepped into his place.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I saw all the living who wander under the sun – they were with the second child who was to rise up in his stead.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I have seen all the living who walk under the sun with the second child, which arises after him.


###### Ecclesiastes 4:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:16)


אֵֽין־קֵ֣ץ לְכׇל־הָעָ֗ם לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־הָיָה֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם גַּ֥ם הָאַחֲרוֹנִ֖ים לֹ֣א יִשְׂמְחוּ־ב֑וֹ כִּֽי־גַם־זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וְרַעְי֥וֹן רֽוּחַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
There was no limit to all the peoples, to all of them whom he lead; even though [it is so now] those who come after [the next generation] will not rejoice in him; for this, too, is vanity and vexation of spirit.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
There is no end of all the people who come to acclaim the one who goes before them: yet they who come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a striving after wind.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
There is no end to all the people, to all [the good] that was before them. The latter ones, too, will not rejoice in it. For this, too, is [the outcome of] vanity and breaking of spirit.


###### Ecclesiastes 4:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/4:17)


שְׁמֹ֣ר (רגליך) [רַגְלְךָ֗] כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר תֵּלֵךְ֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְקָר֣וֹב לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ מִתֵּ֥ת הַכְּסִילִ֖ים זָ֑בַח כִּֽי־אֵינָ֥ם יוֹדְעִ֖ים לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת רָֽע׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Guard your foot when you go to the House of God, come near and listen rather than offer sacrifices like the fools; for they do not know that they do evil.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God; to draw near to hearken is better than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Guard your feet when you go to the house of G-d [(that you bring the proper sacrifice there)]. And be close(r) to hear [(the word of G-d)] than to bring sacrifice as the fools do, [(sinning and sacrificing)]; for they know not that they do evil [thereby].



## Chapter 5

###### Ecclesiastes 5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:1)


אַל־תְּבַהֵ֨ל עַל־פִּ֜יךָ וְלִבְּךָ֧ אַל־יְמַהֵ֛ר לְהוֹצִ֥יא דָבָ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים בַּשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְאַתָּ֣ה עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ עַל־כֵּ֛ן יִהְי֥וּ דְבָרֶ֖יךָ מְעַטִּֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Do not be impulsive with your mouth, nor let your heart be hasty to utter a word before God; for God is in heaven and you are on earth, therefore, let your words be few.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thy heart be hasty to utter anything before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Be not rash with your mouth, and let your heart not be over-hasty to utter a thing against G-d; for G-d is in the heavens [i.e., omnipotent], and you are on the earth; therefore, let your words be few.


###### Ecclesiastes 5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:2)


כִּ֛י בָּ֥א הַחֲל֖וֹם בְּרֹ֣ב עִנְיָ֑ן וְק֥וֹל כְּסִ֖יל בְּרֹ֥ב דְּבָרִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For a dream comes with many subjects and the voice of a fool with many words.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For a dream comes through a multitude of business; and a fool’s voice is known by a multitude of words.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For a dream comes with much preoccupation [(with a particular thought in the daytime)], and the voice of a fool with a multitude of words [(wherefore I say: "Let your words be few.")]


###### Ecclesiastes 5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:3)


כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ תִּדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר לֵֽאלֹהִ֗ים אַל־תְּאַחֵר֙ לְשַׁלְּמ֔וֹ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין חֵ֖פֶץ בַּכְּסִילִ֑ים אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־תִּדֹּ֖ר שַׁלֵּֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
When you make an oath to God, do not delay in its fulfillment, for He has no desire in fools; whatever you vow, fulfill.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
When thou vowest a vow to God, do not defer to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
When you make a vow to G-d, do not delay to pay it, because there is no desire in fools [(i.e., He does not desire the wicked, who vow and do not pay.)] What you vow, pay.


###### Ecclesiastes 5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:4)


ט֖וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־תִדֹּ֑ר מִשֶּׁתִּדּ֖וֹר וְלֹ֥א תְשַׁלֵּֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
It is better that you not vow [at all] rather than vow and not fulfill.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Better is it that thou shouldst not vow, than that thou shouldst vow and not pay.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Better that you not vow than that you vow and not pay.


###### Ecclesiastes 5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:5)


אַל־תִּתֵּ֤ן אֶת־פִּ֙יךָ֙ לַחֲטִ֣יא אֶת־בְּשָׂרֶ֔ךָ וְאַל־תֹּאמַר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמַּלְאָ֔ךְ כִּ֥י שְׁגָגָ֖ה הִ֑יא לָ֣מָּה יִקְצֹ֤ף הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ עַל־קוֹלֶ֔ךָ וְחִבֵּ֖ל אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדֶֽיךָ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Do not permit your mouth to bring guilt on your flesh, nor say before the angel that it was an error; why should God be angered by your voice, and destroy the work of your hands.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Do not let thy mouth cause thy flesh to sin; nor say before the angel, that it was an error: why should God be angry at thy voice and destroy the work of thy hands?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not allow your mouth to bring sin upon your flesh [i.e., upon your children.] And do not say before the messenger [(who comes to claim the charity that you pledged in public)] that it [(your vowing)] was a mistake. Why should G-d be angry at [i.e., because of] your voice, and destroy the work of your hands [(the mitzvoth that you have already done)]?


###### Ecclesiastes 5:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:6)


כִּ֣י בְרֹ֤ב חֲלֹמוֹת֙ וַהֲבָלִ֔ים וּדְבָרִ֖ים הַרְבֵּ֑ה כִּ֥י אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְרָֽא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For in the multitude of dreams and vanities and in the multitude of words; man should fear God.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For this comes from the multitude of dreams and vanities and many words: but fear thou God.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For [(you should pay no heed)] to a multitude of dreams and vain [prophecies] and a multitude of words [(bidding you to depart from the L-rd)], but fear G-d.


###### Ecclesiastes 5:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:7)


אִם־עֹ֣שֶׁק רָ֠שׁ וְגֵ֨זֶל מִשְׁפָּ֤ט וָצֶ֙דֶק֙ תִּרְאֶ֣ה בַמְּדִינָ֔ה אַל־תִּתְמַ֖הּ עַל־הַחֵ֑פֶץ כִּ֣י גָבֹ֜הַּ מֵעַ֤ל גָּבֹ֙הַּ֙ שֹׁמֵ֔ר וּגְבֹהִ֖ים עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Oppression of the poor, perversion of justice and righteousness—should you observe these in the state—do not be astonished by the fact; for One higher than the high watches, and there are high ones above them.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and the violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, do not marvel at the matter: for there is a high one who watches over him that is high; and there are yet higher ones over them.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If oppression of the poor and miscarriage of justice and of righteousness you see in the land, do not wonder about the will [(of G-d when He brings evil upon the evildoers)]. For high upon high is the Watcher [(and He sees their deeds)], and there are those who are higher than they [(and who execute the L-rd's command to exact payment of them)]


###### Ecclesiastes 5:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:8)


וְיִתְר֥וֹן אֶ֖רֶץ בַּכֹּ֣ל (היא) [ה֑וּא] מֶ֥לֶךְ לְשָׂדֶ֖ה נֶעֱבָֽד׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The profit of the earth is desired by all; the king himself is subject to the soil.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Moreover, land has an advantage for everyone: he who tills a field is a king.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
and [(to exact payment)] of the lofty of the land [(who anger the L-rd)]. With every thing [at his command] he [(G-d's messenger) fulfills His embassy]. The King subserves Himself to the "field" [(of Zion) to exact payment of its shamers and to reward its builders].


###### Ecclesiastes 5:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:9)


אֹהֵ֥ב כֶּ֙סֶף֙ לֹא־יִשְׂבַּ֣ע כֶּ֔סֶף וּמִֽי־אֹהֵ֥ב בֶּהָמ֖וֹן לֹ֣א תְבוּאָ֑ה גַּם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He who loves money will never be satisfied with money, and he who loves abundance will have no produce; this too is vanity.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loves abundance with increase: this is also vanity.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The lover of silver [i.e., of mitzvoth] will not be sated with mitzvoth; and he who loves [mitzvoth] promiscuously [(without attaching special value to distinct mitzvoth)] will not [reap their] produce. This, too, is vanity.


###### Ecclesiastes 5:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:10)


בִּרְבוֹת֙ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה רַבּ֖וּ אוֹכְלֶ֑יהָ וּמַה־כִּשְׁרוֹן֙ לִבְעָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֖י אִם־[רְא֥וּת] (ראית) עֵינָֽיו׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
As goods increase so do those who consume them; and what advantage has the owner except beholding them with his eyes.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
When goods increase, they who eat them are increased: and what good is there to their owner, saving the beholding of them with his eyes?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
With the increase of good [i.e., when Israel improves its ways], their eaters [(of the reward of mitzvoth)] increase. And what benefit to their Master, but the seeing of His eyes [(i.e., His beholding of their allegiance to Him)]?


###### Ecclesiastes 5:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:11)


מְתוּקָה֙ שְׁנַ֣ת הָעֹבֵ֔ד אִם־מְעַ֥ט וְאִם־הַרְבֵּ֖ה יֹאכֵ֑ל וְהַשָּׂבָע֙ לֶֽעָשִׁ֔יר אֵינֶ֛נּוּ מַנִּ֥יחַֽ ל֖וֹ לִישֽׁוֹן׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Sweet is the sleep of the laborer, whether he eats little or much; but the satiety of the rich will not permit him to sleep.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the repletion of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Sweet is the sleep of the worker, whether he eat little or much, but the fullness [(of possessions)] of the rich man does not allow him to sleep [(in his anxiety over them)].


###### Ecclesiastes 5:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:12)


יֵ֚שׁ רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ עֹ֛שֶׁר שָׁמ֥וּר לִבְעָלָ֖יו לְרָעָתֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
There is a sickening evil [which] I have seen under the sun—wealth preserved by its owner to his own detriment.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
There is a sore evil which I have seen under the sun, namely, riches kept for their owner to his hurt.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
There is a sore evil that I have seen under the sun — wealth stored up for its owner, for his ill.


###### Ecclesiastes 5:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:13)


וְאָבַ֛ד הָעֹ֥שֶׁר הַה֖וּא בְּעִנְיַ֣ן רָ֑ע וְהוֹלִ֣יד בֵּ֔ן וְאֵ֥ין בְּיָד֖וֹ מְאֽוּמָה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And should he lose that wealth through some tragic mishap; and should a son be born to him—he will have nothing in his hand.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But those riches perish by evil adventure: and he begets a son, and there is nothing in his hand.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And that wealth is lost by ill conduct, and he begets a son with nothing in his hand [(not even the merit of the fathers.)]


###### Ecclesiastes 5:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:14)


כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר יָצָא֙ מִבֶּ֣טֶן אִמּ֔וֹ עָר֛וֹם יָשׁ֥וּב לָלֶ֖כֶת כְּשֶׁבָּ֑א וּמְא֙וּמָה֙ לֹא־יִשָּׂ֣א בַעֲמָל֔וֹ שֶׁיֹּלֵ֖ךְ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
As he came from his mother’s womb, naked will he return as he came; he will take nothing for his labor, [nothing] that he will carry in his hand.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
As he came forth from his mother’s womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and he shall take nothing for his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
As he emerged from his mother's womb, naked, so shall he return to go as he came; and [(when he dies)] nothing shall he bear of his toil, [(no merit of charity that he did with his wealth in his lifetime)], to take in his hand.


###### Ecclesiastes 5:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:15)


וְגַם־זֹה֙ רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה כׇּל־עֻמַּ֥ת שֶׁבָּ֖א כֵּ֣ן יֵלֵ֑ךְ וּמַה־יִּתְר֣וֹן ל֔וֹ שֶֽׁיַּעֲמֹ֖ל לָרֽוּחַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
This too is a sickening evil; as he came, so shall he depart; what profit did he gain that he toiled for the wind.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And this also is a sore evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit has he that labours for the wind?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And this, too, is a grievous evil. Just as it [(that wealth)] came, so shall it go. And what does it profit him that he works for the wind?


###### Ecclesiastes 5:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:16)


גַּ֥ם כׇּל־יָמָ֖יו בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ יֹאכֵ֑ל וְכָעַ֥ס הַרְבֵּ֖ה וְחׇלְי֥וֹ וָקָֽצֶף׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Also, all his days he eats in darkness; and he has much grief, illness and anger.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All his days also he eats in darkness, and he has much sorrow and sickness and wrath.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Also, all of his days shall he eat in darkness, and [know] much ire, and sickness, and wrath.


###### Ecclesiastes 5:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:17)


הִנֵּ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־רָאִ֣יתִי אָ֗נִי ט֣וֹב אֲשֶׁר־יָפֶ֣ה לֶֽאֱכוֹל־וְ֠לִשְׁתּ֠וֹת וְלִרְא֨וֹת טוֹבָ֜ה בְּכׇל־עֲמָל֣וֹ**׀** שֶׁיַּעֲמֹ֣ל תַּֽחַת־הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ מִסְפַּ֧ר יְמֵי־חַיָּ֛ו אֲשֶׁר־נָֽתַן־ל֥וֹ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־ה֥וּא חֶלְקֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Behold that which I have seen: it is good, even commendable for one to eat and drink and to enjoy the good of all his labor that he labors under the sun, during the counted days of his life that God has given him for that is his portion.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Behold that which I have seen: it is good and comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour in which he toils under the sun all the days of his life, which God gives him: for it is his portion.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Behold what I have seen to be good. It becomes one to eat and to drink and to see good [i.e., to occupy himself with Torah (and not to seek to amass great wealth, but to rejoice in what he has been given)], in all of his toil wherein he toils under the sun the number of the days of his life which G-d has given him; for this is his portion.


###### Ecclesiastes 5:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:18)


גַּ֣ם כׇּֽל־הָאָדָ֡ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָֽתַן־ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִים֩ עֹ֨שֶׁר וּנְכָסִ֜ים וְהִשְׁלִיט֨וֹ לֶאֱכֹ֤ל מִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ וְלָשֵׂ֣את אֶת־חֶלְק֔וֹ וְלִשְׂמֹ֖חַ בַּעֲמָל֑וֹ זֹ֕ה מַתַּ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Also, every man to whom God has given wealth and possession, and the power to enjoy them, to take his share and to rejoice in his labor; this is the gift of God.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this is the gift of God.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Also, every man to whom G-d has given wealth and possessions, and dominion to eat of it [in his lifetime] and to bear his portion [at his death (G-d enabling him to occupy himself with Torah and mitzvoth in his lifetime so as to receive eternal reward)], and to rejoice in his toil — this is the gift of G-d.


###### Ecclesiastes 5:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/5:19)


כִּ֚י לֹ֣א הַרְבֵּ֔ה יִזְכֹּ֖ר אֶת־יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֑יו כִּ֧י הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים מַעֲנֶ֖ה בְּשִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For they are not many, let him remember, the days of his life; while God answers [provides] him with the joy of his heart.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For he shall remember that the days of his life are not many, in which God provides him with the joy of his heart.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For not for long will he remember the [short] days of his life. [Why, then, should he exert himself to acquire wealth? Let him exert himself in the eternal Torah for the eternal world]. For G-d is testimony [in the next world] to the joy of his heart [(i.e., in his having rejoiced in doing good in his lifetime)].



## Chapter 6

###### Ecclesiastes 6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:1)


יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְרַבָּ֥ה הִ֖יא עַל־הָאָדָֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
There is an evil which I have seen under the sun; and it weighs heavily on man.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy upon men:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it besets many men:


###### Ecclesiastes 6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:2)


אִ֣ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתֶּן־ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִ֡ים עֹ֩שֶׁר֩ וּנְכָסִ֨ים וְכָב֜וֹד וְֽאֵינֶ֨נּוּ חָסֵ֥ר לְנַפְשׁ֣וֹ**׀** מִכֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־יִתְאַוֶּ֗ה וְלֹֽא־יַשְׁלִיטֶ֤נּוּ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לֶאֱכֹ֣ל מִמֶּ֔נּוּ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ נׇכְרִ֖י יֹֽאכְלֶ֑נּוּ זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וׇחֳלִ֥י רָ֖ע הֽוּא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
A man to whom God grants wealth, possessions and honor, and lacks nothing for himself of all he desires, yet God does not give him the power to eat thereof but instead a stranger will enjoy them; this is vanity and an evil disease.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
a man to whom God has given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God does not give him power to eat of it but a stranger eats it: this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
a man whom G-d gives wealth, and possessions, and honor, and his soul lacks nothing of all that it desires; but G-d does not grant him the power to eat of it [(and give charity of it and enjoy it.)] This is vanity and a sore evil.


###### Ecclesiastes 6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:3)


אִם־יוֹלִ֣יד אִ֣ישׁ מֵאָ֡ה וְשָׁנִים֩ רַבּ֨וֹת יִֽחְיֶ֜ה וְרַ֣ב**׀** שֶׁיִּהְי֣וּ יְמֵֽי־שָׁנָ֗יו וְנַפְשׁוֹ֙ לֹא־תִשְׂבַּ֣ע מִן־הַטּוֹבָ֔ה וְגַם־קְבוּרָ֖ה לֹא־הָ֣יְתָה לּ֑וֹ אָמַ֕רְתִּי ט֥וֹב מִמֶּ֖נּוּ הַנָּֽפֶל׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
If a man begets a hundred [children], and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, and his soul is not sated of goodness, and moreover he has no burial; I say, that better off than he, is the stillborn child.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If a man begets a hundred children, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, and his soul is not content with the good, and also that he has no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If a man beget a hundred [sons], and live many years, and the days of his years suffice [for all manner of good] — if his soul not be sated of that good, [(the man not rejoicing in his lot)], and burial, also not be his [(all of these having obtained with King Achav)], then I say that better than he is the still-born, [(who had never seen good nor lusted for it)].


###### Ecclesiastes 6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:4)


כִּֽי־בַהֶ֥בֶל בָּ֖א וּבַחֹ֣שֶׁךְ יֵלֵ֑ךְ וּבַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ שְׁמ֥וֹ יְכֻסֶּֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For he [the stillborn child] comes in vain and departs in darkness; and its name shrouded in darkness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For it comes in vanity, and departs in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For in vanity he comes and in darkness he goes and in darkness his name is covered.


###### Ecclesiastes 6:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:5)


גַּם־שֶׁ֥מֶשׁ לֹא־רָאָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֑ע נַ֥חַת לָזֶ֖ה מִזֶּֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Though it never saw the sun, nor knew of it; its contentment is greater than his.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Moreover it has not seen the sun, nor known anything: this has more comfort than the other.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He has neither seen the sun nor known it. This one [(the still-born)] is more "gratified" than the other.


###### Ecclesiastes 6:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:6)


וְאִלּ֣וּ חָיָ֗ה אֶ֤לֶף שָׁנִים֙ פַּעֲמַ֔יִם וְטוֹבָ֖ה לֹ֣א רָאָ֑ה הֲלֹ֛א אֶל־מָק֥וֹם אֶחָ֖ד הַכֹּ֥ל הוֹלֵֽךְ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Though he live a thousand years twice over, and enjoy no goodness; indeed, to one place, they all go.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For though he live a thousand years twice told, yet he has seen no good: do not all go to one place?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And even if he [(this wealthy one)] lived a thousand years twice over and had seen no good [i.e., had not rejoiced in his wealth], do not all [(both he and the pauper)], go to the same place [in the end]?


###### Ecclesiastes 6:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:7)


כׇּל־עֲמַ֥ל הָאָדָ֖ם לְפִ֑יהוּ וְגַם־הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ לֹ֥א תִמָּלֵֽא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
All man’s labor is to fill his mouth; yet his appetite is never filled.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All the toil of man is for his "mouth" [i.e., that he enjoy both this world and the world to come]; and shall the desire [(for this world as well as for the next)] also not be fulfilled [by this wealthy man]?


###### Ecclesiastes 6:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:8)


כִּ֛י מַה־יּוֹתֵ֥ר לֶחָכָ֖ם מִֽן־הַכְּסִ֑יל מַה־לֶּעָנִ֣י יוֹדֵ֔עַ לַהֲלֹ֖ךְ נֶ֥גֶד הַחַיִּֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
What advantage has the wise man over the fool? What disadvantage has the poor man who knows how to cope with [the problems of] life?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For what advantage has the wise more than the fool? what has the poor man who knows how to make his way among the living?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For what advantage has this wise man over the fool? What does the poor man lack in respect to him]? He [(the poor man)] also knows how to walk among the living!


###### Ecclesiastes 6:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:9)


ט֛וֹב מַרְאֵ֥ה עֵינַ֖יִם מֵֽהֲלׇךְ־נָ֑פֶשׁ גַּם־זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Better is what the eyes actually see, than the imagination of the soul; this too is vanity and vexation of spirit.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this is also vanity and a striving after wind.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[It would have been] better [(for this wealthy man to behold his wealth and enjoy it)] with the vision of his eyes than [to enjoy food and drink], which courses through the body. This, too, is a vanity and a breaking of the spirit [accorded the wicked].


###### Ecclesiastes 6:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:10)


מַה־שֶּֽׁהָיָ֗ה כְּבָר֙ נִקְרָ֣א שְׁמ֔וֹ וְנוֹדָ֖ע אֲשֶׁר־ה֣וּא אָדָ֑ם וְלֹא־יוּכַ֣ל לָדִ֔ין עִ֥ם (שהתקיף) [שֶׁתַּקִּ֖יף] מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Whatever has been has already been named, and it is foreknown what man is; he cannot contend with one who is mightier than he.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
That which has been was named long ago, and it is known that it is but man: nor may he contend with one who is mightier than he.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
What was [i.e., the distinction that this man enjoyed in his lifetime] was already called by name [i.e., acknowledged, and now it is past,] and it is known that he is [only] a man [and not a god] and that he cannot contend with the angel of death], who is stronger than he.


###### Ecclesiastes 6:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:11)


כִּ֛י יֵשׁ־דְּבָרִ֥ים הַרְבֵּ֖ה מַרְבִּ֣ים הָ֑בֶל מַה־יֹּתֵ֖ר לָאָדָֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For there are many things that increase vanity; in what way is man better for it?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Seeing there are many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For there are many [inane] things [which he occupied himself with in his lifetime], which increase vanity; and what advantage [do they prove] for a man [when he dies]?


###### Ecclesiastes 6:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/6:12)


כִּ֣י מִֽי־יוֹדֵ֩עַ֩ מַה־טּ֨וֹב לָֽאָדָ֜ם בַּֽחַיִּ֗ים מִסְפַּ֛ר יְמֵי־חַיֵּ֥י הֶבְל֖וֹ וְיַעֲשֵׂ֣ם כַּצֵּ֑ל אֲשֶׁר֙ מִֽי־יַגִּ֣יד לָֽאָדָ֔ם מַה־יִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָ֖יו תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For who knows what is good for man in [his] life, in the counted days of his vanity, which he spends as a [mere] shadow; for who can tell a man what will be after him under the sun.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For who knows what is good for man in this life, all the days of his vain life which he spends like a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For who knows what is good for a man [to do] in his lifetime [(to stand for him in the eternal world)], the few days of his life of vanity, so that he should do them [in this time, which is] as [short as a passing] shadow? For who will tell a man how his wealth will fare that he amassed unscrupulously for his sons] after him under the sun?



## Chapter 7

###### Ecclesiastes 7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:1)


ט֥וֹב שֵׁ֖ם מִשֶּׁ֣מֶן ט֑וֹב וְי֣וֹם הַמָּ֔וֶת מִיּ֖וֹם הִוָּלְדֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Better a good name than precious oil; and the day of death than the day of birth.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Better a [good] name than good oil, and [in] the day of one's death more than [on] the day of his birth.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:2)


ט֞וֹב לָלֶ֣כֶת אֶל־בֵּֽית־אֵ֗בֶל מִלֶּ֙כֶת֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה בַּאֲשֶׁ֕ר ה֖וּא ס֣וֹף כׇּל־הָאָדָ֑ם וְהַחַ֖י יִתֵּ֥ן אֶל־לִבּֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for that is the end of all men; and the living should take it to heart.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Better to go to a house of mourning [(in which both the living and the dead are "subsumed")] than to go to a house of feasting [(in which only the living are subsumed)], in that it [(the mourning)] befalls all men. And let the living one take [this] to his heart [(that as he shows lovingkindness to the dead, so will others show lovingkindness to him at his death)].


###### Ecclesiastes 7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:3)


ט֥וֹב כַּ֖עַס מִשְּׂח֑וֹק כִּֽי־בְרֹ֥עַ פָּנִ֖ים יִ֥יטַב לֵֽב׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Better vexation than levity; for through a grieved countenance, the heart is made better.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made glad.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Better (the) wrath [of the L-rd, (which turns one to repentance)] than [His] "laughter" [i.e., His indulgence]; for with a stern countenance, the heart [will be moved] to better [its ways].


###### Ecclesiastes 7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:4)


לֵ֤ב חֲכָמִים֙ בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִילִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית שִׂמְחָֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The heart of the wise [reflect on] the house of mourning; but the heart of the fools [are attracted] to the house of feasting.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning [i.e., their thoughts are on the day of death]; and the heart of the fools is in the house of feasting.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:5)


ט֕וֹב לִשְׁמֹ֖עַ גַּעֲרַ֣ת חָכָ֑ם מֵאִ֕ישׁ שֹׁמֵ֖עַ שִׁ֥יר כְּסִילִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for man to hear the song of fools.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for a man to hear the song of the fools.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:6)


כִּ֣י כְק֤וֹל הַסִּירִים֙ תַּ֣חַת הַסִּ֔יר כֵּ֖ן שְׂחֹ֣ק הַכְּסִ֑יל וְגַם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For like the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool; this too is vanity.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool: this also is vanity.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For as the sound of the thorns [crackling] under the pot, so is the laughter of the fool [("crackling" with self-importance)]. And this, too, [(the "toil" of contending with the fools)] is a vanity [(relegated to men by G-d)].


###### Ecclesiastes 7:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:7)


כִּ֥י הָעֹ֖שֶׁק יְהוֹלֵ֣ל חָכָ֑ם וִֽיאַבֵּ֥ד אֶת־לֵ֖ב מַתָּנָֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For quarreling makes the wise foolish, and a gift corrupts the heart.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Surely oppression makes a wise man mad; and a bribe destroys the heart.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For the taunting [of the fool] confounds the sage and destroys the bestowed heart [i.e., the gift of understanding bestowed upon a man].


###### Ecclesiastes 7:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:8)


ט֛וֹב אַחֲרִ֥ית דָּבָ֖ר מֵֽרֵאשִׁית֑וֹ ט֥וֹב אֶֽרֶךְ־ר֖וּחַ מִגְּבַהּ־רֽוּחַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Better is the end of a matter than its beginning; better is patience than pride.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Better is the end of a thing than the beginning of it: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Better the [(good)] end of a thing than the [(good)] beginning [(the goodness of the first being certain, and of the second, uncertain.)]


###### Ecclesiastes 7:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:9)


אַל־תְּבַהֵ֥ל בְּרֽוּחֲךָ֖ לִכְע֑וֹס כִּ֣י כַ֔עַס בְּחֵ֥יק כְּסִילִ֖ים יָנֽוּחַ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Do not quicken your spirit to anger; for anger rests in the bosom of fools.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger rests in the bosom of fools.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Be not hasty in your spirit to be wroth, for anger lies in the lap of fools.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:10)


אַל־תֹּאמַר֙ מֶ֣ה הָיָ֔ה שֶׁ֤הַיָּמִים֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים הָי֥וּ טוֹבִ֖ים מֵאֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֛י לֹ֥א מֵחׇכְמָ֖ה שָׁאַ֥לְתָּ עַל־זֶֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Do not say: was it that the former days were better than these? for it is not out of wisdom that you ask this question.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Do not say, How was it that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not inquire wisely concerning this.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not say: How is it that the earlier days were better than these? [i.e., that the earlier tzaddikim merited more good than today's] For not with reason do you ask this [(for all is relative to the merit of the generations)]


###### Ecclesiastes 7:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:11)


טוֹבָ֥ה חׇכְמָ֖ה עִֽם־נַחֲלָ֑ה וְיֹתֵ֖ר לְרֹאֵ֥י הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
It is good to have wisdom with inheritance; and [such wisdom] benefits those who see the sun [i.e. mankind].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and by it there is profit to them that see the sun.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Goodly is wisdom (together) with [the] inheritance [of the fathers], and an advantage to the seers of the sun [i.e., to all the creation].


###### Ecclesiastes 7:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:12)


כִּ֛י בְּצֵ֥ל הַֽחׇכְמָ֖ה בְּצֵ֣ל הַכָּ֑סֶף וְיִתְר֣וֹן דַּ֔עַת הַֽחׇכְמָ֖ה תְּחַיֶּ֥ה בְעָלֶֽיהָ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For wisdom shelters [as well] as money shelters; but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of him who possesses it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom gives life to those who have it.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For [whoever is] in the shadow of wisdom (is) in the shadow of silver. And [a further] advantage of knowledge [over silver] is that wisdom gives life to its possessors.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:13)


רְאֵ֖ה אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֣י מִ֤י יוּכַל֙ לְתַקֵּ֔ן אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִוְּתֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Consider the deeds of God; for who [else] can straighten that which he [man] made crooked.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he has made crooked?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
See the work of G-d [(how perfectly ordered it is, all according to man's deeds; paradise for the righteous, gehinnom for the wicked. See which you choose)]; for who can make straight [(after death)] what was made crooked [(in his lifetime)]?


###### Ecclesiastes 7:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:14)


בְּי֤וֹם טוֹבָה֙ הֱיֵ֣ה בְט֔וֹב וּבְי֥וֹם רָעָ֖ה רְאֵ֑ה גַּ֣ם אֶת־זֶ֤ה לְעֻמַּת־זֶה֙ עָשָׂ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים עַל־דִּבְרַ֗ת שֶׁלֹּ֨א יִמְצָ֧א הָֽאָדָ֛ם אַחֲרָ֖יו מְאֽוּמָה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
On a day of goodness [prosperity] be in good spirits, and on a day of adversity reflect [that]: the one was set up against the other by God, in order that man should not find anything after him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
On a day of [opportunity of doing] good, be among [the doers of] good; and on a day of evil [i.e., when punishment is visited upon the wicked], see [i.e., be among the lookers-on, and not upon the looked upon.] Also this [(the good and its reward)] against this [(the evil and its punishment)] has G-d made, so that a man find nothing [to "bethink himself" of] in regard to His conduct.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:15)


אֶת־הַכֹּ֥ל רָאִ֖יתִי בִּימֵ֣י הֶבְלִ֑י יֵ֤שׁ צַדִּיק֙ אֹבֵ֣ד בְּצִדְק֔וֹ וְיֵ֣שׁ רָשָׁ֔ע מַאֲרִ֖יךְ בְּרָעָתֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I have seen all things in the days of my vanity, there is a righteous man who perishes [despite] his righteousness, and there is a wicked man whose life is prolonged [despite] his wickedness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who prolongs his life in his wickedness.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I have seen everything in the days of my vanity: There is a tzaddik, who [though going] lost, persists in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who extends his wickedness.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:16)


אַל־תְּהִ֤י צַדִּיק֙ הַרְבֵּ֔ה וְאַל־תִּתְחַכַּ֖ם יוֹתֵ֑ר לָ֖מָּה תִּשּׁוֹמֵֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Be not exceedingly righteous nor overly wise; why destroy yourself.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Be not righteous overmuch; nor make thyself overwise: why shouldst thou destroy thyself?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not be over-righteous, and do not be over-wise. Why should you become desolate?


###### Ecclesiastes 7:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:17)


אַל־תִּרְשַׁ֥ע הַרְבֵּ֖ה וְאַל־תְּהִ֣י סָכָ֑ל לָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּת בְּלֹ֥א עִתֶּֽךָ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Be not excessively wicked, and don’t be a fool; why should you die before your time.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Be not wicked overmuch, nor be foolish: why shouldst thou die before thy time?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not be over-wicked [i.e., If you have been wicked, do not add to your wickedness], and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?


###### Ecclesiastes 7:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:18)


ט֚וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֶּאֱחֹ֣ז בָּזֶ֔ה וְגַם־מִזֶּ֖ה אַל־תַּנַּ֣ח אֶת־יָדֶ֑ךָ כִּֽי־יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים יֵצֵ֥א אֶת־כֻּלָּֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
It is best to take hold of one, and also from the other withdraw not your hand; for he who fears God will discharge his duty to both.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
It is good that thou shouldst take hold of this; but do not withdraw thy hand from that either: for he that fears God performs them all.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
It is good that you hold on to this [(righteousness)]; and also from this [("wickedness")] do not let your hand go [i.e., Always obey the righteous prophet; for even what may strike you as a wicked command, in the last analysis will be found to be a righteous one.] The fearer of G-d will fulfill all [(that the prophet says)].


###### Ecclesiastes 7:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:19)


הַֽחׇכְמָ֖ה תָּעֹ֣ז לֶחָכָ֑ם מֵֽעֲשָׂרָה֙ שַׁלִּיטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ בָּעִֽיר׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Wisdom gives [more] strength to the wise than ten rulers of the city.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Wisdom strengthens the wise more than ten rulers who are in a city.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Wisdom shall fortify the sage more than ten rulers who were in the city, [(his wisdom causing him to examine his deeds and repent of them, as opposed to the wicked rulers, who lack the wisdom to repent)].


###### Ecclesiastes 7:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:20)


כִּ֣י אָדָ֔ם אֵ֥ין צַדִּ֖יק בָּאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֶׂה־טּ֖וֹב וְלֹ֥א יֶחֱטָֽא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For there is not a righteous man on earth; who does [only] good, and never sins.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For there is not a just man upon earth, that does good, and sins not.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For the man is not (so) righteous in the land, who will do good and never sin [(wherefore such self-examination is an absolute necessity)].


###### Ecclesiastes 7:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:21)


גַּ֤ם לְכׇל־הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ אַל־תִּתֵּ֖ן לִבֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־תִשְׁמַ֥ע אֶֽת־עַבְדְּךָ֖ מְקַלְלֶֽךָ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Furthermore, of all the words that are spoken, take them not to heart; lest you hear your own servant curse you.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Also take no heed to all words that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Also, to all the words which they [(slander-mongers)] speak, do not pay heed, so that you not hear your servant curse you.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:22)


כִּ֛י גַּם־פְּעָמִ֥ים רַבּ֖וֹת יָדַ֣ע לִבֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר גַּם־[אַתָּ֖ה] (את) קִלַּ֥לְתָּ אֲחֵרִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For also there were many times as you know in your heart that you, too, have cursed others.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
for oftentimes also thy own heart knows that thou thyself hast likewise cursed others.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For your heart knows full well that many times you cursed others.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:23

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:23](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:23)


כׇּל־זֹ֖ה נִסִּ֣יתִי בַֽחׇכְמָ֑ה אָמַ֣רְתִּי אֶחְכָּ֔מָה וְהִ֖יא רְחוֹקָ֥ה מִמֶּֽנִּי׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
All this I have probed with wisdom; I said “I will be wise, but it [proved to be] far beyond me.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All this I probed through wisdom [(the Torah)]. I said I would become wise [(and master wisdom)]; but it is far from me:


###### Ecclesiastes 7:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:24)


רָח֖וֹק מַה־שֶּׁהָיָ֑ה וְעָמֹ֥ק׀עָמֹ֖ק מִ֥י יִמְצָאֶֽנּוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
That which was, is far beyond me; and so very deep, who can find it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Far is what was [(the recondite matters of the creation)], and exceedingly deep. Who shall find it? [(the studies of such matters is forbidden)].


###### Ecclesiastes 7:25

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:25](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:25)


סַבּ֨וֹתִֽי אֲנִ֤י וְלִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת וְלָת֔וּר וּבַקֵּ֥שׁ חׇכְמָ֖ה וְחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן וְלָדַ֙עַת֙ רֶ֣שַׁע כֶּ֔סֶל וְהַסִּכְל֖וּת הוֹלֵלֽוֹת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
So I turned about and applied my heart to know, to explore, and to search for wisdom and the reason for things, and to know that wickedness is folly, and foolishness is madness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I cast about in my mind to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things, and to know the wickedness of folly and foolishness which is madness:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I cast about in my heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom [(that of the mitzvah of the red heifer)], and accounting [(of the time of the redemption)], and to know [i.e., to plumb] the wickedness of folly [i.e., heresy], and its intermixture of madness.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:26

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:26](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:26)


וּמוֹצֶ֨א אֲנִ֜י מַ֣ר מִמָּ֗וֶת אֶת־הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁר־הִ֨יא מְצוֹדִ֧ים וַחֲרָמִ֛ים לִבָּ֖הּ אֲסוּרִ֣ים יָדֶ֑יהָ ט֞וֹב לִפְנֵ֤י הָאֱלֹהִים֙ יִמָּלֵ֣ט מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְחוֹטֵ֖א יִלָּ֥כֶד בָּֽהּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And I find more bitter than death, the woman—whose heart is full of traps and nets, her hands as chains; he who seeks to please God, will escape from her, but the sinner will be trapped by her.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands are fetters: he who pleases God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be caught by her.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I find more bitter than death the "woman" [(heresy)], whose heart is snares and nets. Her hands are bonds. The good before G-d shall escape her, and the sinner shall be snared by her.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:27

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:27](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:27)


רְאֵה֙ זֶ֣ה מָצָ֔אתִי אָמְרָ֖ה קֹהֶ֑לֶת אַחַ֥ת לְאַחַ֖ת לִמְצֹ֥א חֶשְׁבּֽוֹן׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
See this is what I have found says Koheles; adding one to another to find an accounting.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Behold, this have I found, says Qohelet, counting one thing to another, to find out the sum,


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
See, this have I found, said Koheleth: [(All the mitzvoth of the righteous and the transgressions of the wicked, respectively,)] [are added] one to one, to emerge [in a great] account.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:28

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:28](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:28)


אֲשֶׁ֛ר עוֹד־בִּקְשָׁ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֑אתִי אָדָ֞ם אֶחָ֤ד מֵאֶ֙לֶף֙ מָצָ֔אתִי וְאִשָּׁ֥ה בְכׇל־אֵ֖לֶּה לֹ֥א מָצָֽאתִי׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For which yet my soul searches, and yet I have not found; one [worthy] man among a thousand I have found, but a [worthy] woman among all of them, I have not found.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
which yet my soul seeks, but I have not found it: One man among a thousand I have found; but a woman among all those I have not found.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[(Aside from everything mentioned above, which I sought to fathom but could not)], there was another thing that my soul sought, [(a woman of complete integrity)], but I could not find (one). One man [(of such integrity)] among a thousand I found; but [such] a woman among a thousand I did not find.


###### Ecclesiastes 7:29

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:29](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/7:29)


לְבַד֙ רְאֵה־זֶ֣ה מָצָ֔אתִי אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֧ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־הָאָדָ֖ם יָשָׁ֑ר וְהֵ֥מָּה בִקְשׁ֖וּ חִשְּׁבֹנ֥וֹת רַבִּֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
See, this only have I found: that God made man upright; but they sought out many stratagems.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Lo, this only have I found, that God has made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
See, this alone have I found: G-d made Adam straight, but they [(the combination of Adam and Eve)] sought many [sinful] schemes.



## Chapter 8

###### Ecclesiastes 8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:1)


מִ֚י כְּהֶ֣חָכָ֔ם וּמִ֥י יוֹדֵ֖עַ פֵּ֣שֶׁר דָּבָ֑ר חׇכְמַ֤ת אָדָם֙ תָּאִ֣יר פָּנָ֔יו וְעֹ֥ז פָּנָ֖יו יְשֻׁנֶּֽא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Who is like the wise person and who knows how to interpret things? A man’s wisdom lights up his face, and the boldness of his face is changed.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Who is like the wise man? and who knows the interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom makes his face to shine, and the boldness of his face is changed.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Who is as [distinctive as] the sages, and who knows [(as he does)] the meaning of a thing? A man's wisdom will light his face, and the splendor of his countenance will transcend [(the faces of other men, so that they will come to fear him)].


###### Ecclesiastes 8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:2)


אֲנִי֙ פִּי־מֶ֣לֶךְ שְׁמֹ֔ר וְעַ֕ל דִּבְרַ֖ת שְׁבוּעַ֥ת אֱלֹהִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
My [advice to you is]: keep the King’s command, and do so because of the oath to God.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I counsel thee to keep the king’s commandment, and that in the manner of an oath of God.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[Therefore,] I [need and prepared to] heed the mouth [i.e., the words] of the King according to the oath of G-d [into which we entered in Chorev, to observe His mitzvoth].


###### Ecclesiastes 8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:3)


אַל־תִּבָּהֵ֤ל מִפָּנָיו֙ תֵּלֵ֔ךְ אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹ֖ד בְּדָבָ֣ר רָ֑ע כִּ֛י כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַחְפֹּ֖ץ יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Do not hasten to leave His Presence do not persist in doing evil; for whatever pleases Him, He does.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Be not hasty to go out of his presence: stand not in an evil thing; for he does whatever pleases him.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not be hasty [to think] that you can escape Him [(for wherever you may go, there He reigns)]. Do not persist in [the doing of] an evil thing. For whatever He wishes He may do [(in exacting punishment of you)].


###### Ecclesiastes 8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:4)


בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דְּבַר־מֶ֖לֶךְ שִׁלְט֑וֹן וּמִ֥י יֹֽאמַר־ל֖וֹ מַֽה־תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For the King’s word is all powerful; and who can say to Him, “What are You doing?”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For the word of a king has authority: and who may say to him, What doest thou?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For the King's word rules, and who can tell Him what to do?


###### Ecclesiastes 8:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:5)


שׁוֹמֵ֣ר מִצְוָ֔ה לֹ֥א יֵדַ֖ע דָּבָ֣ר רָ֑ע וְעֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֔ט יֵדַ֖ע לֵ֥ב חָכָֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He who preserves the commandment will know no evil; and [the significance of] time and judgment is known by the wise man.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He who keeps the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man’s heart discerns both time and method.
