**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[But] the keeper of a mitzvah will not know an evil thing; and the heart of the wise one knows (of) the time of retribution [upon the wicked].


###### Ecclesiastes 8:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:6)


כִּ֣י לְכׇל־חֵ֔פֶץ יֵ֖שׁ עֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּֽי־רָעַ֥ת הָאָדָ֖ם רַבָּ֥ה עָלָֽיו׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For every matter there is a time and judgement; when the evil of man overwhelms him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For every matter has its time and method, though the misery of man is great upon him.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For every [evil] will [acted out] has a time [for punishment], when a man's evil is great upon him [i.e., when his "measure" of evil is full].


###### Ecclesiastes 8:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:7)


כִּֽי־אֵינֶ֥נּוּ יֹדֵ֖עַ מַה־שֶּׁיִּֽהְיֶ֑ה כִּ֚י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יִֽהְיֶ֔ה מִ֖י יַגִּ֥יד לֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For he does not know what will be, for when it comes to pass who will tell him?


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For he knows not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For [when the wicked man transgresses], he does not know what [punishment awaits him]. And when it arrives, who will tell him [(in the swiftness of its onslaught, what counsels to take)]?


###### Ecclesiastes 8:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:8)


אֵ֣ין אָדָ֞ם שַׁלִּ֤יט בָּר֙וּחַ֙ לִכְל֣וֹא אֶת־הָר֔וּחַ וְאֵ֤ין שִׁלְטוֹן֙ בְּי֣וֹם הַמָּ֔וֶת וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁלַ֖חַת בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־יְמַלֵּ֥ט רֶ֖שַׁע אֶת־בְּעָלָֽיו׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Man has no power over the spirit, to retain the spirit, he has no power over the day of death, nor dispatch in battle; nor will wickedness save its perpetrator.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
There is no man who has power over the wind to retain the wind; nor has he power over the day of death: and there is no discharge in that war; nor shall wickedness deliver those who are given up to it.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
No man keeps the spirit [i.e., the will of the L-rd's messenger] from depriving him [(the man)] of the spirit [(i.e., the breath of his body,) so that the Angel of Death not take it]. And [no king's] rule prevails [on the appointed] day of his death. [e.g., we always find “And King David did, etc."; but, on the day of his death, we find (I Kings 2:1): "And the days of David drew near to die."] And there is no deputation [(of another to serve as a stand-in)] in this war. And evil will not rescue its practitioner.


###### Ecclesiastes 8:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:9)


אֶת־כׇּל־זֶ֤ה רָאִ֙יתִי֙ וְנָת֣וֹן אֶת־לִבִּ֔י לְכׇֽל־מַעֲשֶׂ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ עֵ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֧ט הָאָדָ֛ם בְּאָדָ֖ם לְרַ֥ע לֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
All this I have seen, and I applied my heart to [understand] all the work that is done under the sun; there is a time when man rules over man to his detriment.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All this have I seen, and have appointed my heart to every work that is done under the sun: there is a time when one man rules over another to his own hurt.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All of this [(the above)] I saw. And I [also] applied my heart to all the deeds [of men] done under the sun, seeing how one man lorded it over another to his [own] undoing.


###### Ecclesiastes 8:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:10)


וּבְכֵ֡ן רָאִ֩יתִי֩ רְשָׁעִ֨ים קְבֻרִ֜ים וָבָ֗אוּ וּמִמְּק֤וֹם קָדוֹשׁ֙ יְהַלֵּ֔כוּ וְיִֽשְׁתַּכְּח֥וּ בָעִ֖יר אֲשֶׁ֣ר כֵּן־עָשׂ֑וּ גַּם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And so I have seen how the wicked were buried and came forth anew [whereas the righteous] who were gone from the holy place were forgotten in the very city where they performed [righteousness;] this, too, is vanity.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And so I saw the wicked buried, and come to their rest; but those who had done right were gone from the holy place, and were forgotten in the city: this also is vanity.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And then I saw [prophetically], wicked men [deserving to be] buried, who came [to destroy Israel], and who went from the holy place [(the Temple, which they had defiled], vaunting themselves in [their] cities for having done so. This, too, is vanity [(intended to try humankind, leading them to think — from the delay of punishment — that there is no judgment and no Judge.]


###### Ecclesiastes 8:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:11)


אֲשֶׁר֙ אֵין־נַעֲשָׂ֣ה פִתְגָ֔ם מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ה מְהֵרָ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֡ן מָלֵ֞א לֵ֧ב בְּֽנֵי־הָאָדָ֛ם בָּהֶ֖ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת רָֽע׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Because the execution of sentence against evil deeds is not done quickly; therefore, the hearts of men are filled with encouragement to do evil.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The fact that punishment for wrongdoing is not hastily executed fills the hearts of men within them to do evil


###### Ecclesiastes 8:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:12)


אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֹטֶ֗א עֹשֶׂ֥ה רָ֛ע מְאַ֖ת וּמַאֲרִ֣יךְ ל֑וֹ כִּ֚י גַּם־יוֹדֵ֣עַ אָ֔נִי אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִהְיֶה־טּוֹב֙ לְיִרְאֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִֽירְא֖וּ מִלְּפָנָֽיו׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and his days are prolonged; nevertheless, I know that it will be well with those who fear God, who fear before His Presence.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Though a sinner do evil a hundred times, and his days are prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with those who fear God, who fear before him:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
in that [they see that] the sinner does evil a hundred [times] and that He withholds [punishment] from him. For [in spite of this] I know also that [in the end] it will go well for the fearers of G-d for fearing Him.


###### Ecclesiastes 8:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:13)


וְטוֹב֙ לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה לָֽרָשָׁ֔ע וְלֹֽא־יַאֲרִ֥יךְ יָמִ֖ים כַּצֵּ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֛ר אֵינֶ֥נּוּ יָרֵ֖א מִלִּפְנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And it will not be well with the wicked, nor shall he prolong his days which are like a shadow; because he does not fear before the Presence of God.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
but it shall not be well with the wicked, and, like the shadow, he will not prolong his days; because he does not fear before God.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
But it shall not go well for the wicked one and his days will not be prolonged, [(but he will be)] like a shadow, for not having feared G-d.


###### Ecclesiastes 8:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:14)


יֶשׁ־הֶ֘בֶל֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נַעֲשָׂ֣ה עַל־הָאָ֒רֶץ֒ אֲשֶׁ֣ר**׀** יֵ֣שׁ צַדִּיקִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר מַגִּ֤יעַ אֲלֵהֶם֙ כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָרְשָׁעִ֔ים וְיֵ֣שׁ רְשָׁעִ֔ים שֶׁמַּגִּ֥יעַ אֲלֵהֶ֖ם כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הַצַּדִּיקִ֑ים אָמַ֕רְתִּי שֶׁגַּם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
There is a vanity which is done upon the earth: there are righteous men who suffer as if they had performed [the same] deeds as those who are wicked; and there are wicked men who receive [reward] as if they had performed the same deeds as the righteous; I said that this too is vanity.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there are just men, to whom it happens according to the deeds of the wicked; again, there are wicked men, to whom it happens according to the deeds of the righteous: I said that this also is vanity.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
There is vanity [(confounding men)] that is done upon the earth — righteous men being visited [with evil,] which befits the deeds of the wicked, and wicked men being accorded [good,] which befits the deeds of the righteous. I said: This, too, is vanity [i.e., one of the vanities incident to the world].


###### Ecclesiastes 8:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:15)


וְשִׁבַּ֤חְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ אֶת־הַשִּׂמְחָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֵֽין־ט֤וֹב לָֽאָדָם֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ כִּ֛י אִם־לֶאֱכֹ֥ל וְלִשְׁתּ֖וֹת וְלִשְׂמ֑וֹחַ וְה֞וּא יִלְוֶ֣נּוּ בַעֲמָל֗וֹ יְמֵ֥י חַיָּ֛יו אֲשֶׁר־נָֽתַן־ל֥וֹ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I extolled [the concept of] rejoicing for there is nothing better for man under the sun than to eat and drink and be joyful; and this will accompany him in his toil [all] the days of his life which God has given him under the sun.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
So I commend mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall accompany him in his labour during the days of his life, which God gives him under the sun.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I praised the happiness [(of rejoicing in one's lot and occupying oneself with joy-giving mitzvoth and with shunning transgression)], there being nothing better for a man [all] the days of his life that G-d has given him under the sun than eating, drinking, and rejoicing [in this manner]. And it [(this joy)] will accompany him in his toil.


###### Ecclesiastes 8:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:16)


כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤תִּי אֶת־לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת חׇכְמָ֔ה וְלִרְאוֹת֙ אֶת־הָ֣עִנְיָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֣י גַ֤ם בַּיּוֹם֙ וּבַלַּ֔יְלָה שֵׁנָ֕ה בְּעֵינָ֖יו אֵינֶ֥נּוּ רֹאֶֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
When I applied my heart to know wisdom and to observe the activity that is done on the earth—for neither by day nor by night does he see sleep with his eyes.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (how one sees no sleep with one’s eyes either by day or by night;)


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
When I set my heart to know wisdom and to see what is done upon the earth, that both day and night, he [(the wicked one, who is steeped in the pursuit of wealth and of lust)] does not see [i.e., does not attain the object of his desires],


###### Ecclesiastes 8:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/8:17)


וְרָאִ֘יתִי֮ אֶת־כׇּל־מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִים֒ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יוּכַ֜ל הָאָדָ֗ם לִמְצוֹא֙ אֶת־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נַעֲשָׂ֣ה תַֽחַת־הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ בְּ֠שֶׁ֠ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲמֹ֧ל הָאָדָ֛ם לְבַקֵּ֖שׁ וְלֹ֣א יִמְצָ֑א וְגַ֨ם אִם־יֹאמַ֤ר הֶֽחָכָם֙ לָדַ֔עַת לֹ֥א יוּכַ֖ל לִמְצֹֽא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And I saw all the works of God—that man cannot discover the work that is done under the sun; and though a man labor to seek it out he will not find it; and even though a wise man declares that he knows it, he, too, will not be able to discover it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek it out, yet he shall not find it; furthermore; though a wise man think to know it, yet he shall not be able to find it.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Then I saw, of all the acts of G-d [that He revealed to men], that a man could not discover the full meaning of the deed that is done [by G-d] under the sun [e.g., the wicked prospering and the righteous failing]. For [I have seen] many men toiling to seek it and not finding it. And even if the sage claims to know it, he cannot know it, [(as even Moses could not know it), viz. Exodus 33:13, etc.]



## Chapter 9

###### Ecclesiastes 9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:1)


כִּ֣י אֶת־כׇּל־זֶ֞ה נָתַ֤תִּי אֶל־לִבִּי֙ וְלָב֣וּר אֶת־כׇּל־זֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הַצַּדִּיקִ֧ים וְהַחֲכָמִ֛ים וַעֲבָדֵיהֶ֖ם בְּיַ֣ד הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים גַּֽם־אַהֲבָ֣ה גַם־שִׂנְאָ֗ה אֵ֤ין יוֹדֵ֙עַ֙ הָֽאָדָ֔ם הַכֹּ֖ל לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For all this I put to my heart and [I sought to] make all this clear: that the righteous and the wise and their works are in the hand of God; whether it be love or hate, man does not know, all is before them.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For all this I laid to my heart, and sought to clarify all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their deeds, are in the hand of God: no man knows whether love or hatred is in store: all is before them.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For all of this I took to heart and [I endeavored] to elucidate all this, that the righteous and the sages and their servants [(their disciples, attendants, and emulators] are in the hand of G-d. [He assists and judges them to benefit them in their latter end.] [Parameters of] both love [i.e., what would make men loved by the L-rd] and of hatred are unknown to [other] men; but all [lies revealed] before them [(the righteous and the sages)].


###### Ecclesiastes 9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:2)


הַכֹּ֞ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר לַכֹּ֗ל מִקְרֶ֨ה אֶחָ֜ד לַצַּדִּ֤יק וְלָרָשָׁע֙ לַטּוֹב֙ וְלַטָּה֣וֹר וְלַטָּמֵ֔א וְלַ֨זֹּבֵ֔חַ וְלַאֲשֶׁ֖ר אֵינֶ֣נּוּ זֹבֵ֑חַ כַּטּוֹב֙ כַּֽחֹטֶ֔א הַנִּשְׁבָּ֕ע כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר שְׁבוּעָ֥ה יָרֵֽא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
All things come alike to all; the same fate [awaits] the righteous and the wicked, the good and the pure and the impure, to him who brings offerings, and to him who does not bring offerings; as is with the good man so is it with the sinner, as is with the one who swears [easily] so is it with the one who fears an oath.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him who sacrifices, and to him who does not sacrifice: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he who swears, as he who fears an oath.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All [take it to heart] when [they perceive that] all [men receive their just desserts]. [And all men know] that one fate [(death)] befalls all men in this world. But the righteous, knowing that judgment awaits all men in the world to come, choose to be righteous in this world.] [Some instances of the above phenomenon:] the righteous one [(Noach)] and the wicked one [(Pharaoh Nechoh), both of whom were lame], the pure one [(Aaron)] and the unclean one [(the spies) — the same fate [(not entering Eretz Yisrael) befalling both, though Aaron spoke in praise of the land, and the spies, against it]; the sacrificer [Yoshiyahu, viz. II Chronicles 35:11) and the non-sacrificer [(Achav) — both of whom were slain by arrows]; the good man [(David, who built the Temple)] and the sinner [(Nevuchadnezzar, who destroyed it) — both reigned forty years]; the false swearer [(Tzidkiyahu, viz. II Chronicles 36:134)] and the fearer of oaths [(Shimshon, viz. Judges 15:12,) both of whom died by having their eyes gouged out.]


###### Ecclesiastes 9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:3)


זֶ֣ה**׀** רָ֗ע בְּכֹ֤ל אֲשֶֽׁר־נַעֲשָׂה֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ כִּֽי־מִקְרֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד לַכֹּ֑ל וְגַ֣ם לֵ֣ב בְּֽנֵי־הָ֠אָדָ֠ם מָלֵא־רָ֨ע וְהוֹלֵל֤וֹת בִּלְבָבָם֙ בְּחַיֵּיהֶ֔ם וְאַחֲרָ֖יו אֶל־הַמֵּתִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
This is an evil in all that is done under the sun: that the same fate awaits all; [therefore], the hearts of men are filled with evil, and madness is in their hearts during their lifetime, and afterwards they join the dead.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
This is an evil in all things that are done under the sun, that there is one event to all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
This is an evil among all that is done under the sun — that one fate befalls all. And the heart of men, too, is full of evil. [(They say that there is no punishment for the wicked and that everything is governed by chance, the same thing happening, sometimes to the righteous and sometimes to the wicked.)] There is revelry in their hearts in their lives, and afterwards — to the dead [i.e., Gehinnom].


###### Ecclesiastes 9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:4)


כִּי־מִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר (יבחר) [יְחֻבַּ֔ר] אֶ֥ל כׇּל־הַחַיִּ֖ים יֵ֣שׁ בִּטָּח֑וֹן כִּֽי־לְכֶ֤לֶב חַי֙ ה֣וּא ט֔וֹב מִן־הָאַרְיֵ֖ה הַמֵּֽת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope; for a live dog is better than a dead lion.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For one [(even a wicked one)] who is connected to all that lives [(even to wicked men)] has hope [(of repenting before he dies)], for [(in this respect]) it is better to be a living dog than a dead lion.


###### Ecclesiastes 9:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:5)


כִּ֧י הַֽחַיִּ֛ים יוֹדְעִ֖ים שֶׁיָּמֻ֑תוּ וְהַמֵּתִ֞ים אֵינָ֧ם יוֹדְעִ֣ים מְא֗וּמָה וְאֵֽין־ע֤וֹד לָהֶם֙ שָׂכָ֔ר כִּ֥י נִשְׁכַּ֖ח זִכְרָֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For the living know that they will die; but the dead know nothing, and there is no further reward for them, for their memory is forgotten.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know nothing, nor do they have any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For the living know that they will die [(and the thought of death might move them to repentance)]. But the dead know nothing, and reward [(for new mitzvoth)] no longer awaits them, their remembrance having been forgotten.


###### Ecclesiastes 9:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:6)


גַּ֣ם אַהֲבָתָ֧ם גַּם־שִׂנְאָתָ֛ם גַּם־קִנְאָתָ֖ם כְּבָ֣ר אָבָ֑דָה וְחֵ֨לֶק אֵין־לָהֶ֥ם עוֹד֙ לְעוֹלָ֔ם בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־נַעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Also their love, their hate, and their jealousy have already perished; and a portion they will never again have in anything that is done under the sun.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now long perished; nor have they any more a portion forever in any thing that is done under the sun.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Also their love of [(idolatrous folly)]; also their hatred [of wisdom]; also their [objects of G-d's] envy, [i.e., their idols], have already gone lost; but they will never have a portion [i.e., the merits of their children (to atone for them after their death)] in all that is done under the sun.


###### Ecclesiastes 9:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:7)


לֵ֣ךְ אֱכֹ֤ל בְּשִׂמְחָה֙ לַחְמֶ֔ךָ וּֽשְׁתֵ֥ה בְלֶב־ט֖וֹב יֵינֶ֑ךָ כִּ֣י כְבָ֔ר רָצָ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶֽת־מַעֲשֶֽׂיךָ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Go eat your bread in joy, and drink your wine with a glad heart; for already God has accepted your deeds.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God has already accepted thy works.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[But you, the righteous one,] go and eat your bread in joy, and drink your wine with a good heart, for G-d has already accepted your good deeds [and you will merit the world to come.]


###### Ecclesiastes 9:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:8)


בְּכׇל־עֵ֕ת יִהְי֥וּ בְגָדֶ֖יךָ לְבָנִ֑ים וְשֶׁ֖מֶן עַל־רֹאשְׁךָ֥ אַל־יֶחְסָֽר׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
At all times, let your garments be white; and your head never lack oil.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no oil.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
At all times let your garments be white, and let oil not be lacking upon your head [i.e., be constantly engaged in mitzvoth, so that if you die today, you will enter the world to come in peace.]


###### Ecclesiastes 9:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:9)


רְאֵ֨ה חַיִּ֜ים עִם־אִשָּׁ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־אָהַ֗בְתָּ כׇּל־יְמֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י הֶבְלֶ֔ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽתַן־לְךָ֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י הֶבְלֶ֑ךָ כִּ֣י ה֤וּא חֶלְקְךָ֙ בַּֽחַיִּ֔ים וּבַעֲמָ֣לְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה עָמֵ֖ל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
See [to enjoy] life with the wife you love, all the days of your vain life which He has given you under the sun—all the days of your vanity;—for that is your portion in life, and in your labor in which you toil under the sun.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he has given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in life, and in thy labour in which thou dost labour under the sun.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
See life with the woman that you love [i.e., choose an occupation that will provide sustenance for you, together with your Torah study], all the days of the life of your vanity [i.e., your life in this world] that He has given you under the sun all the days of your vanity. For it is your portion in this life and in your toil wherein you toil under the sun [i.e., if you do this, you will enjoy life both in this world and in the world to come; for engaging in both (labor and Torah study) banishes sin.]


###### Ecclesiastes 9:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:10)


כֹּ֠ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּמְצָ֧א יָֽדְךָ֛ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת בְּכֹחֲךָ֖ עֲשֵׂ֑ה כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין מַעֲשֶׂ֤ה וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן֙ וְדַ֣עַת וְחׇכְמָ֔ה בִּשְׁא֕וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה הֹלֵ֥ךְ שָֽׁמָּה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Whatever you are able to do do with all your might; for there is neither deed, nor strategy, nor knowledge, nor wisdom in the grave where you are going.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Whatever thy hand finds to do, do it with thy strength, for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in She᾽ol, whither thou goest.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All that your hand finds to do [(in accordance with the will of your Master)], while you are [yet] in your strength [(in this world)], do it. For there is no act [to your credit after you die. And if you act righteously during your lifetime, there is no] accounting [that you need fear] in the grave whither you go. [Neither is there act] or knowledge or wisdom [there to the credit of the wicked, who will have to give an accounting for their sins.]


###### Ecclesiastes 9:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:11)


שַׁ֜בְתִּי וְרָאֹ֣ה תַֽחַת־הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ כִּ֣י לֹא֩ לַקַּלִּ֨ים הַמֵּר֜וֹץ וְלֹ֧א לַגִּבּוֹרִ֣ים הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְ֠גַ֠ם לֹ֣א לַחֲכָמִ֥ים לֶ֙חֶם֙ וְגַ֨ם לֹ֤א לַנְּבֹנִים֙ עֹ֔שֶׁר וְגַ֛ם לֹ֥א לַיֹּדְעִ֖ים חֵ֑ן כִּי־עֵ֥ת וָפֶ֖גַע יִקְרֶ֥ה אֶת־כֻּלָּֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Again I saw under the sun: that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor does bread [come] to the wise, nor riches to men of understanding, nor favor to the learned; for time and chance happen to them all.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happens to them all.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I turned and saw under the sun that not to the swift is the race, and not to the strong is the war, and also, not to the wise is bread, and also, not the understanding is wealth, and also, not to the knowing is favor; for time and chance befall all.


###### Ecclesiastes 9:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:12)


כִּ֡י גַּם֩ לֹֽא־יֵדַ֨ע הָאָדָ֜ם אֶת־עִתּ֗וֹ כַּדָּגִים֙ שֶׁנֶּֽאֱחָזִים֙ בִּמְצוֹדָ֣ה רָעָ֔ה וְכַ֨צִּפֳּרִ֔ים הָאֲחֻז֖וֹת בַּפָּ֑ח כָּהֵ֗ם יֽוּקָשִׁים֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָֽאָדָ֔ם לְעֵ֣ת רָעָ֔ה כְּשֶׁתִּפּ֥וֹל עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם פִּתְאֹֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
For also, man does not know his time, as fish that are caught in a fatal net, as birds that are caught in a snare; like them, men are snared in the moment of misfortune, when it falls upon them suddenly.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For man also knows not his time: like the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and like the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly upon them.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For a man also does not know his time, like fishes that are caught in a flimsy net and like birds that are caught in the snare. Like them, men are snared in a time of evil [i.e., when their evil is visited upon them], when it falls upon them suddenly.

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
This, too, I have seen [concerning] wisdom under the sun; and its impact was great upon me.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed great to me:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Also this [(what follows)] have I seen to be wisdom under the sun, and it is great to me.

[There was] a small city, with few men within it; and a mighty king came upon it and surrounded it and built great bulwarks against it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
there was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great siegeworks against it:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A little city, and few people in it, and there came to it a great king and surrounded it, and built against it great siegeworks.


###### Ecclesiastes 9:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:15)


וּמָ֣צָא בָ֗הּ אִ֤ישׁ מִסְכֵּן֙ חָכָ֔ם וּמִלַּט־ה֥וּא אֶת־הָעִ֖יר בְּחׇכְמָת֑וֹ וְאָדָם֙ לֹ֣א זָכַ֔ר אֶת־הָאִ֥ישׁ הַמִּסְכֵּ֖ן הַהֽוּא׃

But there was found in the city, a poor wise man, and he saved the city with his wisdom; yet no person remembered that poor man.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom saved the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And he found therein a wise, unfortunate man, who rescued the city with his wisdom, and no one remembered that unfortunate man [i.e., he was regarded as naught.]


###### Ecclesiastes 9:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:16)


וְאָמַ֣רְתִּי אָ֔נִי טוֹבָ֥ה חׇכְמָ֖ה מִגְּבוּרָ֑ה וְחׇכְמַ֤ת הַמִּסְכֵּן֙ בְּזוּיָ֔ה וּדְבָרָ֖יו אֵינָ֥ם נִשְׁמָעִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And [yet] I said: “Wisdom is better than might; [although] a poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words go unheeded.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I said to myself: Better is wisdom than strength [(wisdom having rescued the city where strength had failed)]; but the wisdom of the poor one is shamed, and his words are not heeded.


###### Ecclesiastes 9:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/9:17)


דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֔ים בְּנַ֖חַת נִשְׁמָעִ֑ים מִזַּעֲקַ֥ת מוֹשֵׁ֖ל בַּכְּסִילִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The words of the wise, are received with pleasure more than the shouts of a ruler of fools.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The words of wise men heard in quiet are better than the cry of him who rules among fools.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The words of the wise spoken softly are more readily accepted than the cry of the ruler of the fools.

טוֹבָ֥ה חׇכְמָ֖ה מִכְּלֵ֣י קְרָ֑ב וְחוֹטֶ֣א אֶחָ֔ד יְאַבֵּ֖ד טוֹבָ֥ה הַרְבֵּֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroys a multitude of good.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroys much good.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Better wisdom than weapons of war; and one sinner can destroy an abundance of good.



## Chapter 10

###### Ecclesiastes 10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:1)


זְב֣וּבֵי מָ֔וֶת יַבְאִ֥ישׁ יַבִּ֖יעַ שֶׁ֣מֶן רוֹקֵ֑חַ יָקָ֛ר מֵחׇכְמָ֥ה מִכָּב֖וֹד סִכְל֥וּת מְעָֽט׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Dead flies decay and pollute the perfumer’s ointment; wisdom and honor are outweighed by a little foolishness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Dead flies cause the perfumer’s ointment to give off a foul odour: so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honour.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The flies of death [i.e., the flies of winter, though devitalized and near death, still] putrefy [and cause to] ferment the [purest] perfumer's oil. [In the same way,] weightier than [a man's] wisdom and honor is a little folly.


###### Ecclesiastes 10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:2)


לֵ֤ב חָכָם֙ לִֽימִינ֔וֹ וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִ֖יל לִשְׂמֹאלֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The heart [understanding] of a wise man is at his right hand; but the heart of a fool is at his left.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
A wise man’s heart inclines him to his right hand: but a fool’s heart to his left.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The heart of the wise man is [inclined] to his right [i.e., to good] and the heart of the fool is inclined] to his left [i.e., to evil.]


###### Ecclesiastes 10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:3)


וְגַם־בַּדֶּ֛רֶךְ (כשהסכל) [כְּשֶׁסָּכָ֥ל] הֹלֵ֖ךְ לִבּ֣וֹ חָסֵ֑ר וְאָמַ֥ר לַכֹּ֖ל סָכָ֥ל הֽוּא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Also, when a fool walks by the way, his heart [understanding] fails him; and proclaims to all that he is a fool.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Yea also, when a fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he reveals to everyone that he is a fool.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And even on the path that the fool walks, his heart is wanting and [in his manner of walking and speaking] declares to all that he is a fool.


###### Ecclesiastes 10:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:4)


אִם־ר֤וּחַ הַמּוֹשֵׁל֙ תַּעֲלֶ֣ה עָלֶ֔יךָ מְקוֹמְךָ֖ אַל־תַּנַּ֑ח כִּ֣י מַרְפֵּ֔א יַנִּ֖יחַ חֲטָאִ֥ים גְּדוֹלִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
If the spirit [anger] of the Ruler flares up against you, do not leave your place; for softness pacifies great offenses.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, do not leave thy place; for deference appeases great offences.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If the spirit [of judgment] of the Ruler arises against you, do not leave your place [i.e., do not abandon those good traits that you possess], for it [i.e., the suffering that comes upon you] attenuates your transgressions and lightens [your] grave sins.


###### Ecclesiastes 10:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:5)


יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ כִּשְׁגָגָ֕ה שֶׁיֹּצָ֖א מִלִּפְנֵ֥י הַשַּׁלִּֽיט׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
There is an evil which I have seen under the sun; like an error emanating from the ruler.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, when an error proceeds from the ruler:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, like an inadvertency issuing from the mouth of the Ruler, [which cannot be retracted.]


###### Ecclesiastes 10:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:6)


נִתַּ֣ן הַסֶּ֔כֶל בַּמְּרוֹמִ֖ים רַבִּ֑ים וַעֲשִׁירִ֖ים בַּשֵּׁ֥פֶל יֵשֵֽׁבוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Folly is set upon great heights; but the rich sit in low places.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[The evil:] He has placed folly [i.e., men of wickedness and folly, who are destined to destroy the Temple] in the height of heights, and the "wealthy" [i.e., Israel, the distinguished men of my (Solomon's) days] shall sit in lowliness [viz. Eichah 2:10].


###### Ecclesiastes 10:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:7)


רָאִ֥יתִי עֲבָדִ֖ים עַל־סוּסִ֑ים וְשָׂרִ֛ים הֹלְכִ֥ים כַּעֲבָדִ֖ים עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
I have seen slaves on horses, and princes walking on foot like slaves on the ground.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I saw [(prophetically,) former slaves [(the Kasdim)] on horseback, and princes [(bound Jewish captives)] walking [before them] like slaves, on the ground [viz. Isaiah 23:13].


###### Ecclesiastes 10:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:8)


חֹפֵ֥ר גּוּמָּ֖ץ בּ֣וֹ יִפּ֑וֹל וּפֹרֵ֥ץ גָּדֵ֖ר יִשְּׁכֶ֥נּוּ נָחָֽשׁ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He who digs a pit will fall into it; he who breaks down a fence will be bitten by a snake.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He who digs a pit shall fall into it; and whoever breaks through a hedge, a snake shall bite him.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The digger of a pit will fall in it; and the breacher of a fence will be bitten by a snake.


###### Ecclesiastes 10:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:9)


מַסִּ֣יעַ אֲבָנִ֔ים יֵעָצֵ֖ב בָּהֶ֑ם בּוֹקֵ֥עַ עֵצִ֖ים יִסָּ֥כֶן בָּֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He who removes stones will be hurt by them; he who splits logs will be endangered by them.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He who removes stones shall be hurt by them; and he who chops wood shall be endangered by that.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The carrier of stones [from the quarry] will be wearied by them. The chopper of wood will be warmed by it.


###### Ecclesiastes 10:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:10)


אִם־קֵהָ֣ה הַבַּרְזֶ֗ל וְהוּא֙ לֹא־פָנִ֣ים קִלְקַ֔ל וַחֲיָלִ֖ים יְגַבֵּ֑ר וְיִתְר֥וֹן הַכְשֵׁ֖יר חׇכְמָֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
If the axe is blunt, and one has not sharpened its edge, he must exert more strength; there is more profit in a skill of wisdom.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If the iron is blunt, and one does not whet the edge, then he must put to more strength: but wisdom increases skill.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[Even] if the iron [of the sword] be blunted and the edge has not been honed, he [(the commander)] may [yet] spur on [his] soldiers [to victory]. And [there is yet] an additional advantage [in] wisdom [i.e., in the sage's emboldening them by his wisdom.]


###### Ecclesiastes 10:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:11)


אִם־יִשֹּׁ֥ךְ הַנָּחָ֖שׁ בְּלוֹא־לָ֑חַשׁ וְאֵ֣ין יִתְר֔וֹן לְבַ֖עַל הַלָּשֽׁוֹן׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
If the snake bites before it is charmed; there is no advantage in having a charmer.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If the serpent bites and cannot be charmed, then there is no advantage in a charmer.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If a snake bites [a man, it is because] there has not been a charm [from the charmer to prevent it from doing so]. And there is no profit to the man of the tongue [(the charmer who did not use his tongue to prevent the biting). Likewise, there is no profit (but loss) to the sage, who could have used his tongue to teach the laws, so that they not be violated, but who failed to do so.]


###### Ecclesiastes 10:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:12)


דִּבְרֵ֥י פִי־חָכָ֖ם חֵ֑ן וְשִׂפְת֥וֹת כְּסִ֖יל תְּבַלְּעֶֽנּוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The words of a wise man win favor; but the lips of a fool devour him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The words of the sage [find] grace [in their hearers], but the lips of the fool, [(who incites men to evil)] swallow them.


###### Ecclesiastes 10:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:13)


תְּחִלַּ֥ת דִּבְרֵי־פִ֖יהוּ סִכְל֑וּת וְאַחֲרִ֣ית פִּ֔יהוּ הוֹלֵל֖וּת רָעָֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The beginning of his words is foolishness, and the end of his talk is evil madness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is grievous madness.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The beginning of the word of his [(the fool's)] mouth are folly; and the last of his mouth is evil waywardness.


###### Ecclesiastes 10:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:14)


וְהַסָּכָ֖ל יַרְבֶּ֣ה דְבָרִ֑ים לֹא־יֵדַ֤ע הָאָדָם֙ מַה־שֶּׁיִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר יִֽהְיֶה֙ מֵֽאַחֲרָ֔יו מִ֖י יַגִּ֥יד לֽוֹ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The fool multiplies words; man knows not what will be; and what will be after him, who can tell him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
A fool also multiplies words: yet no man can tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the fool multiplies words, [(saying: "Tomorrow, I shall do this and this.")] How can a man know what is to be if what is behind him [i.e., what is immediately past], he needs someone to apprise him of !


###### Ecclesiastes 10:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:15)


עֲמַ֥ל הַכְּסִילִ֖ים תְּיַגְּעֶ֑נּוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יָדַ֖ע לָלֶ֥כֶת אֶל־עִֽיר׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The labor of the fools exhausts them; for he does not know the way to the city.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The labour of fools wearies himself; for he does not know to get to the city.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The toil of the fools [i.e., the slothfulness of the forsakers of Torah, which brings upon them the "toil" of Gehinnom)] wearies them, in that they know not how to go to the city [of truth].


###### Ecclesiastes 10:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:16)


אִֽי־לָ֣ךְ אֶ֔רֶץ שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ נָ֑עַר וְשָׂרַ֖יִךְ בַּבֹּ֥קֶר יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Woe to you, O land, if your king is a [mere] lad and whose officers feast in the morning.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes dine in the morning!


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Woe unto you, O land, whose king is a child [i.e., a fool], and whose princes dine in the morning!


###### Ecclesiastes 10:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:17)


אַשְׁרֵ֣יךְ אֶ֔רֶץ שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ בֶּן־חוֹרִ֑ים וְשָׂרַ֙יִךְ֙ בָּעֵ֣ת יֹאכֵ֔לוּ בִּגְבוּרָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א בַשְּׁתִֽי׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Fortunate are you, land whose king is a free [noble] man; and your officers feast at the proper time—in strength and not in drunkenness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Happy art thou, O land, when thy king is a man of dignity, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Happy are you, O land, whose king is of noble bearing and whose princes dine in season, in [the] strength [of wisdom and understanding] and not in the drinking [of wine].


###### Ecclesiastes 10:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:18)


בַּעֲצַלְתַּ֖יִם יִמַּ֣ךְ הַמְּקָרֶ֑ה וּבְשִׁפְל֥וּת יָדַ֖יִם יִדְלֹ֥ף הַבָּֽיִת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Where there is slothfulness, the ceiling sags, and where there is idleness, the house leaks.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
By much slothfulness the beams collapse; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Through slothfulness [(in repairing small cracks)] the vaulting sags, and through negligence of the hands, the house leaks.


###### Ecclesiastes 10:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:19)


לִשְׂחוֹק֙ עֹשִׂ֣ים לֶ֔חֶם וְיַ֖יִן יְשַׂמַּ֣ח חַיִּ֑ים וְהַכֶּ֖סֶף יַעֲנֶ֥ה אֶת־הַכֹּֽל׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
A feast is made for laughter, and wine will gladden life; and money answers all things.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes life joyful: and money answers all things.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For joy [i.e., for festive occasions] feasts are made, and wine rejoices the living, and money answers all [needs — wherefore let one labor so that he have the means for these necessary luxuries.]


###### Ecclesiastes 10:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/10:20)


גַּ֣ם בְּמַדָּֽעֲךָ֗ מֶ֚לֶךְ אַל־תְּקַלֵּ֔ל וּבְחַדְרֵי֙ מִשְׁכָּ֣בְךָ֔ אַל־תְּקַלֵּ֖ל עָשִׁ֑יר כִּ֣י ע֤וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ יוֹלִ֣יךְ אֶת־הַקּ֔וֹל וּבַ֥עַל (הכנפים) [כְּנָפַ֖יִם] יַגֵּ֥יד דָּבָֽר׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Even in your thoughts do not curse the king, and in your bed-chamber do not curse the rich; for a bird of the skies may carry [your] voice, and that which has wings will reveal the matter.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Do not curse the king, no, not even in thy thought; and do not curse the rich even in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the sky shall carry the sound, and that which has wings shall tell the matter.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Even in your thoughts do not curse the King; and (even) in your bedchambers do not curse the wealthy. For the bird of Heaven [i.e., your soul, which will ultimately return to its source] will carry the voice, and the winged creature [the angel that accompanies you thither (viz. Psalms 91:11)] will speak the thing.



## Chapter 11

###### Ecclesiastes 11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:1)


שַׁלַּ֥ח לַחְמְךָ֖ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַמָּ֑יִם כִּֽי־בְרֹ֥ב הַיָּמִ֖ים תִּמְצָאֶֽנּוּ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Cast your bread upon the waters, for in the abundance of days, you will find it. [i.e., do good even to one you never expect to see again (e.g., Yithro vis-à-vis Moses, Exodus 3:20)].


###### Ecclesiastes 11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:2)


תֶּן־חֵ֥לֶק לְשִׁבְעָ֖ה וְגַ֣ם לִשְׁמוֹנָ֑ה כִּ֚י לֹ֣א תֵדַ֔ע מַה־יִּהְיֶ֥ה רָעָ֖ה עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Contribute to seven and even to eight; for you never know what calamity will come upon the earth.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Give a portion to seven, and even to eight; for thou knowst not what evil shall be upon the earth.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Give a portion [of your bread] to seven [needy ones] and also to eight [others]. For you do not know what evil will befall the earth [and you may need all of them, or the merit of the charity you gave them, to survive.]


###### Ecclesiastes 11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:3)


אִם־יִמָּלְא֨וּ הֶעָבִ֥ים גֶּ֙שֶׁם֙ עַל־הָאָ֣רֶץ יָרִ֔יקוּ וְאִם־יִפּ֥וֹל עֵ֛ץ בַּדָּר֖וֹם וְאִ֣ם בַּצָּפ֑וֹן מְק֛וֹם שֶׁיִּפּ֥וֹל הָעֵ֖ץ שָׁ֥ם יְהֽוּא׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
When the clouds are filled with rain they will empty themselves upon the earth; and if a tree falls in the south or in the north, in the place where the tree falls there it remains.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth: and if the tree falls towards the south, or towards the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it shall lie.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If the clouds be filled with rain, there [i.e., where they can be of most benefit] will they be emptied. [Likewise,] if a “tree” [(a sage and a tzaddik)] dwell in the south or in the north, in the place that the "tree" dwells, there shall it [i.e., the good deeds and virtues of the tzaddik] be [perpetuated, even after his death].


###### Ecclesiastes 11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:4)


שֹׁמֵ֥ר ר֖וּחַ לֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ע וְרֹאֶ֥ה בֶעָבִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִקְצֽוֹר׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
He who watches [waits] for the wind, will never sow; and he who looks to the clouds will never reap.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He who observes the wind shall not sow; and he who regards the clouds shall not reap.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
He who waits for the wind will not sow [(for it might not come at all)], and he who looks for the clouds [to clear] will not harvest [(for fear of rain)].


###### Ecclesiastes 11:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:5)


כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֙עַ֙ מַה־דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָר֔וּחַ כַּעֲצָמִ֖ים בְּבֶ֣טֶן הַמְּלֵאָ֑ה כָּ֗כָה לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙ אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה אֶת־הַכֹּֽל׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Just as you do not know the way of the wind, nor the nature of that which is hidden in the womb of her that is with child, so will you never know the working of God Who does all things.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
As thou knowst not what is the way of the wind, nor how the bones grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowst not the works of God who makes all.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Just as you do not know the way of the wind, as [you do not know] what is enclosed in the full womb, so you do not know the deed [i.e., the decree] of G-d [in respect to poverty and wealth], which does all, [(so do not shrink from fulfilling His mitzvoth for fear of being impoverished)].


###### Ecclesiastes 11:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:6)


בַּבֹּ֙קֶר֙ זְרַ֣ע אֶת־זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וְלָעֶ֖רֶב אַל־תַּנַּ֣ח יָדֶ֑ךָ כִּי֩ אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜עַ אֵ֣י זֶ֤ה יִכְשָׁר֙ הֲזֶ֣ה אוֹ־זֶ֔ה וְאִם־שְׁנֵיהֶ֥ם כְּאֶחָ֖ד טוֹבִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
[Therefore] in the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not remain idle; for you do not know which will prosper, whether this or that, or whether both are equally good.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening do not withhold thy hand: for thou knowst not which shall prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
In the morning, sow your seed [e.g., in your youth, learn Torah, etc.], and in the evening [i.e., in your old age], do not slacken your hand; for you do not know which will prosper, this or the other, or whether both alike shall be good.


###### Ecclesiastes 11:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/11:7)


וּמָת֖וֹק הָא֑וֹר וְט֥וֹב לַֽעֵינַ֖יִם לִרְא֥וֹת אֶת־הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And the light is sweet; and it is good [pleasant] for the eyes to behold the sun.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And sweet is the light [of Torah], and good for the eyes [of Torah scholars] to see the sun of Torah [in its full resplendence.]


###### Ecclesiastes 11:8

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**

for if a man live many years, let him rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

For they shall live in those [eternal days] more [than in the days of their life in this world]. All that comes [upon them in those days of the afterlife] will be punishment [(if they do not take heed in this world.)]

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, follow the ways of your heart and the sight of your eyes; but realize that for all these things, God will bring you to judgement.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thy heart, and in the sight of thy eyes: but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[(stated sarcastically:) Go ahead and] rejoice, young man, in your youth; and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and walk in the ways of your heart and in the sights of your eyes — but know that for all of these, G-d will bring you into judgment.


###### Ecclesiastes 11:10

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Therefore, banish anger from your heart and remove evil from your flesh; for childhood and youth are vanity.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Therefore remove vexation from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And remove [the] anger [of the L-rd] from your heart, and rid your flesh [i.e., your heart] of evil [i.e., of the evil inclination]; for childhood and youth are vanity.

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:2)


עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־תֶחְשַׁ֤ךְ הַשֶּׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ וְהָא֔וֹר וְהַיָּרֵ֖חַ וְהַכּוֹכָבִ֑ים וְשָׁ֥בוּ הֶעָבִ֖ים אַחַ֥ר הַגָּֽשֶׁם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Before the darkening of the sun, the light, the moon and the stars; and the clouds return after the rain.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
before the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain:


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
["Remember etc.",] before the sun [(the forehead, which glows in youth)] darkens [(with creases, as old age approaches)], and the light [(of the countenance, the nose, darkens)], and the moon the [(soul)], and the stars [(the cheeks)], and the [(light-obscuring)] clouds return after the rain [(of tears over the troubles that have passed over you)].


###### Ecclesiastes 12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:3)


בַּיּ֗וֹם שֶׁיָּזֻ֙עוּ֙ שֹׁמְרֵ֣י הַבַּ֔יִת וְהִֽתְעַוְּת֖וּ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הֶחָ֑יִל וּבָטְל֤וּ הַטֹּֽחֲנוֹת֙ כִּ֣י מִעֵ֔טוּ וְחָשְׁכ֥וּ הָרֹא֖וֹת בָּאֲרֻבּֽוֹת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**

in the day when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows are dimmed,


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
On the day that the keepers of the house [(the ribs)] tremble, and the men of war [(the legs)] are cramped, and the grinders [(the teeth)] cease, from fewness, and the seers in the windows [(the eyes)] darken.


###### Ecclesiastes 12:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:4)


וְסֻגְּר֤וּ דְלָתַ֙יִם֙ בַּשּׁ֔וּק בִּשְׁפַ֖ל ק֣וֹל הַֽטַּחֲנָ֑ה וְיָקוּם֙ לְק֣וֹל הַצִּפּ֔וֹר וְיִשַּׁ֖חוּ כׇּל־בְּנ֥וֹת הַשִּֽׁיר׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And the doors to the street will be shut, when the sound of the grinding is low; and when one will awaken at the sound of a bird, and muffled will be the daughters [sounds] of song.

and the doors are shut in the street, when the sound of the grinding is low, and one starts up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of music are brought low;


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the doors in the marketplace [(the organs of elimination)] be closed with the muffling of the sound of the mill [(the stomach)], and he [(the old man] arise [from sleep] at the sound of a bird, and all songsters be base [in his eyes].


###### Ecclesiastes 12:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:5)


גַּ֣ם מִגָּבֹ֤הַּ יִרָ֙אוּ֙ וְחַתְחַתִּ֣ים בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְיָנֵ֤אץ הַשָּׁקֵד֙ וְיִסְתַּבֵּ֣ל הֶֽחָגָ֔ב וְתָפֵ֖ר הָֽאֲבִיּוֹנָ֑ה כִּֽי־הֹלֵ֤ךְ הָאָדָם֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית עוֹלָמ֔וֹ וְסָבְב֥וּ בַשּׁ֖וּק הַסּוֹפְדִֽים׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Also, when they will fear heights, and terrors on the road, and the almond tree will blossom and the grasshopper will be a burden, and the desire will fail; for, [in this manner,] man goes to his eternal home, and the mourners go about the streets.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
when they are also afraid of that which is high, and terrors are in the way, and the almond tree blossoms, and the grasshopper drags itself along, and the caperberry fails; because the man goes to his eternal home, and the mourners go about the streets;

עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־[יֵרָתֵק֙] (ירחק) חֶ֣בֶל הַכֶּ֔סֶף וְתָר֖וּץ גֻּלַּ֣ת הַזָּהָ֑ב וְתִשָּׁ֤בֶר כַּד֙ עַל־הַמַּבּ֔וּעַ וְנָרֹ֥ץ הַגַּלְגַּ֖ל אֶל־הַבּֽוֹר׃

before the silver cord is loosed, or the golden bowl is shattered, or the pitcher is broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern;


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Ecclesiastes 12:7

וְיָשֹׁ֧ב הֶעָפָ֛ר עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ כְּשֶׁהָיָ֑ה וְהָר֣וּחַ תָּשׁ֔וּב אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְתָנָֽהּ׃

and the dust returns to the earth as it was: and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Vanity of vanities says Koheles, all is vanity.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Vanity of vanities, says Qohelet; all is vanity.

###### Ecclesiastes 12:9

וְיֹתֵ֕ר שֶׁהָיָ֥ה קֹהֶ֖לֶת חָכָ֑ם ע֗וֹד לִמַּד־דַּ֙עַת֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וְאִזֵּ֣ן וְחִקֵּ֔ר תִּקֵּ֖ן מְשָׁלִ֥ים הַרְבֵּֽה׃

###### Ecclesiastes 12:10

בִּקֵּ֣שׁ קֹהֶ֔לֶת לִמְצֹ֖א דִּבְרֵי־חֵ֑פֶץ וְכָת֥וּב יֹ֖שֶׁר דִּבְרֵ֥י אֱמֶֽת׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
Koheles sought to find words of delight; and to write in a proper way words of truth.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Qohelet sought to find out acceptable words: and words of truth written in proper form.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Koheleth sought to find [and found] things of desire [("laws to Moses on Sinai") and righteous writ [(the Written Torah and the Prophets)].


###### Ecclesiastes 12:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:11)


דִּבְרֵ֤י חֲכָמִים֙ כַּדָּ֣רְבֹנ֔וֹת וּֽכְמַשְׂמְר֥וֹת נְטוּעִ֖ים בַּעֲלֵ֣י אֲסֻפּ֑וֹת נִתְּנ֖וּ מֵרֹעֶ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
The words of the wise are like goads, like well fastened nails [are the words] of the masters of [learned] assemblies; all were given from one Shepherd.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The words of the wise are like spurs, and like nails well driven in are the sayings of the masters of collections; they are given by one shepherd.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The words of the sages [(who made fences for the Torah by enacting decrees to distance the Jews from actual transgressions)] are like goads [(Just as a goad guides the bullock in its furrows, so their words guide a man in the ways of life)]; and like nails, planted [(Just as nails are fixed, so the sages' words are fixed; and just as plants multiply, so their words "multiply" [i.e., they generate new learning.])] [nails] with "great heads," given by one shepherd [(Moses, by the mouth of G-d)].


###### Ecclesiastes 12:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:12)


וְיֹתֵ֥ר מֵהֵ֖מָּה בְּנִ֣י הִזָּהֵ֑ר עֲשׂ֨וֹת סְפָרִ֤ים הַרְבֵּה֙ אֵ֣ין קֵ֔ץ וְלַ֥הַג הַרְבֵּ֖ה יְגִעַ֥ת בָּשָֽׂר׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
And, furthermore, my son, be admonished; of making many books, there is no end, and much study wears away the flesh.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And more than they [("righteous writ” 12:10)], my son, take heed [to heed the words of the sages. And if you ask: If there is need of them, why were they not written down?] In the making of books there is no end [and if we began, we could never finish.]; and overmuch thought [i.e., attempts to digest more than we can understand] is a weariness of the flesh.


###### Ecclesiastes 12:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:13)


ס֥וֹף דָּבָ֖ר הַכֹּ֣ל נִשְׁמָ֑ע אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים יְרָא֙ וְאֶת־מִצְוֺתָ֣יו שְׁמ֔וֹר כִּי־זֶ֖ה כׇּל־הָאָדָֽם׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
In conclusion, after all has been heard; fear God, and preserve His commandments, for this is the whole [duty] of man.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The end of the matter, when all is said and done: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for that is the whole duty of man.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[(And if you ask: If I cannot complete the work, why should I begin it?)] the end of the matter, all having been heard — fear G-d [i.e., do whatever you can, with your heart to Heaven)], and keep His mitzvoth; for this is [the purpose of the creation of] all men.


###### Ecclesiastes 12:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ecclesiastes/r/12:14)


כִּ֚י אֶת־כׇּל־מַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים יָבִ֥א בְמִשְׁפָּ֖ט עַ֣ל כׇּל־נֶעְלָ֑ם אִם־ט֖וֹב וְאִם־רָֽע׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

# Esther

אסתר

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Esther](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Esther)

אסתר נעשית מלכת פרס ומסכלת מזימה להשמיד את היהודים, ולרגל נס ההצלה נקבע לדורות חג הפורים.

Esther becomes queen of Persia and foils a plot to destroy the Jews, establishing the Purim holiday.

## Chapter 1

###### Esther 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Esther/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Esther/r/1:1)


וַיְהִ֖י בִּימֵ֣י אֲחַשְׁוֵר֑וֹשׁ ה֣וּא אֲחַשְׁוֵר֗וֹשׁ הַמֹּלֵךְ֙ מֵהֹ֣דּוּ וְעַד־כּ֔וּשׁ שֶׁ֛בַע וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּמֵאָ֖ה מְדִינָֽה׃


**The Metsudah Five Megillot, Lakewood, N.J., 2001:**
It was in the days of Achashverosh—this was the Achashverosh who reigned from Hodu to Cush—one hundred and twenty-seven colonies.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

# Daniel

דניאל

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Daniel](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Daniel)

יועץ יהודי למלכי בבל הפותר חלומות ונמלט מסכנות בדרך נס.

A Jewish advisor to Babylonian kings interprets dreams and miraculously escapes danger.

youths in whom was no blemish, but well favoured, and skilful in all wisdom, and discerning in knowledge, and perceptive in understanding, and such as had ability in them to stand in the king’s palace, and whom they might teach the learning and the tongue of the Kasdim.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
boys without any blemish, and of goodly appearance, and acquainted with all wisdom, and possessing understanding and insight, and having the strength in them to attend [deferentially] in the palace of the king and to be taught the script and the speech of the Kasdim.

## Chapter 2

###### Daniel 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Daniel/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Daniel/r/2:1)


וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֗יִם לְמַלְכוּת֙ נְבֻֽכַדְנֶצַּ֔ר חָלַ֥ם נְבֻֽכַדְנֶצַּ֖ר חֲלֹמ֑וֹת וַתִּתְפָּ֣עֶם רוּח֔וֹ וּשְׁנָת֖וֹ נִהְיְתָ֥ה עָלָֽיו׃

And in the second year of the kingdom of Nevuchadnezzar [i.e., the second year after the destruction of the Temple], Nevuchadnezzar dreamed dreams and his spirit throbbed within him, [(both the dream and its meaning evading him)], and his sleep was broken upon him.


###### Daniel 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Daniel/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Daniel/r/2:2)


וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַ֠מֶּ֠לֶךְ לִקְרֹ֨א לַֽחַרְטֻמִּ֜ים וְלָֽאַשָּׁפִ֗ים וְלַֽמְכַשְּׁפִים֙ וְלַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים לְהַגִּ֥יד לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חֲלֹמֹתָ֑יו וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ וַיַּֽעַמְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Daniel/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Daniel/r/2:3)

###### Daniel 2:4

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

I make a decree that in every dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the G-d of Daniel; for He is the living G-d, and steadfast forever, and His kingdom is one which shall not be destroyed, and His dominion [shall endure] to the end [of time].

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Seventy sevens [i.e., 490 years] have been decreed upon your people and upon your holy city [(from the destruction of the first Temple in the days of Tzidkiyahu until the destruction of the second Temple — seventy years in the Babylonian exile and four hundred twenty in the second Temple —)], to consummate [purging of] the offense and to end and atone [their] transgressions [(in the exile of Titus and in subjugation)], in order to bring eternal righteousness and to consummate [the burdens of] vision and prophet, and to anoint the holy of holies [(the ark, the altars, and the holy vessels, which will be brought to them by the king, Messiah.)]

And know and understand from this word that has gone forth, to restore and to rebuild Jerusalem. **The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And after sixty two weeks shall an anointed one be cut off, and none will be left to him: and the people of a prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and his end shall be with a flood, and to the end of the war desolations are decreed.


**The Rashi Ketuvim by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

And his end [will be] to be swept away [(by the Messiah)], and until the end of the war [(of Gog and Magog, the city will be a trench of desolation)].

## Chapter 11

###### Daniel 11:1

[(With the fall of the kingdom of Bavel, when the kingdom of Madai and Paras petitioned on high to strengthen their yoke over you, I, Gabriel came to the assistance of Michael, your heavenly intercessor)].

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Daniel/r/11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Daniel/r/11:2)

And now, I will tell you the truth. Behold, three more kings will arise for Paras [(Koresh, Achashverosh, and the Darius who built the Temple)], and the fourth [(the latter Darius, fourth in the succession of Madai)], will accumulate great wealth, more than all [the others], and, growing strong in his wealth, he will rouse all [his kingdom to war] with the kingdom of Yavan (Greece).
